item.title: 2026 Fresh Graduate Job Hunt Guide for Taiwan: Resume Tips That Triple HR Callback Rates
item.description: Taiwan's 220,000 fresh graduates have just 6 seconds to grab HR attention. This guide covers the 3-second rule, 5 alternative experience types, the STAR method for cover letters, customization tactics, and optimal submission timing — a complete blueprint for landing interviews.
item.content:encoded:
The graduation season is about to begin in June 2026, and it is estimated that more than 220,000 fresh graduates will enter the job market in Taiwan. If you haven’t prepared a resume or submitted 30 submissions but no one responded, the problem is often not that you are not good enough, but that the resume did not grab HR’s attention in the first 3 seconds. From resume structure, autobiography writing to customization techniques, this article gives you a job search blueprint for "asking for an interview proactively." The information in this article is updated as of May 2026.

The 3-second rule for resumes: Will HR really read it carefully?

According to the Human Bank survey, the average time it takes HR to review a resume is 6 to 10 seconds, and 70-80% of resumes will be deleted in the first round. In other words, your resume only has 6-10 seconds to fight for the opportunity to "enter the second round."

Grasp 3 principles:

  • Focus on the first 1/3 of the page: title, job application, academic qualifications, and 1-2 most representative experiences, within the range that can be seen without scrolling.
  • Numbers are greater than adjectives: "Assisting in marketing activities" is very vague, "Assisting in organizing offline lectures for 200 people, and posts reaching over 50,000" is specific.
  • White space and font: Use 11-12pt font level, 1.5 line spacing, and 2cm left and right white space. Only when it looks breathable will you want to read it.

If you haven't made a formal resume yet, you can first use the resume generator to fill in the basic information and quickly produce a standard version. This saves you time on typesetting. Write the content first, and then slowly adjust the visuals.

5 alternative experiences that you can write about without internship experience

The most common anxiety among fresh graduates is "I don't have an internship", but HR actually looks at "what you have done that shows your ability", and it does not necessarily have to be an internship. You can write about the following 5 experiences:

  • Class Topic: Quantify results. For example, "Market Research Project: Interview 30 consumers, produce a 40-page report, and get the highest score in the class."
  • Society Cadres: Emphasis on leadership and cross-group communication. For example, "Served as the activity director of the department society, hosted 300 people to welcome new students, controlled the budget within 80,000, and achieved a satisfaction level of 4.6/5."
  • Work experience: You can also write in the service industry. For example, "2 years of experience in a beverage store, assisted in training 5 new employees, and increased monthly sales by 12%."
  • Self-study courses: Certificates from Coursera, Hahow, and Udemy count. The key point is "what you learned and which project you used it in", not just posting the certificate link.
  • Personal works: GitHub, Behance, IG, blogs, and podcasts can all be listed. Creative work especially requires personal works.

The key point is to "use specific numbers to illustrate the impact." If you really don’t have numbers to write down, write “execution details”: when, how many times it was done, how many people it was done with.

How to write an autobiography that doesn’t look like a running account: STAR Rule in practice

The STAR rule is the most practical structure when writing about experiences:

  • S (Situation): the background at the time and the problems faced
  • T (Task): The specific task you are assigned or take the initiative to undertake
  • A (Action): What did you do and how did you do it?
  • R (Result): What measurable impact is produced

Example (bad way of writing): "I serve as an activity leader in the department society, organized many activities, and learned a lot of communication skills."

Example (rewritten by STAR): "As a junior, I served as the long-term organizer of department society activities (S) and was responsible for hosting the orientation of 300 people (T). I prepared 2 months in advance, recruited a team of 15 people to divide the work, tracked the progress with Trello, and negotiated a 20% discount with 3 vendors (A). The final budget was controlled at 85% of the original, and the student satisfaction rate was 4.6/5, which is the highest in the past 3 years (R)."

The recommended word count for your autobiography is 500-800 words, divided into 3 paragraphs: the first paragraph directly writes the position you are applying for and the strongest proof of ability; the second paragraph writes 1-2 representative experiences using STAR; the third paragraph writes your specific understanding and expectations of this position and this company. Avoid starting with childhood memories like "I come from a warm family in Taichung." HR has no time to read.

What should be customized when applying for different positions?

Applying to 50 companies with the same resume is a big no-no. Spend 5-10 minutes doing these 3 things before submitting your resume each time:

  • Find out the keywords of the job vacancy: For example, if you are looking for "digital marketing specialist", "FB advertising", "GA", "copywriting" and "KPI" often appear in JD. These words should naturally appear in your resume and autobiography, because many companies will use ATS systems to do keyword screening first.
  • Modify resume title and first paragraph of autobiography: Change the title from "Personal Resume" to "Application for Digital Marketing Specialist of OO Company - Wang Xiaoming", and directly write "Why am I suitable for this position" in the first paragraph of the autobiography.
  • Reorder experience: Put experience related to the position you are applying for first, and shorten or delete irrelevant experience. For example, if you are applying for an engineer job, put your community experience in one line and put the topic and GitHub links at the top.

Use a Chinese typo checker to scan your resume and autobiography before sending it out. Typos are the most likely points to be deducted, especially typos in the job title and company name you are applying for, which is almost equal to being eliminated immediately.

4 common reasons for no response after submitting resume

I haven’t received any response after a month of submitting. Please check these 4 points first:

  • The match between academic experience and position is less than 60%: For example, if you apply for a "senior marketing specialist" that requires 1 year of experience, fresh graduates will be automatically rejected. Start with the positions open to fresh graduates such as "junior", "reserve cadre" and "assistant".
  • Resume format running, the file is too large: Word will run on different computers, save it as PDF and then submit. The file size should be controlled within 2MB. Files that are too large may be blocked by the mailbox.
  • Autobiography writes about family background rather than ability: "My parents taught me to be responsible since I was a child." HR really doesn't want to read this kind of sentence.
  • Contact hours are not suitable: If you cannot answer the phone number on your resume during class during the day, write down a time period that is convenient for contact, such as "You can answer the phone after 17:00 on weekdays."

Timing for active follow-up: If there is no response within 7-10 working days after submission, you can write a short inquiry letter, reiterate your interest and introduction, attach your resume and send it again. Don't make the letter too long, 3-5 sentences is enough.

FAQ

Do I need to include a photo on my resume?

Depends on the industry. Most traditional industries, service industries, and financial industries require photos, while those in the technology industry and foreign investors are optional. If you do, be sure to use ID photos taken within the past year (white background, front face, natural expression). Do not use travel photos or social media photos.

Do you need to write if your GPA is not good?

It’s okay not to write if it’s lower than 3.0, most companies won’t take the initiative to ask. However, if you are from a prestigious university or related department, and you are applying for a position that requires an academic background (such as research, consultant), it is recommended to write it down and strengthen other highlights.

Do you want to make a self-introduction video?

If the job vacancy does not require it, you will not get too many points if you do it, but it will take time. Unless you are applying for positions in marketing, new media, PR, etc. that require a statement, a 1-2 minute self-introduction video will be a bonus.

Which is the best day for delivery?

According to Labor Bank statistics, the highest proportion of HR personnel looking at resumes is between 9 and 11 a.m. on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. Mondays are usually spent dealing with matters accumulated over the weekend, and Fridays are spent preparing to take the holidays, which is less efficient.

5-minute checklist before submitting your resume: Is the title the correct position name, is the photo within 1 year, scan it for typos, the PDF format should be less than 2MB, and the email should not be a middle school nickname (it is recommended to use the format of "English name. Last name@gmail.com"). Starting today, revise your resume to the point where HR can take the initiative to make an appointment with you, and your job search will be much smoother.

item.title: 14 Days to Taiwan 2026 Tax Deadline: Extension Applications, Last-Week Tax-Saving Tips, and Refund Inquiry
item.description: Taiwan's 2026 income tax deadline is May 31, with only 14 days left. Missed it? Need to pay in installments? Wondering whether your refund arrives in July or October? This guide covers online filing steps, last-week tax-saving tips, the three-batch refund schedule, and amended-return tutorials — essential reading for Taiwan office workers.
item.content:encoded:
Taiwan's 2026 individual income tax filing season ends on May 31 — just 14 days away. Whether you haven't filed yet, want to amend a return you already submitted, or want to know exactly when your refund hits, this guide covers it. From online filing and extension applications to last-minute deductions and the July refund schedule, here's how to wrap up tax season without panic. Information current as of May 2026.

14 days left: what to do if you haven't filed yet

Taiwan's 2026 income tax filing season runs from May 1 to May 31. Miss the deadline and the National Taxation Bureau adds a 1% late surcharge per day on the tax payable, capped at 15%. Once you're 30 days overdue, the bureau assesses your tax directly and pursues collection — at that point, you've lost any room to push back.

If you haven't started, you have two paths now: file online, or apply for an extension. Online filing skips the card reader — you can log in with your NHI card and registration password, mobile-phone authentication, or the Ministry of Finance's eTax Mobile Service app. The recommended portal is the MOF's Individual Income Tax e-Filing and Tax Payment System, which auto-imports your withholding statements, insurance premiums, donations, and medical expenses. Most people finish in 15 minutes.

If you don't have a tax password yet, NHI card + registration password is the fastest route — you can register on your phone in minutes. Prefer a physical workflow? Convenience-store KIOSKs can print your income statement so you can review it at home. Use a date calculator to count down to May 31, and set an alarm for May 29 to avoid the last-day system crush.

Truly out of time: 3 steps to apply for installments online

If your trial calculation shows a large amount due and you can't pay it in one shot, you can apply for installment payments — up to 36 installments, with each installment no less than NT$3,000. The interest rate tracks the one-year postal savings deposit rate, roughly 1.6% in 2026 — far below revolving credit card interest.

Three steps to apply for installments:

  • Tick the installment box when filing online: In the e-filing system, when choosing your payment method, select "Apply for installment tax payment" and the system calculates each installment amount.
  • Choose the number of installments: Tax due under NT$20,000 splits into 2–3 installments; under NT$50,000 into up to 6; up to 36 installments maximum. More installments mean more total interest.
  • Pay after approval: The bureau typically approves within 2–4 weeks. Once approved, you receive a payment slip for each installment — pay on time via ATM or credit card. Miss one installment and you lose installment eligibility entirely.

Note that installments apply only to tax owed, not refunds — if you're getting money back, you don't need to apply. If your household has had a major event (job loss, serious illness), you can also apply for a payment deferral of up to one year by submitting supporting documents to your local National Taxation Bureau office.

Last-week tax-saving moves that still work

Many people forget you can take whichever is larger: the standard deduction or itemized deductions. For 2026, the standard deduction is NT$124,000 for singles and NT$248,000 for married couples filing jointly. If your documented expenses add up to more than that, itemizing pays off:

  • Medical expenses: Receipts for you, your spouse, and dependents (orthodontics, long-term care, childbirth, and health checkups all count). No cap when documented.
  • Insurance premiums: Personal life insurance, NHI and Labor Insurance, and National Pension contributions — capped at NT$24,000 per person per year.
  • Donations: Donations to education, culture, public welfare, and charity — capped at 20% of your total gross income. No cap on donations to the government.
  • Home mortgage interest (owner-occupied): Up to NT$300,000 per household.
  • Rental expense: If you or your spouse rent a place in Taiwan as your primary residence — capped at NT$120,000 per household.

One more reminder: the Special Preschool Deduction was expanded in 2024 to NT$150,000 per child under age 8, and NT$225,000 per child from the second child onward. Many first-time parents miss this one.

How to check your refund: the 2026 three-batch schedule

Taiwan's 2026 tax refunds land in three batches:

  • Batch 1: July 31 — for filers who completed their return before May 10 and chose direct deposit.
  • Batch 2: October 31 — for filers who filed after May 10, or who filed on paper.
  • Batch 3: January 20 the following year — for special cases involving supplemental documents or appeals.

To check status: go to the MOF Tax Portal, enter your ID number and date of birth, and look up your record. For the refund method, choose direct deposit to your own bank account — far easier than waiting for a paper check. If your refund hasn't arrived by early August, first verify that your registered address hasn't changed and your account number is correct, then call the National Taxation Bureau service line at 0800-000-321.

One critical warning: the National Taxation Bureau will never call you to operate an ATM for a tax refund. Any call asking you to transfer money or share your account password is a scam. Hang up and dial 165 (the anti-fraud hotline).

Filed incorrectly? How to amend your income tax return

What if you realize after filing that you under-reported income, missed a deduction, or applied the wrong tax rate? Two scenarios:

Caught before May 31: Just log back into the e-filing system and overwrite your original return — the system takes the last submission as final. If you filed on paper, you'll need to resubmit at your local National Taxation Bureau office.

Caught after May 31: You go through the amended return process. If you overpaid, fill out a refund application form and attach the recalculation — you can claim a refund up to 5 years later. If you underpaid, file the make-up payment as soon as possible. Voluntarily paying the shortfall usually triggers only interest; if the bureau catches it first, you face penalties.

Common amendments include: forgetting to claim dependents, omitting dividend income, exceeding the insurance premium cap, and forgetting to list medical receipts. Keep all your documents for at least 5 years after filing — the bureau has a 5-year review window.

FAQ

Will I owe a lot of tax on a monthly salary of NT$40,000?

For a single office worker earning NT$480,000 a year: after subtracting the personal exemption of NT$97,000, the standard deduction of NT$124,000, and the special deduction for salaries and wages of NT$218,000, the taxable income is roughly NT$41,000. That falls in the 5% bracket, so the tax is around NT$2,000. In most cases, the amount your employer already withheld exceeds this, so you'll see a refund of anywhere from a few thousand to over ten thousand NT dollars.

Is paying tax by credit card worth it?

Depends on the bank's offer. Most credit cards give 1.5%–3% cashback on tax payments, which usually still nets a profit after the processing fee. But note: most banks don't count credit card tax payments toward their "regular spending" threshold, so you won't earn miles or bonus points — just the straight cashback.

Will I get a notification when the refund hits?

Yes. After a direct-deposit refund posts, a notice is mailed to your registered address, and your bank app pushes a notification. Be careful, though: scammers have been sending text messages pretending to be the National Taxation Bureau and asking you to click a link. Only trust the official lookup page on the MOF Tax Portal.

How do I file if I left a job mid-year?

When you leave a job, the company issues a Withholding Statement for Various Incomes listing every salary payment from January 1 to your last day. If you switched jobs mid-year, the new company issues a separate statement — the e-filing system pulls both automatically when you file. Just cross-check the amounts against your original pay slips.

Start now: spend 15 minutes running a trial calculation in the MOF e-filing system to see whether you owe or are owed. If you owe a large amount, apply for installments today. If you're getting a refund, choose direct deposit to your regular account. With 14 days left, the earlier you file, the sooner your refund arrives — and the sooner this whole tax season is behind you.

item.title: Building a 6-Month Emergency Fund on a NT$40K Salary: A Practical Guide for Taiwan Office Workers
item.description: Average unemployment in Taiwan lasts 22 weeks, yet nearly 70% of office workers have no cash reserves. Using an NT$40K monthly salary example, this guide shows how to save NT$165,000 in 18 months — with a three-account flow strategy that keeps your emergency fund from being spent halfway.
item.content:encoded:
"If you suddenly lose your job tomorrow, how many months can your savings last?" This question is quite worrying for many office workers. According to statistics from Taiwan’s Ministry of Labor, the average unemployment cycle in 2025 will be 22.4 weeks (about 5.6 months), but less than 30% of office workers have a six-month emergency reserve fund. When something unexpected happens—losing a job, getting sick, or a family member needs money—people without a reserve have no choice but to swipe their credit cards or borrow money, and the debt snowball grows.

This article uses a standard office worker with a monthly salary of 40,000 yuan as an example to tell you how to start from scratch and save an emergency reserve of 165,000 yuan in 18 months. Information updated as of May 2026.

Why is 6 months of emergency reserve sufficient?

The most common saying on the Internet is "prepare 3-6 months of living expenses", but in fact 3 months is obviously not enough. There are three reasons:

  • It takes an average of 5-6 months to find a job: According to statistics from the Job Bank, it takes an average of 4-7 months for office workers in Taiwan to change jobs. A three-month reserve fund cannot cover the next salary at all.
  • Unexpected expenses are bigger than expected: medical expenses, car accident compensation, emergency needs for the elderly, these are not included in the monthly fixed expenses
  • Psychological stress will ruin your job search performance: The job search anxiety when you only have enough money left to last for 1 month can easily make you accept the first offer instead of the most suitable job.

If you are a case worker, contract worker, or work of a business nature, it is recommended to wait until 9-12 months, because the income fluctuates more. If you have a mortgage or have children at home, the starting time is at least 8 months.

Calculate your emergency fund target amount

The bigger the emergency reserve, the better. The calculation formula only looks at the "minimum living expenses", not the current consumption level. Divide your monthly expenses into three categories:

  • Necessary expenses: rent, water, electricity, gas and internet, food expenses (mainly self-catering), transportation expenses, insurance premiums
  • Semi-essential expenses: Cell phone bills, monthly gym fees, streaming subscriptions
  • Non-essential expenses: eating out, entertainment, shopping, travel

Emergency funds only count as Category 1 plus half of Category 2. Take a single office worker living in Taipei with a monthly salary of 40,000 as an example:

  • Rent 13,000 yuan, water, electricity and gas 1,500 yuan, internet 600 yuan
  • Food expenses (mainly self-cooked) 8,000 yuan, transportation expenses 1,500 yuan, insurance premium 2,000 yuan
  • Total necessary expenses are 26,600 yuan
  • Semi-necessary expenses 1,500 yuan (mobile phone 800, streaming 700)
  • Minimum monthly expenses are approximately NT$27,500, and 6-month reserve fund target is NT$165,000

For those who live at home or share a house, the amount may only be around 120,000; for those who have a mortgage or support a family, the amount will be increased. Figure out your own numbers first and your goals will make sense.

Actual distribution plan of monthly salary 40,000

The monthly salary is RMB 40,000, after deducting labor and health insurance, and the actual pension is approximately RMB 36,500. To save 165,000 yuan in 18 months, save an average of 9,200 yuan every month, which is equivalent to saving 25% of your salary. It sounds harsh, but it works in the right way:

  • Necessary expenses 26,600 yuan (73%)
  • Emergency fund savings of $9,200 (25%)
  • Entertainment flexibility NT$700 (2%)

But the "entertainment flexibility" of this plan is almost zero, which makes it unbearable. It is recommended to use the accelerated version of the "521 Rule": changing food expenses from eating out to cooking at home can save 4,000 yuan, deactivating idle subscriptions can save 600 yuan, and bringing a kettle to work can save 5,000 yuan a year. These small adjustments add up to an additional 1,500 yuan in flexibility every month, which can last until 18 months without breaking the bank.

Where should the emergency fund be kept so that it will not be spent?

Many people fail to save money not because they earn less, but because they put their money in the wrong place - they have a salary transfer account that they use every day, but it is spent when they swipe their cards. The principle of storing emergency reserves is "you can get it, but you can't get it smoothly":

  • Digital account high profit margin (recommended): Taishin Richart 1.5%, Wing Fung DAWHO 1.6%, Cathay Pacific KOKO 1.5%. There is a monthly limit limit (mostly within 300,000), but the liquidity is high and the interest rate is more than 5 times better than ordinary living savings.
  • Term Savings Deposit: The 1-year annual interest rate is about 1.7%, but the interest on early termination is 20% off. Suitable for parts that are sure not to be moved within a year
  • Absolutely don't invest in stocks, funds, or cryptocurrencies. These can fall by 30% at any time. You can just sell them at a loss when you need money urgently.

The recommended allocation is: 1 month of living expenses (27,500) can be put into a salary account for turnover, 2 months can be put into a digital account for immediate use, and the remaining 3 months can be put into a 1-year fixed deposit to earn interest.

Three Common Emergency Fund Myths

Myth 1: “I don’t need to save an emergency fund because I have a credit card limit.”

The annual interest rate of credit card revolving interest is 12-15%. If you borrow RMB 100,000, you will have to repay RMB 12,000 to RMB 15,000 in interest per year. It is equivalent to using the most expensive way to deal with emergencies, turning the problem from no money to money owed plus no money.

Myth 2: “I don’t need to save an emergency fund because I have insurance.”

Insurance claims usually take 2 weeks to 2 months, who will pay your rent during this time? Moreover, the insurance does not cover unemployment or family needs, and the coverage is limited.

Myth 3: “I can borrow it from my family”

Your family's money is a reserve fund for you, but it is also hard-earned money for them. Borrowing money can be emotionally damaging, so avoid it if you can. The essence of an emergency fund is the sense of security that "you can get through it without relying on anyone."

Advanced skills: Use three accounts to split management

After saving the first 165,000, it is recommended to upgrade to "three-account diversion management" so that the emergency reserve can be dynamically adjusted with changes in life:

  • Life-saving account (3 months): Put digital money into your account and only use it if you are really unemployed or hospitalized.
  • Opportunity Account (2 months): Place fixed deposits or Treasury bond ETFs, which can be used when there is a good investment opportunity
  • Buffer account (1 month): Transfer account after salary release, use it directly for temporary expenses of the month, and make up for it at the end of the month.

Do an inventory twice a year. It is recommended to use a date calculator to mark the review dates in January and July each year, confirm that the amount has kept up with the price, and re-confirm whether the proportion of the three accounts is reasonable.

FAQ

Q1: How should I save with a monthly salary of 30,000 yuan as a new employee?

Set a low threshold first, with a target of 3 months (about 90,000). Save 3,000 yuan per month and reach the target in 2 and a half years. Extend to 6 months after salary increase. The key point is to first have "the habit of saving money". Habit is more important than the amount.

Q2: If I have a loan, should I pay it off first or save an emergency fund first?

It is recommended to proceed "at the same time". Cards with interest rates higher than 6% will be repaid first; mortgage loans and student loans with interest rates lower than 4% can be repaid while saving an emergency fund, because you cannot rely on mortgage loans to meet your urgent needs when you are in urgent need.

Q3: Will emergency reserves be eaten up by inflation?

meeting. Therefore, it is recommended to open a digital account or short-term fixed deposit with an annual interest rate of more than 1.5%. The long-term portion that does not move for more than 18 months can be placed in low-risk commodities such as Chunghwa Telecom special stocks and government bond ETFs.

Q4: What situation is considered "really necessary"?

Three judgment criteria: unemployment or serious illness, unexpected expenses exceeding monthly salary, and major family accidents. Buying a new mobile phone, buying a bag, or giving out red envelopes during the Chinese New Year do not count. These should come from the monthly entertainment budget.

item.title: Taiwan 2026 Tax Refund Inquiry Guide: When Will It Arrive? What to Do If You Don't Receive It
item.description: The 2026 tax filing season just ended, and the first batch of refunds arrives as early as late July. This guide covers the three-batch refund schedule, inquiry channels, and remedies if you don't receive yours — plus how to turn the refund into the foundation of an emergency fund.
item.content:encoded:
Every May, what office workers look forward to most is the day their tax refund hits the bank. Taiwan's 2026 individual income tax filing season runs from May 1 to May 31. Based on the National Taxation Bureau's annual rhythm, the first batch of refunds starts on July 31. But here's the catch: depending on your refund method and how early you filed, the deposit date can vary by two or three months.

This guide covers the 2026 refund lookup process, the three-batch schedule, the recovery path if your refund doesn't arrive, and how to actually put the money to work once it lands. Information current as of May 2026.

2026 refund schedule cheat sheet

The National Taxation Bureau runs annual refunds in three batches, based on when you filed and how. Here's this year's schedule:

  • Batch 1 refund: July 31, 2026 — for filers who completed online returns between May 1 and May 10 and passed automatic verification.
  • Batch 2 refund: October 31, 2026 — for filers who filed between May 11 and May 31, or who missed the first batch.
  • Batch 3 refund: January 20, 2027 — for cases under manual review or with supplemental documents.

The earlier you file, the better your shot at Batch 1. If you missed the May 10 early-bird window, don't sweat it — as long as you file by May 31, you still land in Batch 2.

Three refund methods, very different timing

You pick the refund method when you file, and the timing and convenience differ a lot:

1. Direct deposit (recommended)

Your refund lands directly in the bank account you specified — no bank visits, no paper checks. About 95% of taxpayers choose this every year because it's the fastest and easiest. If the account number you entered is wrong or the account has been closed, the bureau falls back to another method, which usually pushes you to a later batch.

2. Voucher redemption

The bureau mails a refund voucher to your registered address; you take your ID to a designated bank to cash it in. If you're often away from your registered address and the voucher gets lost, you have to apply for a replacement — that step alone adds about a month.

3. Credit against next year's tax

You can hold this year's refund to offset next year's tax owed. This suits people who are certain they'll owe tax next year. Few people pick it in practice, because money parked at the bureau earns no interest.

How to track your refund: MOF lookup tutorial

Starting July 2026, you can check your refund status through three channels:

  • MOF Tax Portal (tax.nat.gov.tw): After logging in, click "Individual Income Tax Refund Lookup" and enter your ID number, date of birth, and filing year.
  • Regional National Taxation Bureau websites: Bureaus like the Taipei National Taxation Bureau and the Northern Region National Taxation Bureau have their own refund lookup pages.
  • Phone: Dial the toll-free hotline 0800-000-321 and follow the voice prompts.

The lookup shows three statuses: "Under approval" means your case is still being reviewed; "Transferred" means the bank has received the instruction and you'll typically see the deposit within 1–3 business days; "Returned" means further action is required.

Common reasons you didn't get your refund, and how to fix them

Every year, plenty of people still haven't seen their refund by August. There are four main culprits:

  • Wrong bank account number: One digit short, one digit too many, or a closed account. Fix: correct the account number on the MOF Tax Portal, or call the bureau for help.
  • Voucher returned due to wrong address: You chose voucher redemption but your registered address changed. Fix: bring your ID to the household registration office to update your address, then ask the bureau to reissue the voucher.
  • Outstanding taxes offset against the refund: Unpaid house tax, land value tax, or NHI premiums get deducted directly from your refund. Fix: pull the arrears detail from the MOF Tax Portal.
  • Filing flagged for manual review: For example, your itemized deduction amounts look unusual. Fix: wait patiently for Batch 3, or proactively submit supplemental documents to speed things along.

How to put your refund to work

Plenty of people blow their refund the moment it hits — celebratory dinner, new phone, new appliance. The average refund is NT$15,000 to NT$30,000 per person, and if you torch it in one swipe, you've essentially worked a year for nothing. A better split:

  • 50% into your emergency fund: Park it in a high-yield digital account like Taishin Richart or SinoPac DAWHO, paying around 1.5%–2% annually.
  • 30% invest in yourself: Sign up for a language course, take a certification exam, buy books — the highest-return investment you can make.
  • 20% enjoy life: Eat a good meal, buy that thing you've been eyeing, reward yourself for a year of work.

If you plan to put your refund toward overseas travel or a big purchase, use online tools to track live exchange rates and lock in the best buying window, then use a date calculator to map out departure and return days — that beats impulse-spending the whole pile.

Will under-reported income get caught? How to amend

If you realize you under-reported dividends, rental income, or side gigs last year, don't gamble. The National Taxation Bureau runs a "cash-flow reconciliation system" that cross-references bank deposits, withdrawals, and brokerage transaction records. Once they catch under-reporting, on top of paying the shortfall, you face a fine of up to 2× the tax owed plus late-payment surcharges.

The right move is to walk into the bureau yourself and file a voluntary amended return. If you self-report before the bureau opens an investigation, Article 48-1 of the Tax Collection Act exempts you from penalties — you only pay the back tax plus interest (currently around 1.5% per year). For NT$50,000 of evaded tax, a voluntary amendment might cost you only a few hundred NT dollars in interest. Getting caught and fined tens of thousands of NT dollars is a very different story.

FAQ

Q1: When's the earliest the 2026 refund can land?

Batch 1 is July 31, assuming you completed your online return before May 10 and chose direct deposit. If you filed at the end of May, you wait until October 31 for Batch 2.

Q2: Will the bank charge a fee on the refund?

No. The bureau's direct-deposit refunds are official government transfers, and no Taiwan bank charges a handling fee on them. The exact amount lands intact.

Q3: If I moved but didn't update my registered address, will my refund voucher go missing?

Yes. The bureau relies on household registration data, so verify your registered address before filing — or just choose direct deposit and skip the mailing problem entirely.

Q4: I forgot to file. Can I still do it?

Yes, you can still file after May 31, but you'll be charged a late-payment surcharge (1% for every 2 days overdue, capped at 15%) plus interest. If you're actually due a refund, filing late still gets you the money — it just bumps your refund to the first batch the following year.

item.title: 2026 Complete Unit Conversion Guide for Taiwan: Length, Weight, Volume, Area, and Temperature with Local Units
item.description: Taiwan uses metric daily, but US sizes, inches for screens, pings for real estate, and Taiwanese catties at the market all collide in everyday life. This 2026 guide covers length, weight, volume, area, and temperature with precise conversions—including Taiwan-specific units (1 catty = 600g, 1 ping = 3.30579 m², 1 jia = 0.9699 hectares)—plus cooking, travel, shopping, and home-buying quick references.
item.content:encoded:
Taiwan uses the metric system every day, but as soon as you step out of the wet market, step into the store, or enter the office of a real estate agent, five sets of units will appear in turn: when buying fruit, it is measured in kilograms, when buying beef, it is measured in grams, when buying computer screens, it is measured in inches, when buying shoes, it is measured in US Size, when buying a house, it is measured in square footage, when looking at farmland, it is measured in A, when looking at weather, it is measured in Celsius, and when looking at oven recipes, it is measured in Fahrenheit. This article integrates the five major categories of length, weight, capacity, area, and temperature, and lists the conversion relationships most frequently used in daily life at once. It also attaches 4 common situation quick checks and 5 FAQs, so that you can find the answers to unfamiliar units in the future.

1. Length units: How to interchange between metric and imperial systems?

Taiwan officially uses the metric system, but when buying international brand products, the imperial system (inch, foot, mile) will definitely come out. Remember the following five basic relationships, and you can handle 90% of daily situations.

  • 1 inch = 2.54 cm
  • 1 foot = 30.48 cm = 12 inches
  • 1 yard = 91.44 cm = 3 feet
  • 1 mile = 1.609 km
  • 1 meter ≈ 3.281 feet

Quick Facts for Buying Shoes: US shoe size US 9 ≈ 27 cm (men's shoes). In practice, the size charts of each brand are slightly different, so it is recommended to refer to the brand's official website. The European size EU is approximately equal to the centimeter plus 33 (adult men's shoes), such as EU 42 ≈ 27 cm foot length.

Quick Facts for Buying a Screen: The inches marked on TVs/monitors are "diagonal length", not width. Always remember three groups: 24 inches ≈ 61 cm, 27 inches ≈ 68 cm, and 55 inches ≈ 140 cm.

Height conversion: 170 cm ≈ 5 feet 7 inches (5'7"). Conversion formula: cm ÷ 30.48 = feet, remainder × 12 = inches.

Furniture and Space: Commonly found in American homes are 32-inch door width ≈ 81 cm; 8-foot ceiling height ≈ 244 cm; 24-inch walkway width ≈ 61 cm. When buying imported furniture, be careful about mixing up inches and centimeters when looking at size labels.

Quick check on suitcases: The size of a carry-on suitcase is usually 20 inches (≈ 51 cm), which corresponds to the carry-on baggage specification of "length + width + height ≤ 115 cm" of most airlines. 28 inches ≈ 71 centimeters is considered large checked baggage.

2. Weight unit: jin, kilogram, pound, ounce. Clarify at once

The weight unit is the easiest to mix up in Taiwan - the four sets of kilograms, kilograms, pounds, and ounces are mixed, and they are all different in wet markets, supermarkets, gyms, and cafes.

Taiwan’s Traditional 16 Two Systems (Taijin System)

  • 1 Taiwan pound = 600 grams = 16 taels
  • 1 Taiwan Liang = 37.5 Grams = 10 Qian
  • 1 Taiwan dollar = 3.75 grams

⚠️ The Taijin is Taiwan's unique 600-gram standard (16 Liang system), which originates from the "monme" weight system implemented during the Japanese rule (1895-1945): a Japanese pound is defined as 160 grams, 1 Mon = 3.75 grams, 160 × 3.75 = 600 grams, and the number of Taijin is fixed accordingly. The Chinese "market jin" is 500 grams (10 liang system), the standard established after the Weights and Measures Reform of the People's Republic of China in 1959. There is a difference of 100 grams from the Taiwanese jin - please pay special attention when buying Chinese products or looking at mainland recipes.

International Units

  • 1 kilogram (kg) = 1,000 grams = 2.205 pounds
  • 1 pound (lb) = 453.6 grams ≈ 0.454 kg
  • 1 ounce (oz) = 28.35 grams
  • 1 metric ton = 1,000 kg

Wet market quick check: "Boss, three kilograms of apples" = 1.8 kilograms. "Half pound" of pork = 300 grams (about the size of a steak).

Cooking American Recipe Quick Fact: 1 lb ground beef ≈ 454 grams; 1 oz cheese ≈ 28 grams (about a slice of cheddar cheese); 1 cup flour ≈ 120 grams (volume to weight will vary depending on the density of the material, flour, sugar, and butter are different).

Quick Gym Fact: Barbell plates are labeled 45 lb ≈ 20.4 kg; plates are labeled 25 lb ≈ 11.3 kg. It is common for heavy training equipment to have mixed standards for British and metric standards. When reporting squats, you must first confirm the units.

3. Capacity units: liters, gallons (American vs British), milliliters

There is an easily overlooked trap in the capacity unit - there is nearly 20% difference between U.S. gallons and British gallons, and confusion can lead to huge errors when reading recipes or refueling.

  • 1 liter (L) = 1,000 milliliters (ml) = 1,000 cubic centimeters (cc)
  • 1 US gal = 3.785 liters (exactly 3.785411784)
  • 1 UK / Imperial gal = 4.546 liters (exactly 4.54609)
  • 1 US cup = 240 ml
  • 1 US teaspoon (tsp) = 5 ml; 1 US tablespoon (tbsp) = 15 ml

⚠️ Source of the difference between the United States and British gallons: Both countries used Queen Anne's gallon (3.785 L) to measure wine in the early days. During the Weights and Measures Reform in 1824, the UK combined the three measurements of wine, beer, and grain into an "English gallon" of 4.546 L. The United States maintains the original Queen Anne's standard to this day. The gallon we see today in the UK, Canada, and Australia is mostly British 4.546 L, but in the United States it must be American 3.785 L.

U.S. gas station quick check: U.S. gas price is $4/gallon = approximately NT$33/US gallon = approximately NT$8.7/liter (subject to exchange rate changes). A must-check when calculating fuel budget when renting a car for travel.

Cooking American Recipe Quick Facts: 1 cup milk = 240 ml (not 250 ml); ½ cup = 120 ml; ¼ cup = 60 ml. Most measuring cups in Taiwan are marked in milliliters. When reading American recipes, it is best to convert to ml on the spot.

Water volume quick check: 1 liter of mineral water ≈ 33.8 US oz (fluid ounces, which are different from weight ounces), and the "20 oz water bottle" commonly found in American convenience stores ≈ 591 ml.

4. Area units: ping, square meter, A, hectare, acre

Area is the unit that is most likely to be misunderstood when viewing a house - it is confusing enough to mix square meters, square meters, and square centimeters. In addition, farmland refers to "A" and foreign maps refer to "acres." Newbies are often confused.

  • 1 ping = 3.30579 square meters (Ministry of Interior’s exact value = 36 ping = 36 × 30.3 cm × 30.3 cm)
  • 1 square meter = 0.3025 ping
  • 1 hectare (ha, ha) = 10,000 square meters = 3,025 ping
  • 1 A = 0.9699 hectares = 9,699 square meters = 2,934 pings (Taiwan’s traditional land measurement unit, commonly used in agricultural land sales)
  • 1 acre = 4,047 square meters ≈ 1,224 square feet

House Buying Quick Check: The "30 ping" apartment is ≈ 99 square meters, which is equivalent to a standard two-bedroom layout with three double beds + living room + kitchen and bathroom. "20 square meters" ≈ 66 square meters, mostly one-bedroom or two-bedroom apartments. "Main buildings + ancillary buildings + public facilities" must be distinguished - the actual usable space is the total square footage minus 30%-40% of the public facilities ratio.

Agricultural land quick check: 1 A land is approximately equal to 1 hectare, which is slightly smaller (3% difference). The older generation in Taiwan still buy farmland in units of "A". I saw that "3A" ≈ 2.91 hectares ≈ 8,800 square meters, which is a quite large piece of land.

Quick house rental check: The standard for a suite is "8 square meters" ≈ 26 square meters, which is equivalent to a space of about 5 meters × 5 meters, including bed, wardrobe, desk, and bathroom. "12 square meters" ≈ 40 square meters is a spacious suite or a small room.

Quick Facts on Rice Furniture Planning: 1 stack of tatami ≈ 0.5 ping ≈ 1.65 square meters. The "6-tatami" Japanese-style room is 3 tsubo.

5. Temperature units: Celsius, Fahrenheit, and Kelvin. Understand it at once

Taiwan’s weather forecast uses Celsius, but the other two appear in oven recipes, U.S. news, and scientific literature—shorthand formulas are more practical than rote memorization.

Three temperature scale conversion formulas

  • Celsius to Fahrenheit: °F = °C × 9/5 + 32 (can also be written °F = °C × 1.8 + 32)
  • Fahrenheit to Celsius: °C = (°F - 32) × 5/9
  • Kevin: K = °C + 273.15 (scientific standard unit of temperature, absolute zero = -273.15°C = 0 K)

Daily temperature comparison quick check

  • 0°C / 32°F: freezing point of water, freezing outdoors
  • 20°C / 68°F: Comfortable room temperature
  • 25°C / 77°F: Daytime in spring and autumn in Taiwan
  • 30°C / 86°F: Taiwan summer outdoor
  • 36.5°C / 97.7°F: normal human body temperature
  • 38°C / 100.4°F: borderline fever
  • 100°C / 212°F: boiling point of water

Cooking Quick Facts (Ovens are mostly marked in Fahrenheit)

  • 325°F ≈ 163°C: low temperature and slow baking (bottom layer of cakes and breads)
  • 350°F ≈ 177°C: Standard bake (preset for most recipes)
  • 400°F ≈ 204°C: medium-high heat baking (biscuits, roasted vegetables)
  • 450°F ≈ 232°C: High temperature baking (pizza, crispy dishes)

Tips for quick travel estimates

When traveling to the United States to check the weather forecast, there is a commonly used quick estimation method: Fahrenheit minus 30 and divided by 2 can give a rough estimate of the Celsius temperature. For example, 80°F → (80 − 30) / 2 = 25°C (exactly 26.7°C), not precise enough but good enough for deciding between short sleeves and a jacket. When you see 20°F during a cold snap, you quickly estimate (20 − 30) / 2 = -5°C, and you know to wear a down jacket.

6. FAQ: 5 of the most confusing questions in daily life

Q1: Is 1 pound in Taiwan the same as 1 pound in China?

no the same. In Taiwan, 1 Taiwan Jin = 600 grams (the 16-liang system used during the Japanese occupation), and in China, 1 Jin = 500 grams (reformed to the 10-liang system in 1959). I read a Chinese recipe that says "2 pounds of pork". If you buy it based on the Taiwanese pound, it will be 200 grams more.

Q2: What is the weight of "16 oz steak" when it is written on American restaurant menus?

Approximately 454 grams (1 oz = 28.35 grams, 16 oz = 1 lb). 16 oz steak is a large portion for Asian stomachs, it is recommended to share between two people or choose 8 oz / 12 oz.

Q3: How big is the house advertisement that says "30 ping" actually?

The total area of ​​the property is 30 square meters ≈ 99 square meters, but the actual usable area depends on the "public utility ratio". The proportion of public facilities in newly-built houses is usually 30-40%. After deducting 35% of public facilities from 30 square meters, the actual indoor area is about 19.5 square meters ≈ 64 square meters, which is equivalent to the standard layout of two bedrooms and one living room.

Q4: What is the Celsius setting for an American recipe oven "350°F"?

Approximately 177°C (176.67°C to be exact). Oven knobs are usually set in 5°C increments, with either 175°C or 180°C being acceptable. Likewise 400°F ≈ 200°C (204°C to be exact).

Q5: Is a treadmill marked 5 mph considered fast?

About 8 km/h (1 mph = 1.609 km/h), equivalent to jogging pace, about 7 minutes and 30 seconds/km. 10 mph ≈ 16 km/h, which is the speed of fast running (the first part of a marathon).

Conclusion: Leave accurate conversions to tools, and leave common sense memory to cheat sheets.

It is enough to memorize the cheat sheet for daily conversions, but when you need precise values ​​for purchasing materials for decoration, giving cooking classes, or calculating recipe proportions, it is recommended to use tools directly. The Unit Conversion Tool on this site covers all units in the five major categories of this article. Enter the value and the corresponding value will be displayed immediately to avoid manual calculation errors. It is recommended to use the square meter calculator for area conversion.

For scenarios that require a quick temperature check, use this site Typhoon Fake Query. When viewing weather warnings, you will also see a comparison between Celsius and Fahrenheit. When traveling abroad, it is recommended to write down the Celsius range corresponding to the local weather in advance, and use the table in this article to quickly determine the thickness of clothing.

item.title: 2026 Taiwan Summer Electricity Rates Start June 1: Correct Bracket Tiers + NT$12,000 Subsidy + 7 Saving Tips
