item.content:encoded:
**The information in this article was updated as of May 2026. ** Taipower's "Summer Month Electricity Price" is implemented from June 1 to September 30 every year, which is much more expensive than during non-summer months. For working families, just by turning on the air conditioner, the electricity bill in June may be 1.5 times higher than in May. This article compiles the latest electricity price range in 2026, practical power-saving tips, and energy-saving subsidies of up to 12,000 yuan to help you prepare before the summer months come.

2026 Summer Electricity Price Range Correct Version

Many old articles have electricity price figures that are out of date. The latest Taipower residential electricity price in 2026 (progressive system of electricity consumption):

Electricity consumption Summer months (6/1-9/30) Non-summer months (other times) Grade gap
1-120 degrees 1.68 1.68 0
121-330 degrees 2.45 2.16 +13%
331-700 degrees 3.70 3.03 +22%
701-1000 degrees 5.04 4.14 +22%
1001-1500 degrees 6.24 5.07 +23%
Above 1501 degrees 8.46 6.63 +28%

Key points of the progressive system: It is not "the highest unit price for all electricity consumption", but "tiered billing". For example, if you use 500 degrees, the first 120 degrees will cost 1.68 yuan, 121-330 degrees will cost 2.45 yuan, and 331-500 degrees will cost 3.70 yuan.

500 Degree Family Summer Month vs Non-Summer Month Actual Trial Calculation

Assume your monthly electricity consumption is 500 kWh:

Electricity bill for non-summer months:

  • 1-120 degrees: 120 × 1.68 = 201.6 yuan
  • 121-330 degrees: 210 × 2.16 = 453.6 yuan
  • 331-500 degrees: 170 × 3.03 = 515.1 yuan
  • Total about 1,170 yuan

Summer Month Electricity Bill:

  • 1-120 degrees: 120 × 1.68 = 201.6 yuan
  • 121-330 degrees: 210 × 2.45 = 514.5 yuan
  • 331-500 degrees: 170 × 3.70 = 629 yuan
  • Total approximately 1,345 yuan

Summer months cost $175 more than non-summer months (+15%). If the electricity consumption reaches 700 degrees, the summer month will cost 400-500 yuan more than the non-summer month; the difference will be even greater when the electricity is above 1000 degrees. Save more than 331 kilowatt hours of electricity, the highest benefit.

Tip 1: Air conditioner setting 26-28 degrees + electric fan assist

For every 1 degree increase in air conditioning, you can save approximately 6% on electricity bills (data from the Energy Administration of the Ministry of Economic Affairs). The best setting is 26-28 degrees for the electric fan. The body temperature is almost the same as setting it to 24 degrees, but the monthly electricity bill can be saved by 200-400 yuan.

Key points for saving energy in air conditioners:

  • Clean the filter regularly (dirty filter consumes 10-15% more power)
  • Close doors and windows, and draw curtains to block sunlight (Walls exposed to the west should be protected even more)
  • Use "Auto" mode to save power than "Strong Cooling"
  • Don’t switch the variable frequency air conditioner on and off frequently, it will save more money if it runs continuously for 4-6 hours.
  • Air conditioner installation location avoid west-facing walls and the outdoor unit should be well ventilated
  • Electric Fan Assist: Creates air convection, reducing body temperature by 2-3 degrees

Tip 2: Find out the hidden power consumption of standby appliances

Standby power (commonly known as vampire power) accounts for about 5-10% of household electricity consumption. The most common hidden power consumers:

-Set-top box, Wi-Fi router (24 hours on)

  • Chargers and transformers that are still plugged in when not at home
  • Microwave and oven with clock display
  • Standby lights for TVs, stereos, and computer screens
  • Water dispenser, smart speaker
  • Printers and scanners (the standby power consumption is higher than expected)

Implementation Suggestion: Buy an "extension cord with switch" (200-500 yuan per set), and cut off unnecessary electrical appliances at once after get off work or when going out. According to actual measurements, an ordinary family can save 100-200 yuan on electricity bills a month, which is more than enough to pay back the cost in one year.

Step 3: Apply for "Residential Time Electricity Price" Assessment

If your household’s electricity consumption pattern is “no one goes to work during the day and only uses it when going home at night”, you can apply for Taipower’s “Residential Time Electricity Price.” Off-peak hours (10:30 pm to 7:30 the next day) The electricity price drops to as low as about 1.96 yuan per kilowatt hour. Washing, drying, cooking, and charging electric vehicles are all arranged during this time, and monthly savings start from 300 yuan.

⚠️ Trial Calculation is Important: First use the Taipower App's "Electricity Bill Trial Calculation" tool to evaluate the electricity consumption pattern in the past 6 months to avoid expensive replacement. Some large electricity consumers in Shuangbei are suitable to maintain the original plan after trial calculations.

No. 4: Seize the 2026 energy-saving subsidy + goods tax refund (up to 12,000 yuan)

In 2026, the Ministry of Economic Affairs' "replacement of old residential appliances with new ones" + the Ministry of Finance's "excise tax reduction" dual subsidies will be launched simultaneously. The following is the combined amount:

Up to NT$5,000 for a single air conditioner

  • Energy-saving subsidy: 3,000 yuan per level 1 energy-efficient air conditioner (Ministry of Economic Affairs save3000.moeaea.gov.tw)
  • Goods tax refund: further refund 2,000 yuan (Ministry of Finance)
  • Total maximum of NT$5,000

Up to RMB 12,000 for a complete set of home appliances

Buy 4 major appliances including air conditioners, refrigerators, water heaters, and dehumidifiers, and apply for subsidies + tax rebates for each, total up to 12,000 yuan:

Home Appliances Energy Saving Subsidy Excise Tax Refund Subtotal
Air conditioning 3,000 2,000 5,000
Refrigerator 3,000 2,000 5,000
Water heater 1,000 — 1,000
Dehumidifier 1,000 — 1,000
Total 12,000

Application conditions

  • Purchase electrical appliances with Level 1 energy efficiency labels (including Level 1 air conditioners and refrigerators)
  • Completed the recycling of old machines (obtained the waste machine recycling form from the Ministry of Environment)
  • The electricity address and phone number comply with "residential, non-commercial use"
  • Invoice period: Purchase from the beginning of 2023 to 2026/12/31
  • Application deadline: **Complete online application before 2027/1/31

If the air conditioner at home has been used for more than 8 years, the old unit consumes 30-40% more electricity than the new unit. After replacement, the electricity bill will be paid back in ** one year**. Each county and city has additional subsidies (for example, Taipei City provides an additional NT$1,000-2,000), which can be found on the official website of the "Ministry of Economic Affairs' Energy-Saving Home Appliances Subsidy."

Tip 5: Use accounting to track monthly electricity bills

Without accounting, there is no way to review results. suggestion:

  1. Monthly meter reading (based on bimonthly bills), write down the kWh, and use a spreadsheet to track the "monthly electricity consumption" and "unit price per kWh"
  2. Taipower App Smart Meter allows you to view the hourly power consumption curve and find out which hours are the peak power consumption
  3. Compare to the same month last year: See how much progress you have made compared to the same month last year

If you need to quickly calculate electricity bill conversion or units, you can use the Unit Conversion Tool to handle the conversion of degrees, watts, and kilowatt hours. If you want to know how many days until today the next meter reading is, you can use the Date Calculator and the Countdown Timer to remind yourself to check the meter every two months.

Tip 6: Change LED bulbs + smart sockets

Many homes still use traditional light bulbs or T8 fluorescent tubes. Change to LED:

  • An 8W LED replaces a 60W tungsten bulb, reducing power consumption by 86%
  • An 18W LED tube replaces a 40W T8 fluorescent tube, reducing power consumption by 55%
  • The average lifespan is 5-10 times longer, and the frequency of lamp replacement is reduced
  • One LED costs 100-300 yuan, and the money will be paid back within half a year.

Smart Socket (200-500 yuan each) allows you to use a mobile app to control the switch of electrical appliances. If you forget to turn off the air conditioner when you go out, you can turn it off remotely.

Tip 7: Do laundry and dishwashing during concentrated periods

Many people don’t know that washing machines + dryers are the invisible killers of summer electricity bills:

  • Laundry Concentration: Wash twice a week, fully loaded each time, saving 50% of electricity compared to washing 1 piece of clothing every day
  • Cold water washing: 90% of the clothes are washed in cold water. The heating power consumption of hot water washing accounts for 80% of the total power consumption of the washing machine.
  • Hanging clothes instead of drying them: In summer, it can be dried in 2-3 hours on a sunny day, which can save about 5-10 kilowatt-hours of electricity each time in the dryer.

Smart meter + time electricity price: full explanation of applicable conditions in 2026

Time-based electricity prices (using different unit prices during the day/night) can save electricity bills, but the prerequisite is that your home must first have a "smart meter". Taipower's construction progress is: A total of 6 million households will be completed in 2030 (119), and 100% will be fully deployed in 2035 (124). As of the end of 2025, 76,000 residential households and 137,000 small shops in Taiwan have adopted time-based electricity prices, totaling 213,000 households.

Currently, you cannot actively apply for smart meters. Taipower will actively install them in only two situations: ① Apply for the "time-based electricity price plan" ② Your home has "renewable energy connected to the grid" (such as your own rooftop solar energy). General users have to wait for the comprehensive replacement schedule from 2030 to 2035.

Is time-based electricity price suitable for you? Simple assessment:

  • Household electricity consumption More than 700 kilowatt hours per month + High proportion of electricity consumption at night → Applicable, potential annual savings of 1,000-3,000 yuan
  • Business electricity consumption More than 1,100 kWh per month → Applicable
  • Low power consumption / peak usage during the day → Not recommended, it may be more expensive

Application channels: ① Over the counter at Taipower Service Center ② Apply online on Taipower website. It is recommended to use the Taipower App to try out the last 6 months of bills before making a decision because it can only be changed once in a year.

4 things you can do before the end of May

Summer electricity prices start on 6/1, it’s not too late to start preparing now:

  1. Air conditioner inventory: Arrange the replacement schedule for the air conditioners in your home that are over 8 years old, and apply for subsidies accordingly
  2. Master switch extension cord: Connect all unnecessary standby appliances to the switch extension cord
  3. Time electricity price trial calculation: Download Taipower App and log in to check the time electricity price trial calculation result.
  4. Energy-saving subsidy delivery: Purchase + delivery 6 months ago to avoid running out of quota (2026 subsidy quota is limited)

After doing these four things, you can save 1,000-3,000 yuan from June to September alone.

FAQ

Q1: When will the summer electricity price end? A: It ends on September 30th every year, and the non-summer electricity prices will resume on October 1st. However, the bill will be calculated across months, and the bill received at the end of October may still include the summer electricity price.

**Q2: Is it more economical to turn the air conditioner on all day or switch it in and out? ** A: If variable frequency air conditioner operates continuously for 4-6 hours, it is more economical to turn it on "continuously on"; fixed frequency air conditioner is not recommended to be turned off when going out for a short time (within 30 minutes). You should turn it off when you are out for a long time (more than 2 hours), otherwise it will be a waste of electricity.

Q3: Does it cost money to apply for electricity price during the time? A: It is free to apply, but it can only be changed once within 1 year. It is also free to change back to the original plan, but you need to wait for the cooling-off period. It is recommended to use the Taipower App to test for 6 months before making a decision.

Q4: Will the price increase for large electricity consumers? A: For residential electricity consumption exceeding 700 kilowatt hours in a single month, the price is 5.04 yuan per kilowatt hour in summer months and 4.14 yuan per kilowatt hour in non-summer months. If it exceeds 1000 degrees, it will be more expensive (from 6.24 yuan in Xia Yue). Controlling the temperature within 700 degrees can avoid the highest level. Households with multiple people may consider applying for electric meters per household.

Q5: How to apply for the energy saving subsidy of 3,000 yuan? A: ① Purchase level 1 energy-efficiency appliances and keep the invoices ② Complete the recycling of old appliances (obtain the waste recycling slip) ③ Submit online to save3000.moeaea.gov.tw + upload ID card, passbook, and electricity bill receipt ④ Wait for the approved subsidy to be credited to your account (about 2-4 weeks).

item.title: 2026 Taiwan Labor Day: First Year of Nationwide Holiday — Overtime Pay 2× Wages, Comp Time, and Complaint Channels
item.description: 2026 marks the first year May 1 Labor Day becomes a nationwide holiday in Taiwan after the 2025-05-28 amendment. This guide covers eligibility, the 2× wages formula, real calculations, 1:1 comp-time rules, and complaint channels.
item.content:encoded:
Labor Day, May 1, is quickly approaching again. 2026 is a historic year: After the amendment of the "Regulations on the Implementation of Memorial Days and Holidays" on 2025-05-28, May 1st Labor Day** was included in the national national holiday** for the first time, and all civil servants, faculty and students were given a day off (in the past, only laborers were given a day off). This article summarizes the applicable objects of Labor Day, the 2 times wage formula for overtime pay, the actual trial calculation of a monthly salary of 30,000 to 60,000, the 1:1 provision for compensatory time off, as well as the appeal channels and penalties when the employer violates the law. The information in this article is updated as of April 2026.

2026 New Labor Day System: From "Labor Exclusive" to "National Uniform"

Law revision background

In the past many years, only “workers” protected by Article 37 of the Labor Standards Act could have a holiday on May 1st. Students, teachers, civil servants and other non-worker people still have to go to work on May 1st - creating a strange phenomenon of "parents have a holiday but their children have to go to school" and "the husband has a holiday but his wife is a civil servant and has to go to work".

On May 28, 2025, the Legislative Yuan passed the "Regulations on the Implementation of Memorial Days and Holidays", adding 5 new national holidays: New Year's Eve / 5/1 Labor Day / 9/28 Confucius's Birthday / 10/25 Taiwan Liberation Day / 12/25 Constitution Anniversary. The new law will take full effect from 2026.

Applicable objects for Labor Day on May 1, 2026

  • National holiday: labor, civil servants, faculty and students (unified for the first time nationwide)
  • Special Transfer: Police, fire fighters, coast guard, and military personnel may be transferred to other days for compensatory leave due to "year-round shift duty", and may not necessarily take the rest on 5/1
  • Financial Market: Domestic bank employees are on holiday, but financial markets are still open (US and Taiwan stock exchanges have their own closing rules)
  • Garbage Truck: According to the announcement of each county and city environmental protection bureau, usually no collection on 5/1

May 1, 2026 is Friday, which together with Saturday (5/2) and Sunday (5/3) form a 3-day holiday (the first time there are 3 days of holidays nationwide).

How to calculate overtime pay for Labor Day attendance? Breakdown of 2 times salary formula

Article 39 of the Labor Standards Law stipulates that if the employer works on a holiday with the employee's consent, ** wages shall be doubled to **. This "double" means "in addition to the original day's salary, plus one day's salary", so you actually get 2 times the daily salary.

Calculation formula

  • Monthly Salary System: Daily Salary = Monthly Salary ÷ 30
  • Labor Day attendance fee = monthly salary ÷ 30 × 1 (originally included in monthly salary) + monthly salary ÷ 30 × 1 (additional)
  • Actual extra amount received = Monthly salary ÷ 30

Note: If the work exceeds 8 hours, the excess will be added to 1.34 times or 1.67 times of the extended working hours on weekdays, not 2 times for the whole day.

Actual calculation of monthly salary of RMB 30,000 to RMB 60,000: How much less did you receive?

Suppose you work 8 hours on Labor Day and your boss only gives you a normal day’s salary:

Monthly salary Daily salary Should be paid Underpaid amount
30,000 1,000 1,000 1,000
40,000 1,333 1,333 1,333
50,000 1,667 1,667 1,667
60,000 2,000 2,000 2,000

Extended calculation for overtime work exceeding 8 hours

If overtime work reaches 10 hours on the same day, extended working hours overtime pay will be added to the additional 2 hours. Take monthly salary 40,000 as an example:

  • Hourly wage is about 167 yuan (40,000 ÷ 30 ÷ 8)
  • First 8 hours: additional payment of RMB 1,333 (the "additional part" of 2 times salary)
  • Delay bonus in the 9th to 10th hour 1.34 times = 167 × 1.34 × 2 = About 447 yuan
  • Total should be extra = 1,333 + 447 = About 1,780 yuan

If you work overtime to 12 hours (the portion over 10 hours will be 1.67 times):

  • Hours 9-10: 1.34 × 2 hours = 447 yuan
  • Hour 11-12: 1.67 × 2 hours = 558 yuan
  • Total should be extra = 1,333 + 447 + 558 = About 2,338 yuan

⚠️ Exceeding 12 hours is prohibited: The maximum working hours in a single day is 12 hours (including normal working hours), and it is illegal for the employer to force overtime.

Can the boss require compensatory time off without overtime pay?

No, this is a common misunderstanding. According to Article 32-1 of the Labor Standards Act:

  • Compensatory leave must be chosen by the worker himself. Employers are not allowed to force compensatory leave to replace overtime pay.
  • Process: The employer first pays double wages in accordance with the law → If the employee wishes to take compensatory leave afterwards, both parties can negotiate
  • The standard of compensatory leave is "1 to 1", not "1 to 2" (that is, after working 8 hours, you will make up 8 hours, not 16 hours)
  • Compensatory leave should be made up within the agreed period. If it is not made up, it will still be converted into salary and paid.

A common dispute in practice is when the boss says, "Our company always provides compensatory time off," which is a violation of the Labor Standards Act. Workers have the right to ask for additional cash payments, and if they are faced with difficulties, they can appeal afterwards.

Regulations on making up work during the May Day holiday are inconsistent with asking for leave

May 1, 2026 is a Friday, there is no problem of making up shifts (the make-up shift system will be canceled from the second half of 2025). However, some companies will "voluntarily" require working on Saturdays. This situation is a "transfer" holiday in the labor agreement and must comply with:

  • Agree with the trade union or labor-management meeting
  • Prior announcement
  • After transfer, you must still comply with the 7-day holiday period (at least 1 day of regular leave within 7 days)

If you want to take a special day off on Thursday (4/30) and take five consecutive days off to go abroad, I would like to remind you to pay attention to the following points:

  • Special leave must be applied for in advance. Employers can only negotiate with you based on business operation needs and cannot refuse without reason.
  • If the leave period falls on Labor Day, 5/1 will not be counted as special leave and will not be deducted as special leave
  • When preparing for a travel trip, you can use the countdown timer to confirm how many days are left during the vacation and arrange air tickets and accommodation.

What should I do if my employer violates the law and refuses to pay overtime? 4-stage appeal process

If your boss refuses to pay overtime for Labor Day, you can take the following actions:

Phase 1: Preserve evidence (execute immediately)

  • Payslip (shows no additional payment)
  • Attendance records (punch records, sign-in sheets)
  • LINE/Email conversation (the boss said "just make up for the time off" and "the company doesn't have double time")
  • Screenshots of check-in and attendance management system

Phase 2: Internal Negotiation (Least Cost)

  • Write a letter or ask the company in person to reissue it in accordance with the law
  • Quoting Article 39 of the Labor Standards Act
  • Give the company 1-2 weeks to respond

Stage 3: Appeal channel (free)

  • Labor Bureau Report: Submit a report to the Labor Bureau where the company is located (County and Municipal Government Labor Bureau)
  • National toll-free number 1955 Labor consultation and complaint hotline (The identity of the whistleblower is kept confidential in accordance with the law)
  • Online Complaint: e-system of the Institute of Labor and Occupational Safety and Health of the Ministry of Labor

Stage 4: Mediation or Litigation

  • Labor dispute mediation: Apply to the local labor bureau (free, usually processed within 30-45 days)
  • Mediation fails → Labor Court Litigation (You can apply for a free lawyer from the Legal Aid Foundation)

Employer Penalties

Employers who violate Article 39 of the Labor Standards Law may be fined 20,000 to 1 million, and the name of the public institution and the name of the person in charge shall be published. The identity of the whistleblower is kept confidential in accordance with the law, and will not be fired in retaliation (if fired in retaliation, it is considered "unfair dismissal" and can be appealed again).

Cross-border 5/1 Comparison: Different positioning of the United States, Japan and South Korea

5/1 has different historical context and positioning in various countries around the world, and it is not a national holiday everywhere. Taiwan's transformation from "labor exclusive" to "national unity" in 2026 is actually a new milestone in line with the spirit of "International Labor Day".

United States: 5/1 is not Labor Day

Many people think that "May Day" is internationally unified, but Labor Day in the United States is the first Monday in September (legislated in 1894) - the date was deliberately moved away from May 1 in order to avoid commemorating the 1886 Chicago Haymarket Riots (this event is the historical origin of International Labor Day on May 1). Instead, 5/1 in the United States is designated as Loyalty Day, which is legal but not a public holiday. Most people will not pay special attention to it.

Japan: 5/1 is part of Golden Week

May 1st in Japan is not a national holiday, but because it is sandwiched between Showa Day on 4/29 + Constitution Memorial Day on 5/3 + Green Day on 5/4 + Children’s Day on 5/5, most companies will regard this day as a special holiday, allowing employees to enjoy the "Golden Week" for 7-9 consecutive days. Japanese workers mostly spend this day to travel abroad/domestic** rather than for trade union gatherings - this is a different atmosphere from the Labor Day in Europe and Taiwan.

South Korea: March 2026 has just been upgraded to a public holiday

Since 1958, Korea’s Labor Day (근로자의 날) has been a special position of “private sector paid leave + civil servants working”. Until March 2026, the South Korean Congress passed an amendment to raise 5/1 to a national holiday, and all civil servants, teachers, and students will have a holiday. This change is close to the timetable of Taiwan’s 2025-05-28 law amendment, reflecting the common trend of East Asian countries in recent years to “universalize” Labor Day.

Comparison conclusion

Country 5/1 Positioning National holiday? Main features
Taiwan National Holidays (from 2025-05-28) ✅ Yes (for the first time from 2026) For the first time, there will be 3 days in the country
South Korea Public holidays (from 2026-03) ✅ Yes (from 2026) Upgraded in the same year as Taiwan
Japan Golden Week (non-national) ⚠️ Most companies are closed 7-9 consecutive days
United States Loyalty Day (not legally determined) ❌ No Labor Day in September

As one of the few countries in Asia that upgraded May 1st to a public holiday in the same year, Taiwan’s Labor Day in 2026 not only includes personal holiday rights, but also is a historical moment for workers’ status to move closer to international standards**.

FAQ

Q1: I am a monthly salary employee, will my salary be deducted during the Labor Day holiday? A: No. Labor Day is a "paid holiday". Employees on a monthly salary system will be paid as they take this day off, and it does not count as absence from work. If the company deducts your salary because you didn't show up for work, it's a violation of the Labor Standards Act.

Q2: Are dispatched employees and part-time workers paid during Labor Day? A: Yes. As long as the Labor Standards Act applies, regardless of dispatch, part-time, or hourly workers, workers should be paid on Labor Day. For part-time workers, wages are calculated on a pro-rata basis. For example, if you agree to work 4 hours a day and have a holiday on that day, you should be paid 4 hours' wages.

Q3: Labor Day happens to be my "regular holiday" (such as Saturday), can it be combined with the holiday? A: cannot be combined with false. If Labor Day overlaps with a regular holiday or a rest day, according to the Ministry of Labor’s explanation, you should “choose a compensatory day off.” Most employers will choose another day to make up for the holiday afterwards. It is recommended to confirm the date of compensatory leave with the company first.

Q4: I am an employee on probation, will I be free on Labor Day? A: Yes. The Labor Standards Law still applies to workers during the probation period, and the rights and interests on all national holidays are exactly the same. Employers are not allowed to give discounts on the grounds of "no leave during the probation period", otherwise it is illegal.

Q5: Can civil servants really release 5/1 in 2026? A: It's really possible. From 2025-05-28, the "Regulations on the Implementation of Remembrance Days and Holidays" has added Labor Day as a national holiday. Civil servants, faculty, and students will all have a holiday on May 1, 2026. This is the first time that Taiwan has held a national holiday for three days. However, the actual holidays for police, fire fighters, coast guard, and military personnel may be moved to other days due to their shift duties.

Q6: Are there Labor Day holidays for foreign migrant workers? A: Yes. The leave provisions of the Labor Standards Law also apply to home care workers and domestic helpers, and employers must pay them wages or double their wages in accordance with the law. If there is any violation, you can appeal to 1955 (supports multiple languages).

Final words of advice

2026 is a historic year for Taiwan’s labor rights—Labor Day has changed from “labor-exclusive” to “nationally unified.” For workers, knowing their rights and interests is the first step, and having the courage to advocate for them is the second step**. If you encounter an illegal boss, 1955 is your free weapon. There is no charge before use, the whistleblower is kept confidential, and the results are guaranteed. **Wish everyone a 3-day family vacation on 5/1. **

item.title: 2026 Taiwan Income Tax Complete Guide: Deadlines, Deductions, Login Methods, and the 5-Step Refund Process
item.description: 2026 income tax filing in Taiwan runs May 1 to May 31 (with June 1 extension). This guide covers personal exemption, standard and itemized deductions, the 6 login methods, the 5-step filing process, top 5 common mistakes, and refund schedule — with worked examples for NT$30K-60K salaried workers to help you avoid overpaying.
item.content:encoded:
The deadline for individual income tax filing — May 1 to May 31 — is only days away. Every year, the National Taxation Bureau handles a pile of cases where people missed the filing deadline, used the wrong deductions, or got stuck on the login method. This guide covers the filing period, the personal exemption, the standard deduction, when to itemize, the 6 e-filing login methods, the 5 most common mistakes, and the earliest possible refund date — all framed for the 2026 (tax year 2025) Individual Income Tax return. Everything below is written for an office worker earning NT$30,000 to NT$60,000 a month, so follow along and avoid overpaying. Information current as of May 2026; defer to the official Ministry of Finance and National Taxation Bureau announcements.

2026 filing period and the basic threshold

What you file in 2026 is your 2025 income (tax year 2025), and the filing period runs May 1 (Fri) to May 31 (Sun), 2026. Because May 31 falls on a Sunday, regulations extend the deadline to 24:00 on Monday, June 1. The rule for whether you need to file is simple: if your annual income exceeds the combined threshold of personal exemption + standard deduction + special salary deduction, you must file.

For a single office worker, you need to file if your annual income (including salary) exceeds about NT$446,000. If you earn under roughly NT$36,000 a month, you may not owe any tax at all — but you should still file, because the salary income tax your employer withheld may be refunded.

Personal exemption and standard deduction: lock in the 2026 numbers

The personal exemption is the slice of income the government considers a baseline cost of living — not taxable. The 2026 figures:

  • NT$97,000 per person (yourself, your spouse, or your dependents).
  • For yourself, spouse, or direct ascendants aged 70 or older: NT$145,500 per person.

The standard deduction is a flat amount you can deduct without any documentation:

  • Single: NT$131,000.
  • Married couple filing jointly: NT$262,000.

For most office workers, the standard deduction is enough — unless you have large medical expenses, mortgage interest, or insurance premiums.

When does itemizing actually pay off?

Itemizing means deducting your actual expenses with receipts — worth doing only if the total exceeds the standard deduction. Common itemized items:

  • Insurance premiums: NHI premiums are fully deductible per person; other personal life insurance is capped at NT$24,000 per person.
  • Medical and maternity expenses: Receipts from MOF-recognized medical facilities are fully deductible (registration, hospitalization, surgery, etc.).
  • Home mortgage interest: Up to NT$300,000 per household (minus the savings-and-investment special deduction).
  • Donations: Donations to government, education, culture, or public-welfare organizations are capped at 20% of total gross income.
  • Disaster losses: Verified at actual amount, with a certificate from the local police or township office.

In practice, households with a mortgage usually come out ahead by itemizing, because interest alone often exceeds NT$100,000 a year. For renters, since tax year 2024, rental expense has moved from itemized to a "special deduction" — capped at NT$180,000 per household and stackable with the standard deduction. That's a real win for budget-conscious workers.

What special deductions exist? Salary, savings, long-term care, and more

Special deductions can be stacked on top of either the standard or itemized deductions, so this is the section people most often miss:

  • Special deduction for salaries and wages: NT$218,000 per person (whichever is larger compared to actual necessary expenses).
  • Special deduction for savings and investments: NT$270,000 per household — bank interest income is deductible up to this amount.
  • Special Preschool Deduction: For children under age 6 — NT$150,000 for the first child, NT$225,000 per child from the second onward (new in tax year 2025; the wealth-exclusion clause has been removed).
  • Special deduction for persons with disabilities: NT$218,000 per person.
  • Special deduction for tuition: NT$25,000 per dependent child enrolled in junior college or above.
  • Special deduction for long-term care: NT$180,000 per qualified disabled person (new starting tax year 2025; raised from NT$120,000, retroactive to January 1, 2025).
  • Special deduction for rental expense: NT$180,000 per household for renters using the place as their primary residence (newly independent).

Many office workers only remember the salary deduction and forget that bank time-deposit interest qualifies for the NT$270,000 savings-and-investment deduction. If you help pay nursing-home fees for a family member, don't forget to claim the long-term care deduction too.

6 e-filing login methods: just pick the fastest one for you

The MOF's Individual Income Tax e-Filing and Tax Payment System supports a total of 6 login methods. Pick based on what tools you already have on hand:

  • Mobile-phone authentication: Your own mobile number + ID number + NHI card number. Fastest at about 30 seconds. ⚠️ The mobile number must be registered in your own name — a number under a family member's name won't work.
  • NHI card + registration password: Requires an NHI card reader; if you don't have one, switch to mobile-phone authentication.
  • Citizen Digital Certificate: Requires the Ministry of the Interior certificate plus a card reader. Downloads the most complete data (auto-imports withholding statements, insurance premiums, donation records).
  • Mobile Citizen Digital Certificate: The mobile version of the Citizen Digital Certificate — set it up once, then use fingerprint or face recognition to authenticate, no card reader needed.
  • Household registration number + lookup code: The lookup code can be printed for free at convenience-store KIOSKs. Quick and easy.
  • Financial Certificate: An electronic certificate issued by your bank or brokerage — handy if you already have one.

⚠️ The QR code on payment slips is for "paying tax," not "logging in": Many people mistake it for a login method. In fact, it's a barcode on the payment slip used to pay tax by credit or debit card after scanning. You still need one of the 6 methods above to log in.

5 steps to file: from login to payment

Once you've picked a login method, the actual filing process is straightforward — most people finish in under 20 minutes:

  • Prep your authentication: Pick one of the 6 methods and verify it works (the Citizen Digital Certificate is valid for 5 years; your NHI card password may need to be registered first).
  • Download the e-filing software and log in: From May 1, the system auto-imports your salary, interest, and withholding statements. For mobile, use the "Individual Income Tax e-Filing" app.
  • Confirm income and dependents: Check whether any side-gig, rental, or dividend income is missing; for dependents, confirm no one else has already claimed them.
  • Choose your deduction method: The software auto-compares standard vs. itemized and picks the more favorable option.
  • Choose payment or refund: Enter your bank account if you're due a refund; if you owe tax, pick a lump sum or installments (over NT$30,000 splits into up to 3 installments), credit card installments, or convenience-store payment (for amounts under NT$20,000).

If you want to confirm whether your full-year salary hits the taxable threshold, use the date calculator to check your employer's pay cycle — that way you don't accidentally count current-year income as last year.

5 most common filing mistakes: people trip over these every year

The bureau publishes an annual error ranking. The traps office workers fall into most:

  • Under-reporting dividends or side income: Brokerage dividends, podcast ad revenue, Shopee stores, food-delivery work, tutoring, royalties, YouTube ad revenue — the bureau reconciles data from 8 major platforms, so don't gamble.
  • Claiming rental expense without a complete contract and transfer record: Renters claiming rental expense must have a lease, proof of payment (transfer records), and proof of residency — all three.
  • Parents both claiming the same dependent, causing duplicate claims among siblings: Each dependent can only be claimed by one filer. Talk it through ahead of time.
  • Ticking "spouse separate calculation" but botching the math: The e-filing software auto-runs all three calculation methods — just pick the lowest result. Don't calculate by hand.
  • Wrong account number for the refund: If the transfer fails, you have to re-apply, which can delay your refund by 1–2 months. Double-check before submitting.

Refund traps and tax-saving moves: most people don't know these

A few details that quietly save tax:

  • Don't forget to include dependents on your joint filing: Each dependent adds about NT$97,000 in extra exemption, provided they meet the dependent criteria (living with you, actual financial support, income below the exemption).
  • Voluntary 6% Labor Pension contribution doesn't count toward current-year income: It's deducted directly from taxable income — one of the most effective tax-saving tools for salary earners. At NT$40,000 monthly salary contributing 6%, NT$28,800 a year is tax-free; a 5% bracket saves NT$1,440, a 12% bracket saves NT$3,456.
  • Ask for electronic donation receipts: Most public-welfare organizations offer a "direct upload to your tax return" service, which saves you sorting through receipts.
  • Medical expenses limited to NHI-contracted facilities: Non-NHI items like cosmetic procedures or orthodontics can't be itemized.
  • 0% interest installments for tax payment: When the amount due is large, 0–12 month credit card installments often beat a bank loan on fees.

When does the refund land? As early as late July

The 2026 refund lands in three batches:

  • Batch 1: July 31, 2026 (filers who submitted between May 1 and May 10, error-free).
  • Batch 2: October 31, 2026 (filers who submitted between May 11 and May 31).
  • Batch 3: January 20, 2027 (supplemental documents, manual review, late filers).

Per past bureau data, the average Batch 1 refund is about NT$15,000–16,000, and Batch 3 averages around NT$11,000 (varies by batch and year). The simplest way to land your refund early: file online before May 10 and choose direct deposit — it can hit your account as early as the end of July.

New in 2026: guidance period for creator income tax

The MOF announced in 2026 that streamer, podcaster, and platform-content-creator income is formally included in individual income tax, with a guidance period through June 30, 2026. During this window, voluntary make-up filings carry no penalty and no interest. If you earned YouTube, Twitch, Instagram, or TikTok ad revenue, sponsored content fees, or paid-subscription income in 2025, file during the guidance period — getting caught later can mean a fine of 2–3× the under-reported tax.

⚠️ If your annual sales approach the NT$100,000 per month for goods / NT$50,000 per month for services ceiling for personal sellers (the 2026 threshold), you may also need to register for business tax — that's a separate regulation.

FAQ

Q1: My monthly salary is NT$35,000 and my employer withholds tax. Do I still need to file?

Yes. Even if your annual income doesn't reach the taxable threshold, the only way to recover the tax your employer already withheld is to file. Skipping the filing is essentially giving the money to the government.

Q2: Can I use both the standard deduction and itemized deductions at the same time?

No. You pick one or the other. Special deductions, however, stack on top of either one. So after choosing the standard deduction, you can still claim salary, savings, rental, and other special deductions.

Q3: I forgot to file last year. Will I be fined? How do I fix it?

Under Article 110 of the Income Tax Act, an individual who fails to file individual income tax with tax payable faces a fine of up to 3× the under-reported tax, on top of paying the back tax. If you filed but under-reported, the cap is 2×. But if you voluntarily file and pay the make-up before any complaint or audit, Article 48-1 of the Tax Collection Act lets you avoid the penalty — you only owe interest. Late tax payment carries a 1% surcharge for every 3 days overdue. ⚠️ Note: Articles often misapply the "10% late-filing fee / 20% non-filing fee" rules — those are corporate income tax rules. Individual income tax has no late-filing or non-filing fees, only the penalties above.

Q4: How do I report dividend income? Is combined or separate taxation better?

Dividends can go through "combined taxation" (which grants an 8.5% tax credit, capped at NT$80,000 per household) or "separate taxation at 28%". For office workers in the 20% bracket or lower, combined taxation almost always wins. The e-filing software auto-compares — just follow its recommendation.

Q5: First time filing on your own — which login method should you use?

The top recommendation is the Mobile Citizen Digital Certificate (mobile app + fingerprint or face recognition): set it up once, reuse it every year, no card reader needed. If you haven't applied for a Citizen Digital Certificate yet, mobile-phone authentication is the fastest path (number must be in your own name) and requires no extra credentials. If your mobile number is in a family member's name, fall back to "household registration number + lookup code" (printed at convenience stores).

New numbers that kick in next year (May 2027 filing)

Under Article 5 of the Income Tax Act, when the cumulative CPI increase reaches 3% or more, the personal exemption, standard deduction, and special salary deduction must be adjusted upward by the increase. The 2027 applicable CPI rose 4.13% versus 2025, hitting the threshold. So the May 2027 filing (tax year 2026 income) will use these new figures:

  • Personal exemption: from NT$97,000 to NT$101,000 (for those 70+, from NT$145,500 to NT$151,500).
  • Standard deduction: singles from NT$131,000 to NT$136,000; married couples from NT$262,000 to NT$272,000.
  • Special deduction for salaries and wages: from NT$218,000 to NT$227,000.
  • Special deduction for persons with disabilities: from NT$218,000 to NT$227,000.

Worth flagging: the long-term care special deduction increase from NT$120,000 to NT$180,000 is already retroactive to tax year 2025 (so it applies for this May 2026 filing) — you don't have to wait until 2027.

Bottom line: most deductions for this May 2026 filing didn't change, but if you support a disabled family member, make sure to use the new NT$180,000 long-term care deduction. If you had platform-creator income in 2025, file during the June 30 guidance period. From next year, all office workers will benefit from higher exemption and deduction thresholds — expect a smaller tax bill.

If you need to combine multiple withholding-statement photos into one PDF for upload, the PDF Merge Tool handles it; if you need to compress receipt photos to meet upload limits, the Image Compression Tool batches them in one pass. Before filing, also worth reading the Tax Refund Money Management Guide — think through the smartest way to allocate the money before it lands.

item.title: How to Use Your 2026 Tax Refund Wisely: 5 Smart Allocation Strategies for Young Workers in Taiwan
item.description: Average refund is about NT$10K-15K per case. This guide gives NT$30K-60K salaried workers a 5-step allocation order — emergency fund, credit card debt, savings, ETFs, self-investment — with worked examples for NT$5K, 10K, and 30K refund amounts and avalanche-vs-snowball debt strategy comparisons.
item.content:encoded:
After filing taxes every May, what office workers look forward to most is the tax refund that will be credited at the end of July. According to the statistics released by the National Taxation Bureau over the years, the average tax refund amount per item is about 10,000 to 15,000 yuan (the first batch of 3.62 million people / 58.5 billion → an average of about 16,000 yuan in 2025; the average of the third batch in 2024 is about 11,000 yuan), and there may be more dual-income families. The problem is that once this "windfall" comes into the account, it will almost always be eaten up silently by eating, shopping, and watching TV series and subscriptions. This article provides 5 priorities for using tax refunds for small bourgeoisie with a monthly salary of 30,000 to 60,000 yuan. It also attaches examples of specific allocation ratios and decision-making examples. If you follow these steps, the tax refunds can truly help your finances. The information in this article is updated as of May 2026.

Why shouldn’t tax refund money be spent directly?

Many people will say, "The tax refund is not in the budget to begin with, so it would be a pity to spend it." This concept has two blind spots:

  • The tax refund is not money given to you by the government: It is the salary tax that was withheld every month from you, which is equivalent to "forced saving for one year" and you will get it back in one go.
  • Single large amounts are the easiest to develop bad habits: The "mental accounting effect" in behavioral economics will make people take sudden money less seriously, and the actual purchase decision will be 2-3 times more relaxed than usual.

Treat the tax refund as the "second year-end bonus of the year" and establish a distribution formula to accumulate considerable assets every year in the future. The point is to deduct first and then spend, not spend first and then see how much is left. Calculated from the annual tax refund of 15,000, if you invest seriously for 10 consecutive years, the tax refund alone can accumulate at least 150,000 principal plus compound interest income.

No. 1: Build a 3-6 month emergency reserve

The emergency reserve fund is the basis of all financial management and can support life in the event of unemployment, illness, or family emergency. The recommended amount is 3 to 6 times your monthly living expenses:

  • Monthly salary of 30,000 yuan: emergency fund of 90,000 to 180,000 yuan
  • Monthly salary of 40,000: emergency fund of 120,000 to 240,000
  • Monthly salary of 50,000: emergency fund of 150,000 to 300,000
  • Monthly salary 60,000: emergency fund 180,000 to 360,000

If you don’t have an emergency fund yet, 100% of your tax refund will be invested in this account. It is recommended to place high-interest savings in digital banks (such as Taishin Richart 3.5% annual interest for new accounts within 300,000, Wing Fung DAWHO, Future Bank, etc.), which can not only receive interest but can be used at any time. A complete emergency fund usually takes 1-2 years to accumulate. Don't rush to buy stocks or funds yet. First, 1 month of living expenses will be used as the "minimum safety allowance", and then it will be paid up to 3-6 months in stages.

Second pick: Pay off high-interest card debt and credit

If you have a recurring credit card (annual interest rate of 7-15%, legal upper limit of 15%, most banks have been between 13-15% in recent years), cash cards, or credit (annual interest rate of 5-12%, depending on personal credit history), the best use of tax refund money is to pay off debt. The reason is simple:

  • High-interest savings 3.5% interest rate vs. credit card debt interest rate 13-15%, the gap is more than 4 times
  • Early repayment is the most certain "rate of return" and there is no market risk
  • After the debt is reduced, the monthly cash flow immediately becomes wider and the credit score recovers.

There are two debt repayment strategies. Which one you choose depends on the easiest way for you to stick to it:

  • Avalanche Method: Prioritize repayment with the highest interest rate (for example, the card with 14% repayment first). The most cost-effective financial solution, the total interest can be saved by 20-30% in 5 years
  • Snowball Method: Pay off the debt with the smallest balance first (for example, pay off the small debt of 8,000 yuan at once). High sense of psychological achievement, suitable for people who easily give up halfway

For example: You have two debts, credit card A is 60,000 yuan / interest rate 14%, and credit card B is 10,000 yuan / interest rate 7%. The avalanche method prioritizes paying off A (saving the most interest), and the snowball method prioritizes paying off B (quickly seeing a debt return to zero). It is recommended that people with a monthly salary of 30,000 to 40,000 yuan and small debts use the snowball method. When they see it return to zero, they will be more motivated to stick to it.

Third pick: Enrich savings insurance and time deposits

If your emergency fund is ready and you have no credit card debt, the next step is to allocate your tax refund to medium-term savings tools:

  • Digital Bank High Interest Savings: 3.5% for new Richart accounts within 300,000 yuan, 1.6% for new Wing Fung DAWHO accounts within 500,000 yuan, 2.5% for new bank accounts within 300,000 yuan in the future, some accounts can reach 2% to 3.5%
  • 1-year fixed deposit: The annual interest rate is about 1.6% (Taiwan dollars), suitable for funds that are not used in the short term; the U.S. dollar fixed deposit is about 4-4.5%, but there is exchange rate risk
  • Savings insurance (more than 6 years): Annualized rate of return 1.5% to 2.5%, locked interest rate, but poor liquidity, cancellation in the first 6 years will result in a loss of 5-15%; if the money may be used in the next 6 years, fixed deposits are more suitable

For example: If you save 1 million for a 6-year savings insurance at the age of 30, if you need money urgently to terminate the contract in the third year, you may only get back 880,000 to 920,000, which is equivalent to a loss of 80,000 to 120,000 in principal. It is recommended to leave at least 50,000 to 100,000 in a digital bank high-interest account as a "semi-emergency fund", somewhere between emergency funds and investments.

No. 4: Try index ETF or monthly dividend distribution

After accumulating emergency funds, tax refund money can be invested. The most friendly tool for petty bourgeoisie is Taiwan Stock Index ETF:

  • 0050 (Yanta Taiwan 50): Tracks the top 50 companies in Taiwan by market capitalization, The annualized return in the past five years is approximately 10.88% (2020-2024 range)
  • 006208 (Fubon Channel 50): Similar to 0050, the total expense ratio is lower (about 0.24% vs 0.43% of 0050)
  • 00878, 00919, 00940 and other high dividend ETFs: suitable for conservatives who pursue quarterly dividend distribution, with a yield rate of about 5-7%

A tax refund of 10,000 yuan can buy 1-2 shares of 00878 (about 21 yuan per share), or you can accumulate 0050 in odd shares (about 220 yuan per share → a tax refund of 10,000 yuan can buy about 45 shares). Before investing, ask yourself: **Will this money be used in the next 3 years? **If so, don't buy stocks; short-term fluctuations in the stock market may make you panic and sell at lows. The best practice is to buy at regular fixed amounts in 2-4 times to average costs and reduce time-point risks.

No. 5: Invest in yourself (learning and health)

If the above four items have been taken care of, the last tax refund can be invested in yourself:

  • Online courses: AI tools (ChatGPT / Claude / Cursor), presentations, English, financial report analysis, you can buy a good course for 1,000 to 5,000 yuan
  • Health Checkup: Over the age of 30, a complete health checkup every 2 years at your own expense costs about 10,000 yuan. Early detection and early treatment of diseases are better than treatment.
  • Sports Equipment or Membership: Annual gym fee, running shoes, yoga mat, to establish exercise habits
  • Professional Certificate: registration examination fees, teaching material fees, and increased salary negotiation chips

Investing in yourself often has the highest rate of return, but only if you really know how to use it. It is a waste to buy an online course and never open it, or to apply for a gym card and only go to it three times. It is recommended to try it out for a week first, and then buy the paid version if you are sure that you will continue.

Example of tax refund allocation ratio (5,000 / 10,000 / 30,000 yuan)

The following are suggestions for the allocation of different tax refund amounts, assuming you already have some emergency funds and no credit card debt:

  • Tax refund of 5,000 yuan: Invest all 5,000 yuan in emergency funds or digital bank high-interest savings (richart new account 3.5% annual interest, receive about 175 yuan interest in one year)
  • Tax refund 10,000 yuan: 6,000 yuan emergency fund + 3,000 yuan ETF odd shares (can buy about 13 shares of 0050 or about 142 shares of 00878) + 1,000 yuan for self-investment (course subscription)
  • Tax refund of RMB 30,000: RMB 10,000 emergency fund + RMB 10,000 ETF + RMB 5,000 savings insurance + RMB 5,000 health check-up or course

Before planning, you may wish to use the Exchange Rate Conversion Tool to see how many shares you can buy if the tax refund money is converted into US dollars to invest in overseas ETFs such as VOO or VT; or to evaluate the pros and cons of retaining Taiwan dollars. Once you create your own distribution formula, it will be executed automatically every July, eliminating the need for any extra thought.

FAQ

Q1: Will the tax refund be credited to my account by the end of July?

uncertain. Only those who completed online declarations from May 1 to May 10 without errors will receive tax refunds in the first batch (end of July). Those who file after May 11th will have to wait until the end of October, and those who submit supplementary documents or manual review will not be credited until January 20th of the following year at the latest. According to announcements by the National Taxation Bureau over the years, the amount credited to the first batch accounts for about 70-80% of the total tax refund households, while the third batch only accounts for about 50,000-70,000 households.

Q2: I have credit card debt and insufficient emergency funds. Should I pay off the debt first or save money first?

It is recommended to save the "minimum safety fund" (1 month's living expenses) first to avoid taking on new debts during the debt repayment process (for example: no emergency fund → sudden toothache and need for dental implant → forced to swipe credit card → new debt). After that, priority will be given to repaying high-interest debts with interest rates above 13%, and the remainder will be used to supplement emergency funds. Do both in parallel to avoid falling into a debt cycle. If your monthly salary is less than 30,000 yuan and your credit card debt exceeds 300,000 yuan, you may consider applying for debt negotiation (the interest rate is reduced to 5-9%) and adding tax refunds to speed up the repayment.

Q3: Can I use my tax refund money to buy ETFs?

Not recommended. Unless you have an emergency fund set aside and won’t need it in the next 5 years. If an investment encounters a sharp drop (2008 / 2020 / 2022 have all fallen by 20-40%), the psychological pressure will be great, and it is easy to accept losses at the low point and rush out. It is recommended to buy ** in regular fixed amounts in 2-4 times to spread the time-point risks and lower the average cost.

Q4: Is savings insurance really cost-effective? Is it better than a fixed deposit?

The annualized rate of return of savings insurance is usually slightly higher than that of fixed deposits (about 1.5-2.5% vs 1.5-1.6% for fixed deposits), but the liquidity is much poorer, and the loss of capital will be 5-15% if canceled in the first 6 years**. If you are likely to use this money within 6 years, a fixed deposit or a digital bank high-interest deposit is more suitable. Savings insurance is suitable for people who "know that they will not use it for more than 10 years + want to force savings", such as setting aside education funds for their children and insuring themselves for retirement at 65.

Q5: Can tax refund funds be used to directly purchase virtual currency or cryptocurrency?

Not recommended as primary configuration. Cryptocurrencies are extremely volatile (Bitcoin fell from 60,000 US dollars to 16,000 US dollars in 2022, a drop of 73%), and are not suitable for use as stable assets. If you are really interested, it is recommended that you only use 5-10% of the tax refund as "entertainment money" to enter the market (for example, if you have a tax refund of 10,000 yuan, only use 1,000 yuan), and choose mainstream currencies (BTC/ETH) instead of small coins; at the same time, remember that "you can only enter the market if you can lose all the money", and never use emergency funds or borrow money to buy coins.

A tax refund is not just a lump sum of money, but a good time to review your financial health. Read [2026 Comprehensive Tax Declaration Complete Guide] (/blog/en/tax-filing-guide-2026/) before your tax refund is credited to your account to confirm how much you should refund; after it is credited, follow the steps in step 5 of this article. Over a period of 5-10 years, the tax refund can be converted into a considerable asset base, rather than another consumption opportunity.

item.content:encoded:
With a monthly salary of RMB 30,000 to RMB 60,000, if your mobile phone suddenly breaks, your motorcycle is sent for repair, a family member gets sick and is hospitalized, or your company suddenly lays off employees...these things are not about "if it will happen" but "when". The emergency fund is life-saving money that allows you to save money in these emergencies without having to swipe your card to borrow money or talk to your family.

This article uses the latest actual figures in 2026 to tell you: how much to save, where to put it, and how to start saving. Even office workers with no basic knowledge can accumulate money painlessly. The information in this article is updated as of May 2026.

What is an emergency fund? Why should every office worker have one?

The definition of emergency fund is simple: Cash that can sustain your basic life for 3-6 months even if you have no income at all. It is not an investment, it is not a savings insurance, it is not money placed in stocks, but cash that can be withdrawn at any time without losing money.

Why is it important? According to data from the Accounting and Accounting Office, the average window period between job changes for Taiwanese employees is about 2-4 months, and it may be longer than half a year for middle-aged and elderly people. In the event of being temporarily laid off, unable to work due to illness, or having an accident in the family, people without reserve funds can only make ends meet by swiping their credit cards, and the snowball of debt will get bigger and bigger.

The function of an emergency fund is to "allow you to maintain your options during low times." You don't have to take a bad job just to pay next month's rent.

How much should you save? Calculation formula for 3-6 months living expenses

The most common rule is: 3 months for singles and 6 months for families. But how to calculate "one month's living expenses"? It's not your monthly salary, but "the money you have to spend in a month", which usually includes:

  • Rent or mortgage
  • Water, electricity, gas, mobile Internet
  • Meal expenses (minimum standard for eating out or self-catering)
  • Transportation expenses
  • Insurance premiums (health insurance, labor insurance, life insurance, etc.)
  • Fixed loan monthly payment (car loan, student loan)

These add up to your "minimum cost of living." Entertainment, dressing up, and dinner parties are not considered, and these can be suspended in an emergency.

Actual calculation of monthly salary of RMB 30,000 to RMB 60,000: How much money do you need?

Here are three typical examples:

Example A: Single person with a monthly salary of 30,000, renting a house

  • Rent 9,000 + Water, electricity and gas 1,500 + Food 8,000 + Transportation 2,000 + Insurance 2,000 = Monthly minimum 22,500
  • 3 months reserve fund = 67,500 yuan

Example B: Monthly salary of 45,000, renting a house with double income and no children (individual part)

  • Rent 15,000 (7,500 shared between two persons) + Water, electricity and gas 1,500 + Food 10,000 + Transportation 3,000 + Insurance 3,000 = Monthly minimum 25,000
  • 3 months reserve fund = 75,000 yuan

Example C: Monthly salary of 60,000, married with children

  • Mortgage 25,000 + Water, electricity and gas 2,500 + Food 18,000 + Childcare 12,000 + Transportation 4,000 + Insurance 5,000 = Monthly minimum 66,500
  • 6 months reserve fund = 399,000 yuan

Seems like a lot? In fact, as long as half of the monthly excess cash is automatically transferred to the reserve account, most people can save the target in 1-2 years. The key point is not "how many there are now", but "has it started yet".

Where is the safest place to put emergency reserves without leaving them idle? 2026 Digital bank high-interest living deposit comparison

The key to reserve funds is Liquidity > Yield. If you put it in the wrong place, it will be discounted. Comparison of high-interest deposits of mainstream digital banks in 2026:

Recommended combination (risk diversification)

  • Below 300,000: 3.5% for new Richart accounts (if you haven’t opened an account yet) or 2% in the future
  • 300,000-500,000: 300,000 to Richart + 100,000 to NewNewBank/Wangdao (enjoy high interest) + the remaining to Sino-Fung / in the future
