Don’t put it anywhere ⛔

  • Stocks, ETFs, Funds: They may fall or be stuck when you need money most.
  • Virtual Currency: Extremely volatile, completely unsuitable as a reserve fund
  • Savings Insurance: If canceled before maturity, you will lose 10-30%, and the liquidity is extremely poor.
  • Long-term fixed deposit: You will lose interest if you cancel it

How to start saving with zero foundation? Painless accumulation in three steps

First Month: Capture True Monthly Expenses

Dig out the credit card bills and EasyCard records for the past 3 months, add them up by category, and calculate the average monthly "necessary expenditures". You can use Excel or accounting apps (MoneyGo, CWMoney, cumulative accounting) to classify.

Second month: Open a dedicated account

It is recommended to use a digital bank to open a special "Emergency Reserve" account, which is separate from the salary account. Richart, Yongfeng, Future, and Wangdao can all open accounts online in 5-10 minutes without having to visit a branch.

Starting from the third month: Set up automatic transfer

On payday, 10-20% of salary will be automatically transferred to this special account until the target amount of 3 or 6 months is reached.

If you want to quickly calculate how many months you need to save to reach your goal, you can use the Date Calculator to work out the target date and use it with the Countdown Timer to track the progress. It is easier to stick to it than relying solely on willpower.

Common misunderstanding: Don’t count this money into the emergency reserve fund

Many people mistakenly think that the following items can be used as reserve funds, but they find out at the critical moment that there is no money to use:

  • Credit Card Limit: This is a liability, not a deposit. If you use a credit card to pay for emergency expenses, the cash pressure will be greater next month. Credit card recurring interest rates of 7-15% (legal limit of 15%) will put you into a deeper debt cycle
  • Savings Insurance: You will lose money if you terminate it before it expires, and the liquidity is extremely poor.
  • Stocks, Funds: If you are forced to sell when the market is bad, you will realize losses instead.
  • Loan Promise from Relatives and Friends: When you really need money, others may not be able to lend it.
  • Estimated year-end bonus: It may be reduced or even canceled when the economy is bad, so it cannot be used as a stable source.

FAQ

Q1: The reserve fund has been saved for 6 months, do I still need to save it? A: No need. After you have saved enough, the excess money can be transferred to investments (stocks, ETFs, retirement withdrawals, etc.) to pursue higher returns. The role of reserve funds is "defense", not "offense". If you put too much, you will miss the opportunity cost. Re-examine it every year and adjust it to meet your living expenses.

Q2: Do people with mortgages need more reserve funds? A: Yes. A mortgage is a fixed and uninterruptible expense. It is recommended that those with a mortgage prepare at least 6 months of living expenses + a reserve fund for the mortgage. If the family only has a single salary, it is recommended to increase it to 9-12 months to avoid unemployment and the risk of supply cuts.

Q3: Can the reserve fund be used to pay card fees or invest? A: Strongly not recommended. Once the reserve fund is diverted to "non-emergency purposes", the original insurance function is lost. If you really need to invest cash flow, you should separate an "investment account" from your salary and manage it completely separately from the reserve fund.

Q4: Can I invest at the same time while saving funds? A: Yes, but the order is important. It is recommended to first save a one-month reserve fund + pay off high-interest-rate liabilities, and then start small regular investments (for example, NT$3,000 per month in ETFs). Investing and saving funds at the same time can help maintain habits, but will not compress the quality of life due to excessive concentration.

Q5: Is NewNewBank 15% true? What are the traps? A: It is true, but there are restrictions: ① Only new accounts ② The limit is 100,000 ③ There is usually a "promotion period" of 3-6 months. Therefore, do not throw all your money into it as a long-term plan. It is suitable for the strategy of "enjoy high profits first, and then transfer to other long-term plans before expiration".

Q6: Richart 3.5% is limited to new accounts, what should I do if I already have Richart? A: 1.8% (in the first half of 2026) for existing accounts within 300,000 yuan, which is still a relatively good living interest rate in the market. If you haven’t had a Richart account yet, it is recommended to open an account as soon as possible to enjoy the high interest rate of 3.5% in the first year** (annual interest gap: 300,000 × (3.5%-1.8%) = 5,100 yuan/year).

Q7: Will it be troublesome to decentralize multiple banks? A: Actually it’s not bad. Every bank app is easy to use, and setting up automatic transfers is done once. Only 1-2 operations are required per year (adjustment of new and old account discounts + review of interest rates at the beginning of the year). For an extra 1-2% interest rate, it's worth spending half an hour setting it up.

Act now

The first thing you can do today: Open the Salary Account App, check your cash balance, calculate how far you are from the 3-month reserve fund, and then set up automatic transfer to the special account starting tomorrow.

Having a target number first is 10 times more effective than just thinking "I should save money". If you don’t have a digital bank account yet, take 10 minutes to open a Richart tonight or in the future, set up automatic debits and start building your safety net from next month’s payday.

item.title: Is Voluntary 6% Labor Pension Self-Contribution Worth It? A 2026 Update Guide for NT$40K-150K Workers
item.description: Is the voluntary 6% Labor Pension self-contribution worth it? This 2026 guide uses real numbers — NT$40K monthly contributors save NT$1.4M-2M over 30 years; NT$80K singles save NT$5,967 in taxes annually; dual-income couples (NT$150K+120K) save NT$32,046 — to help you decide.
item.content:encoded:
Have you ever had this question when you see the withholding details every time you receive your salary: ** "Is it worth it to withdraw 6% on retirement? I will get 2,400 yuan less every month. Is it really a good deal when I retire?"**

This article uses the latest figures for 2026 to help office workers with a monthly salary of RMB 30,000 to RMB 150,000 calculate clearly: how the new labor retirement system works, the three major advantages of self-withdrawal, the actual tax savings, and who should apply immediately and who should wait for a while. The information in this article is updated as of March 2026.

What is the new labor retirement system? What is the difference between the employer’s 6% and the individual’s 6%?

Let’s first clarify the concept: the new labor retirement system (implemented in July 2005) and labor insurance are two completely different retirement systems.

System Nature Source of allocation How to receive
Labor Insurance Old-age annuity, mutual aid from generation to generation Labor + employer + government share in proportion Monthly pension / lump sum
New labor retirement system Personal account, belongs to you forever Employer compulsorily contributes 6% of salary (employees can voluntarily contribute another 0-6%) One-time payment/monthly refund after age 60

Key Point: The money you withdraw from your personal account when you retire can be taken with you when you change jobs. It follows your ID card number, not the company.

So what is "self-withdrawal"? It means that the workers themselves withdraw an additional 0-6% of their salary to the same special account. The employer’s 6% contribution is not a dime, and the portion raised by yourself will be deducted from your salary. In other words, self-withdrawal is to save an extra pension for yourself, and enjoy the benefits of tax saving and guaranteed returns.

Monthly salary of RMB 40,000, self-withdrawal of 6%. Actual calculation.

Suppose you have a monthly salary of 40,000 yuan and a self-withdrawal of 6% is 2,400 yuan per month, which is 28,800 yuan a year. Self-collection for 30 consecutive years:

Annualized rate of return 30-year cumulative principal and interest sum
3% About 1.4 million
4% About 1.7 million
5% About 2 million

This is additional pension, calculated separately from the employer's 6% contribution, which is equal to an extra amount of "available" cash when you retire.

Actual returns of the Labor Retirement Fund in recent years: The long-term average annualized rate is 4-5% (significantly higher than the 1.5-2% for two-year time deposits). Therefore, it is actually close to the accumulated principal and profit of “more than 1.7 million”.

Three major advantages of self-withdrawal: tax saving, forced savings, and guaranteed returns

Many people think that self-improvement means saving oneself, and there is nothing special about it. There are actually three clear advantages:

1. The tax saving effect is immediate

The self-withdrawal amount is not included in the salary income of the current year. In other words, the money you withdraw is deducted from your tax base. The following is the latest calculation for 2026:

Monthly salary Annual self-withdrawal amount Tax rate bracket Annual provincial tax
30,000 21,600 5% 1,080
40,000 28,800 12% 3,456
60,000 43,200 12% 5,184
80,000(Single) 57,744 12-20% About 5,967
100,000 72,000 20% 14,400
Double-income couple 150,000+120,000 108,000+87,048 20% About 32,046

⚠️ A family with a monthly salary of more than RMB 80,000 + married + two-income earners can legally save more than RMB 30,000 in tax per year**, and the accumulated tax savings in 30 years are equivalent to an extra RMB 1 million in pension.

2. Forced Saving

You must be 60 years old to receive from the special labor retirement account, and it cannot be used during the period. For office workers who can't save money, this is the most effective "lock-up" mechanism - it will be deducted on the monthly payday, and your living account will not be handled, so you can naturally save.

3. Lower limit of guaranteed income

The labor retirement fund guarantees that it will not be lower than the two-year time deposit interest rate** (the two-year time deposit rate of public banks in 2026 is about 1.5-2%, announced monthly by the Labor Fund Utilization Bureau of the Ministry of Labor). If the operation loses money, the country will make up the difference**. Compared with the risk of losing money on your own investment, this is a very reassuring bottom line.

Actual average return of labor retirement fund in the past 5 years: about 4-5%, significantly better than the guaranteed lower limit.

Who is suitable for self-pickup? Who is not recommended?

Suitable for self-pickup ✅

  • Monthly salary of more than RMB 40,000 and tax rate above 12%: obvious tax saving benefits
  • People who cannot save money and are prone to impulsive consumption: Forced saving has a strong effect
  • Stable job, no need for large sums of money in the short term: Anyway, you have to wait until you are 60 to receive it
  • Those who already have emergency reserves and basic insurance plans: Self-collection will not affect the quality of daily life

It is not recommended for people who pick it up by themselves ❌

  • Monthly salary below 30,000, tax rate is 5%: The tax saving amount is limited and the cash flow pressure is high. First save the emergency reserve to 3 months of living expenses before considering
  • Have debts with high interest rates (revolving credit cards, cash cards): Pay off the debt first, The annualized interest rate of the recurring credit card is 7-15% (the legal limit is 15%), which is far more terrible than the 3% pension return
  • Those who plan to buy a house, start a business, or get married in the short term: These large expenditures will require cash, and you have to wait until you are 60 to withdraw them.

Centrist (you can test the water temperature from 3%)

  • Monthly salary 50,000-70,000, tax rate 12%
  • Have 1-2 months emergency fund but less than 6 months
  • There are low-interest student loans but not as good as credit cards

It is recommended to test the water temperature from 3%, and then decide whether to raise it to 6% after half a year. Step by step will not disrupt the rhythm of life.

How to apply for self-collection of labor retirement? Operation steps

The application process is simpler than imagined. No need to go to the Labor Insurance Bureau, just go to the company directly:

  1. Talk to company HR or human resources: Fill out the "Application Form for Change of Individual Voluntary Contribution Rate of Labor Pension"
  2. Select self-withdrawal ratio: 1%-6% (every 1% is one level)
  3. Wait until next month to take effect: The new withdrawal rate is usually implemented from the next month
  4. Can be adjusted or stopped at any time: It can be adjusted up to twice a year. If cash is needed temporarily, it can be temporarily reduced to 0%

To estimate the change in actual salary after self-withdrawal, you can use the Unit Conversion Tool to quickly calculate the difference between levels, or use the Countdown Timer to set a cumulative target for the monthly self-withdrawal amount to make progress more visible.

Labor retirement account inquiry and long-term planning suggestions

Three query pipelines

  1. Labor Insurance Bureau website (Log in with natural person certificate or health insurance card)
  2. "Labor Insurance Bureau e-service system" App (log in via mobile phone verification)
  3. Labor Insurance Bureau counter inquiry (local offices)

It is recommended to check every six months to confirm that the employer has actually made contributions, so as to avoid the employer's short payment or missed payment. If you find that the employer should have mentioned it but failed to do so, you can report it to the Labor Insurance Bureau (this is an illegal act by the employer, and workers' rights and interests are protected).

Long-term planning suggestions

The financial pyramid is in order from bottom to top:

  1. Emergency reserve fund (3-6 months living expenses)
  2. Settlement of high interest rate debt (credit card, cash card)
  3. Basic medical insurance, accident insurance
  4. Self-withdrawal of 6% on labor retirement (tax saving + guaranteed income + forced savings)
  5. Active investment (stocks, ETFs, regular quotas)

First save up to 6 months of emergency reserves and pay off high-interest rate debt before you start thinking about withdrawing funds. If you have plenty of money now, you can test the water temperature from 3%, and then decide whether to increase it to 6% after half a year.

FAQ

Q1: Can the self-withdrawn money be withdrawn midway? A: In principle, no. The new labor retirement system stipulates that you must be 60 years old or older to claim retirement benefits. Only in extreme circumstances such as death, total disability, or loss of contact can you claim benefits in advance. If you are in urgent need of cash, you can only stop withdrawing money yourself, but you still have to wait until you turn 60 to receive the amount you have already withdrawn.

Q2: Will self-delivery be interrupted after changing jobs? A: No. The personal retirement account is based on your ID card number, not the company. After changing jobs, as long as you apply for withdrawal again at the new company, the money in the old account will still be retained and interest will continue to accrue.

**Q3: Will there be any conflict between self-payment after retirement and labor insurance and old-age annuity? ** A: No conflict at all. Labor retirement and labor insurance are two independent systems: labor insurance is a monthly pension or a lump sum, and the new labor retirement system is a personal account. **You can receive ** from both payments, which is double protection when you retire.

Q4: Can middle-aged and elderly people who are unemployed or unemployed withdraw money by themselves? A:Yes. Self-employed persons over 55 years old, workers without a fixed employer, and freelance workers can go to the Labor Insurance Bureau to apply for voluntary withdrawals. They also enjoy tax savings and guaranteed benefits, and the monthly salary is based on the insured salary.

Q5: Will the loss of the labor retirement fund affect my principal? A: No. Even if the labor retirement fund loses money that year, your personal account will not be debited, and the principal will be fully retained. The state guarantees that the return will not be lower than that of a two-year time deposit, which is equivalent to providing a "downward guarantee."

Q6: When I receive it at the age of 60, should I receive it in one lump sum or monthly? A:You can choose. One-time payment = all principal and interest plus one payment; monthly payment = calculate the monthly payment amount by dividing the average remaining life by the total amount. It is generally recommended that if your pension is enough to live on, you can choose to receive it monthly to enjoy inflation protection; if you have a large plan (buying a house, starting a business), you can choose to receive it in one lump sum. You can go to the Labor Insurance Bureau website to try out which one is more beneficial to you.

Act now

It is recommended that you start doing one thing today: Open the Labor Insurance Bureau App to check the balance of your labor retirement account, actually see how much has been accumulated, and then decide whether to withdraw it yourself based on your financial situation. Just looking at the numbers will make you more motivated than you think.

If you decide to self-withdraw, when you have a salary interview with HR next time, just mention "I want to apply for self-withdrawal of 6%", and the setting can be completed in 30 seconds. The $2,400 you “take less” every month will become a sense of security in your retirement life in 30 years.

item.title: 2026 Annual Leave Guide for Taiwan: Eligibility, Calculation, Forfeiture Rules, and Salary Compensation
item.description: How many annual leave days do you get? Can your employer force you to forfeit them? This guide covers the Labor Standards Act formula, scheduling rights, unused leave compensation, and common employer violations Taiwan workers should know.
item.content:encoded:
Do you really understand how many days you have special leave?

Special leave (special leave) is a paid leave guaranteed by the Labor Standards Act, and it is also one of the benefits that office workers care most about. But many people are unclear about how many days of special leave they have. They don’t even know that if the special leave is not used up, the company must convert wages to you according to law. At the beginning of Q2, it is a good time to take stock of this year’s special leave quota and plan vacations. This article explains clearly the provisions of the Labor Standards Law on special leave at once, so that you can know where your rights are.

How to calculate the number of special leave days? Complete comparison table

According to Article 38 of the Labor Standards Act, the number of days of special leave is calculated based on your length of service under the “same employer”:

  • 6 months and less than 1 year: 3 days
  • 1 year but less than 2 years: 7 days
  • 2 years but less than 3 years: 10 days
  • From 3 years to 5 years: 14 days
  • From 5 years to 10 years: 15 days
  • Over 10 years: add 1 day for each additional year, up to a maximum of 30 days

For example: If you join the job on July 1, 2024, and your seniority has reached 1 year but less than 2 years by April 2026, your special leave for this period should be 7 days. If you are not sure how many months you have been employed, you can use a date calculator to calculate the exact number of days you have been employed.

What is the difference between the "annual system" and the "calendar system" of special leave?

There are two systems for granting special leave, which are very different:

Anniversary system is based on your arrival date, and you will get new special leave days every time you reach a certain number of years. For example, if you start work on March 15th, your special leave period is from March 15th of each year to March 14th of the following year. This is the original design of the Labor Standards Act, which is most beneficial to workers.

Calendar year system means that the company unifies the period of special leave from January 1st to December 31st, and converts the number of days according to your seniority ratio in that year. Many companies will adopt the calendar year system for administrative convenience, but the premise is that the rights and interests of workers cannot be harmed.

No matter which system the company uses, there is an iron rule: the converted number of special leave days cannot be less than the result of the annual system. If a company calculates fewer days using the calendar year system than the annual system, it is illegal. It is recommended that you count both at once to confirm whether the company has paid you less.

Special leave scheduling rights: Who has the final say?

Many people are confused about this and think that special leave requires the approval of the supervisor. Article 38, Paragraph 2 of the Labor Standards Law clearly stipulates that the arrangement of special leave is, in principle, decided by the "worker" himself. In other words, you basically have the final say on which day you want to take special leave.

However, the law also has a proviso: if the employer has urgent business needs, it can negotiate with the workers to make adjustments. But "negotiation" is not "rejection" - the company cannot unilaterally deny you a special leave, and can only discuss changing the time with you. If you encounter your boss who says, "There are not enough people that day, so you are not allowed to take special leave." He must provide specific reasons for the operation, and negotiate an alternative date that you agree with.

Common violations include: the company stipulates that special leave must be applied for one month in advance, supervisors have the right to veto applications for special leave, and it is completely prohibited to apply for special leave during peak seasons. If these provisions substantially deprive you of your special leave rights, it may violate the Labor Standards Act.

What should I do if my special vacation is not over? The company has to pay you

This may be the most important provision: at the end of the year or when the contract is terminated, if you still have unused special leave, the employer "should" convert it into wages and pay it to you. Note that the law uses "should", not "should" - which means that this is not optional and the company must provide it.

The calculation method for unvacated wages: Divide your "regular working hour wages" for the last month by 30, and then multiply by the number of unvacated days. Assume that your monthly salary is 40,000 yuan, and you have 3 days of special leave that you have not taken. Your untaken salary is 40,000 ÷ 30 × 3 = 4,000 yuan.

There are several common illegal practices that you should pay special attention to:

  • The company said "the special leave will be void if it is not completed" - it is illegal. Unless you don’t want to take the leave yourself and agree to defer it to the next year after negotiation, your salary will be converted into salary.
  • The company said "those who leave the company will not have unpaid wages" - it is illegal. Regardless of whether you resigned on your own or were laid off, the unused portion of the special leave must be calculated.
  • The company mixes special leave with sick leave and personal leave - it is illegal. Special leave is an independent type of leave and cannot be mixed.

5 common workplace traps when taking special leave

In practice, the following situations often occur in Taiwan’s workplace, and you should know how to deal with them:

**Trap 1: There is no special leave after less than one year on the job. **Since the Labor Standards Law was revised in 2017, employees will be entitled to 3 days of special leave after 6 months of age. If the company is still using the old rule of "only taking a special leave after one year of service", it is no longer legal.

**Trap 2: Scheduling special holidays requires supervisor approval. **As for the administrative process, it is okay for you to fill in a form to notify the company, but your supervisor cannot deny your special leave by saying "disapproval".

**Trap 3: At the end of the year, you are suddenly asked to use up your special holiday. **Some companies require employees to take compulsory leave at the end of the year in order to avoid paying unvacated wages. It would also be controversial if the arrangement was forced rather than negotiated.

**Trap 4: Special leave cannot be used during the notice of resignation. **The law does not provide this. You can still use special leave during the preview period.

**Trap 5: The probation period does not count towards seniority. **The Labor Standards Law does not have the concept of "probationary period". Your seniority starts from the first day you join the job.

What should I do if my rights and interests are infringed?

If you find that your company has a problem with its special leave practices, there are several ways to deal with it:

The first step is to report it to the company's human resources department. Sometimes the human resources system is set incorrectly or the supervisor does not understand the regulations, which can be solved through internal communication. It is recommended to communicate in writing (email or text messages via messaging software) and leave records.

In the second step, if the company does not handle the matter, it can submit an application for labor dispute mediation to the labor bureau of each county or city. Mediation is free, and your employer cannot take any adverse action against you during the mediation.

The third step is to report directly to the Labor Bureau. Employers who violate regulations related to special leave may be fined NT$20,000 to NT$1 million.

No matter which route you take, the most important thing is to preserve the evidence. Your attendance records, special leave application records, and the unpaid wages field on your payslip are all key supporting documents. It is recommended that you regularly organize these materials into PDF backups for emergencies.

FAQ

Can I take special leave in "hours"?

The Labor Standards Act stipulates that the minimum unit of special leave is "day", but if both parties agree, the leave can be taken in half-day or hourly units. In other words, if the company agrees, you can only take a half-day special leave. However, the company cannot force you to take time off in hourly units, thereby increasing the threshold for you to take time off.

Are contract workers or dispatch workers also entitled to special leave?

As long as you have a labor contract relationship with your employer, whether you are a full-time employee, a contract employee, or even part-time employee (hourly wage system), you have the right to take special leave. The difference is that the number of special days off for part-time work will be calculated on a pro-rata basis. The dispatch company is responsible for special leave for dispatched workers, and their seniority is also based on their seniority with the dispatch company.

Can the special leave be deferred to next year?

Yes, but only if both parties agree. Deferral is limited to one time, that is, it can be deferred to the next year at most. If the leave is still not taken after deferral, the employer must convert the untaken wages to you.

If I change jobs, can my seniority from the previous company be brought to the new company?

Generally speaking no. The seniority for special leave is based on the "same employer" and will be recalculated if the company changes. However, if a public institution is reorganized or transferred and you are retained by the new company, your original seniority should continue to be recognized.

The information in this article is based on the Labor Standards Act and relevant interpretations from the Ministry of Labor, and is updated as of April 2026.

Special leave is part of your job remuneration, not a favor from the company. Figure out how many days off you have, how to schedule them, and what to do if you don’t take all the time off. These are the basic skills to protect yourself. Take advantage of this month to take stock of this year's special leave quota, and take the leave you need with peace of mind.

item.title: Emergency Fund for Office Workers: A 6-Step Guide to Build From Zero on a NT$30K Salary
item.description: Sudden layoffs or family medical emergencies can devastate workers without an emergency fund. This guide walks you through building one from zero — how much to save, where to keep it, and concrete methods that even low-income earners can execute.
item.content:encoded:
Why is an emergency fund the first step in financial management?

Buy stocks, buy ETFs, learn investing - there are investment teachings everywhere in the financial management community, but few people tell you: before you start investing, you should have an emergency reserve fund. According to a survey by the Accountant General Office of the Executive Yuan, nearly 30% of households in Taiwan are unable to raise NT$100,000 for an emergency within a month. This means that once they encounter unemployment, serious injuries, or home appliances that break down and need to be replaced urgently, many people will be forced to borrow money or use credit cards to pay installments, falling into a cycle of debt. An emergency fund is not a tool to make you money, but a safety net to keep you from being overwhelmed when the unexpected happens.

How much should you save in emergency funds? Calculate it using your monthly expenses

Common advice is to save "three to six months' worth of living expenses," but this number varies from person to person. The key is not monthly salary, but "monthly fixed expenses." You can calculate it like this:

First list the money that must be spent every month: rent, food, transportation, mobile phone network fees, insurance premiums, loans (student loans, car loans), and other fixed payments. Add these up and you have your fixed monthly expenses.

Take a single office worker living in Taipei as an example: rent 10,000 + food expenses 8,000 + transportation expenses 2,000 + mobile phone network 700 + insurance 2,000 + student loan 3,000 + miscellaneous expenses 2,000 = monthly fixed expenses of approximately 27,700 yuan. Saving for 3 months is 83,100 yuan, saving for 6 months is 166,200 yuan.

How to decide whether to save for 3 months or 6 months? It depends on your level of risk:

  • 3 months: Suitable for people with stable income, qualified for labor insurance and unemployment benefits, and have family members who can provide temporary support
  • 6 months: Suitable for people who are freelance workers, have an irregular income, are the only source of income for their families, or whose industry has fluctuating economic conditions.

If you don’t have a bookkeeping habit yet, start it now. No need to make complicated forms, just spend a month recording all your expenses to figure out where your money is spent. Use your phone’s notepad or a simple spreadsheet.

The monthly salary is not high, how can you squeeze out money to save?

People with a monthly salary of over 30,000 yuan often say, "If you spend it all every month, how can you save any money?" However, the reserve fund does not need to be set up in one step. The key is to develop the habit of "fixed deposit", even if the amount is small.

**Method 1: Transfer out the salary immediately after it is credited. **The amount will be automatically transferred to the reserve account on the payday, starting from NT$2,000. Don’t wait until the end of the month to see “how much is left” before you save—usually there won’t be.

**Method 2: Cut off subscriptions that are insignificant. **Have you subscribed to Netflix, Disney+, Spotify, and YouTube Premium at the same time? Organize your subscription services and cut off the 1-2 that you use least frequently. You may save 200-400 yuan per month. It doesn't sound like much, it's 2,400-4,800 yuan a year.

**Method 3: Challenge the "No Spending Day". **Set yourself 1-2 days a week to spend no money at all (fixed expenses such as rent, transportation tickets, etc. do not count), bring lunch boxes, do not buy drinks, and do not shop online. The point of this exercise is not to save much, but to train your awareness of "consumption impulses".

**Method 4: Save all unexpected income. **Year-end bonus, three-section bonus, tax refund, money from winning invoices - these "extra income" are the easiest to spend and the best to save. Your life is not dependent on this money, and saving it will not affect your daily quality at all.

Where should the emergency fund be kept?

The core requirements for emergency funds are "safety" and "availability at any time", not the pursuit of high returns. So don’t use it to buy stocks, don’t use it to buy funds, and don’t use it to make any investment that carries the risk of loss. Suitable place for storage:

  • Digital bank high-interest living account: There are currently many digital accounts on the market that provide preferential interest rates, such as living interest rates of 1.5% to 2% or more (with an upper limit on the amount), which can be transferred and withdrawn at any time, which is the most recommended method
  • Time deposit (short term): If you don’t have enough self-control and are afraid of spending the money, you can consider a short-term time deposit of 1-3 months. If you cancel early, you will lose a little interest, but at least you won’t lose money.
  • Physical bank live deposit: Although the interest rate is low (usually less than 1%), the advantage is that it is simple and requires no operation

A practical approach: open a digital bank account that is “only in but not out” and is dedicated to depositing cash reserves. Don’t lump it in with your daily spending account, physical isolation can reduce the chances of you spending it casually. If you have multiple foreign currency accounts and need to manage interest rates, you can use the exchange rate conversion tool to track them at any time.

6-step action plan from scratch

If your reserve fund is zero now, follow this order:

**Step 1 (this week): Record your regular monthly expenses. **Pull out last month’s bank and credit card statements and list all your expenses.

**Step 2 (this week): Figure out your target amount. **Monthly fixed spending × 3 (conservative goal) or × 6 (safe goal), this is the number you want to save to.

**Step 3 (next week): Open a dedicated account. **Choose a digital bank to open an account specifically for depositing cash. Set up automatic transfer, and a fixed amount will be automatically transferred to your monthly payday.

**Step 4 (this month): Review your subscriptions and fixed expenses. **Cut those who can be cut, and drop those who can be lowered. All the money saved is transferred into the reserve account.

**Step 5 (ongoing): Make a fixed monthly deposit. **The amount does not need to be large, but it must be sustainable. A person with a monthly salary of RMB 30,000 can save a reserve fund of RMB 90,000 in about 2 and a half years if he saves RMB 3,000 per month.

**Step 6 (Quarterly Review): Verify progress. **Look at the balance in your reserve account every three months, use a countdown timer to set a target date for your deposit, and track progress to help maintain motivation.

How to make up for the reserve fund after it is used?

The reserve fund is just for use, and you should use it when there is an emergency. There is no need to feel guilty. But after using it, you should replace it as soon as possible:

If the amount used is not large (less than one month’s living expenses), increase the amount of monthly savings in the next 2-3 months to make up for it. If most of the reserve fund has been used, go back to "Step 5" and start accumulating again. Don't give up the entire plan just because it reaches zero.

In addition, after using the reserve fund, look back to see if the emergency could have been prevented. For example, if a home appliance breaks down, its life can be extended by regular maintenance; if you suddenly fall ill, you can spread the risk by strengthening insurance. Incorporating these precautions into your financial planning can reduce the frequency with which your reserve fund is used in the long term.

FAQ

What is the difference between an emergency fund and a “money saving goal”?

The reserve fund is your safety net to cover unplanned expenses (unemployment, medical emergencies, emergency repairs, etc.) and should not be used normally. "Saving goals" are consumption goals that you proactively plan (travel fund, car purchase fund, wedding fund, etc.). These two amounts should be kept in separate accounts and not mixed together.

If you have debt, should you pay it off first or save a reserve first?

If it is a credit card with recurring interest (annual interest rate above 15%), pay it off first. But at the same time maintain a reserve fund of at least 1 month of living expenses. If it is a student loan or housing loan with a low interest rate, you can repay it normally while slowly accumulating a reserve fund. When there is no reserve fund at all, any small accident may cause you to borrow money again, forming a vicious cycle.

After saving the target amount, can I start investing the extra money?

Can. After the reserve reaches the target, the excess can be used for other financial planning. But don’t touch the reserve fund itself, and don’t move the reserve fund to “level the cost” because of investment losses. The role of reserve funds is a fixed safety net, which is two different things from investing.

Will inflation make reserves less valuable?

Yes, but that's the price of a reserve - it sacrifices return for safety and liquidity. You can fine-tune the target amount each year based on price increases. For example, if inflation is 2% this year, your reserve fund target will also be adjusted upward by 2%. But don’t invest your reserve funds just because you are worried about inflation, otherwise it will lose its protective significance.

The information in this article is updated as of April 2026. The interest rates of each bank are subject to actual announcements.

You don’t need to wait until your monthly salary is 50,000 or 60,000 to start saving a reserve. Open your bank APP today and set up automatic transfers for next month—even if it’s only 2,000 yuan, it’s starting from scratch.

item.title: 2026 Taiwan Income Tax Prep Guide: 8 Steps for Office Workers to Save Time and Tax
item.description: May 2026 tax season is around the corner. Not started yet? This guide walks office workers through 8 things to do before filing — preparing documents, confirming deductions, estimating tax, and avoiding pitfalls — step by step.
item.content:encoded:
May tax season is counting down — are you ready?

May is filing season for Taiwan's individual income tax, and April is the prime time to prepare. According to the Ministry of Finance, more than 6 million households file each year — but plenty wait until the last minute, then either miss income, forget deductible items, or overpay by mistake. This guide walks you through everything you should sort out before the season opens. Information current as of May 2026.

Step 1: Confirm your filing status and login method

The first thing to figure out is your filing status. If you're single, an office worker, with no dependents, you file as an individual. If you're married, you and your spouse must file jointly — but you can choose joint tax calculation or separate tax calculation. Which one saves more tax depends on the income gap between you (the e-filing software auto-runs all three options).

The MOF's Individual Income Tax e-Filing and Tax Payment System has 6 login methods: ① Mobile-phone authentication (number must be in your own name) ② NHI card + registration password (needs a card reader) ③ Citizen Digital Certificate (downloads the most complete data) ④ Mobile Citizen Digital Certificate (fingerprint/face recognition) ⑤ Household registration number + lookup code (free printing at convenience stores) ⑥ Financial Certificate.

For most office workers, the Mobile Citizen Digital Certificate is the most convenient — set it up once and reuse it every year, no hardware required. Mobile-phone authentication is second-fastest (about 30 seconds). Before May, verify your Citizen Digital Certificate hasn't expired (it's valid for 5 years), and check whether your NHI card has been registered with a password on the NHIA website. ⚠️ The QR code on payment slips is a payment barcode (you scan it to pay tax by credit or debit card), not a login method — don't confuse the two.

Step 2: Download or look up your income data

Starting April 28, you can use the MOF's e-Filing system, with a Citizen Digital Certificate or NHI card, to pull last year's income data. The system lists your salary income, interest income, dividend income, rental income, and so on. But some income may not show up — for example:

  • Overseas income (foreign investments, overseas freelance work, foreign rental income).
  • Private transaction gains (property transactions other than car, house, or stock sales).
  • Part of your side-gig or freelance income (when the counterparty didn't file a withholding statement).
  • Side business income (Shopee stores, podcast ad revenue, sponsored content) — though from 2026 onward, many platforms have started reconciling data with the bureau.

Dig out last year's pay slips and bank statements and cross-check the system's data line by line. If you use the currency converter to handle foreign-currency income, don't forget to record the NT-dollar equivalents too.

Step 3: Take stock of your deductions — save what you can

Deductions are the lever that decides how much tax you pay. For tax year 2025 (filed in 2026), the standard deduction is NT$131,000 for singles and NT$262,000 for married couples filing jointly. But if your itemized deductions exceed the standard deduction, you should itemize. Common itemized items:

  • Insurance premiums: Up to NT$24,000 per person per year (personal life insurance); NHI premiums have no cap and are fully deductible.
  • Medical and maternity expenses: Registration fees, hospitalization, surgery, and similar costs — the portion not covered by insurance is deductible (only at NHI-contracted facilities).
  • Home mortgage interest (owner-occupied): Up to NT$300,000 per year.
  • Donations: Donations to the government or to educational, cultural, public-welfare, or charitable organizations — capped at 20% of your total gross income.

⚠️ Rental expense has moved from itemized to a "special deduction" (effective from tax year 2024), capped at NT$180,000 per household. If you rent, make sure to use the special-deduction path — covered in the next step.

Pull last year's insurance receipts, medical receipts, and rent transfer records now, and tally whether your itemized total beats the standard deduction.

Step 4: Don't forget the special deductions (2026 figures updated)

Beyond the general deductions, several special deductions are easy to overlook — and tax year 2025 (filed in 2026) brought major adjustments:

  • Special deduction for salaries and wages: NT$218,000 per person.
  • Special deduction for savings and investments: NT$270,000 per household — bank interest income tax-free up to this amount.
  • Special deduction for persons with disabilities: NT$218,000 per person.
  • Special deduction for tuition: NT$25,000 per dependent child enrolled in junior college or above.
  • Special Preschool Deduction (✅ new in tax year 2025): For children under age 6 — NT$150,000 for the first child, NT$225,000 per child from the second onward (wealth-exclusion clause removed).
  • Special deduction for long-term care (✅ new in tax year 2025): NT$180,000 per eligible disabled person (raised from NT$120,000, retroactive to January 1, 2025).
  • Special deduction for rental expense (✅ independent since tax year 2024): NT$180,000 per household for renters using the place as their primary residence.

⚠️ A lot of stale information is still circulating online (especially "NT$120,000 long-term care" and "NT$120,000 preschool"). Use the figures above — defer to the MOF's 2026 announcement as the final word.

One worth flagging: if you contribute 6% voluntarily to your Labor Pension, that amount comes out of your salary income before tax — no income tax owed. A worker earning NT$40,000 a month contributing 6% saves NT$2,400 a month, or NT$28,800 a year, tax-free. At a 5% tax rate, that's NT$1,440 saved; at 12%, NT$3,456.

Step 5: Estimate your tax bill and plan ahead

Rather than waiting for the system to calculate for you, run your own estimate first. The rough formula:

Net comprehensive income = total income − exemptions − deductions − special deductions

The 2025 personal exemption is NT$97,000 per person. Take a single office worker earning NT$45,000 a month: annual income runs about NT$540,000 (including a one-month year-end bonus). Subtract the NT$97,000 exemption, NT$131,000 standard deduction, and NT$218,000 special deduction for salaries — net comprehensive income lands around NT$94,000, falling in the 5% bracket, with tax due of about NT$4,700.

If your estimated tax bill is high, use the date calculator to count down to the June 1 payment deadline and line up cash in advance to avoid scrambling. Tax due over NT$30,000 can be paid in up to 3 installments, or by credit card in 0–12 installments (depending on the bank's offer).

Step 6: Check whether you're due a refund

Plenty of office workers don't realize they're actually owed money back. Common refund scenarios include:

  • The income tax your employer withheld each month exceeds what you actually owe (most common).
  • You had large medical expenses last year, dropping your tax owed after itemizing.
  • You had a gap in employment mid-year, so your actual annual income came in lower than projected.
  • You support direct ascendants aged 70 or older (their personal exemption doubles to NT$145,500).
  • You made large donations last year (e.g., stock or real estate donations).

Refunds typically land in your bank account in batches between late July and the following January. Filers who completed their online return error-free before May 10 land in Batch 1 (July 31); those who filed between May 11 and May 31 land in Batch 2 (October 31); supplemental-document and manual-review cases land no later than January 20.

Step 7: Filing timeline and things to watch

Mark these dates so you don't slip:

  • From April 28: Income and deduction data become available for lookup.
  • May 1 to May 31 (with June 1 grace extension): Individual income tax filing season.
  • Payment methods: Credit card (including 0–12 installment options), bank transfer, convenience store (for amounts under NT$20,000), ATM transfer, mobile-payment QR code.

A few common pitfalls:

  • In the first year of marriage, you can file separately or jointly (after that, joint filing only).
  • For dependents, confirm no one else has already claimed them — each person can only be claimed by one filer.
  • If you're renting and want to claim the rental special deduction, your landlord may push back — but you have the legal right to file it.
  • Scan and archive your donation, insurance, and medical receipts. The bureau may request supplemental documents.

Step 8: Avoid these 5 traps

Every year, the bureau publishes a ranking of common errors. The ones office workers fall into most often:

  • Under-reporting dividends or side income: Brokerage dividends, podcast ad revenue, Shopee stores, tutoring, royalties, YouTube ad revenue — the bureau reconciles data from various platforms.
  • Claiming rental expense without a complete contract or transfer record (it's a special deduction now, but supporting documents are still required).
  • Parents both claiming the same dependent, causing duplicate claims among siblings: Each dependent can only be claimed by one filer.
  • Ticking "spouse separate calculation" but messing up the math and overpaying: The e-filing software auto-runs the trial — just pick the lowest result.
  • Wrong account number for the refund: If the transfer fails, you have to re-apply, and the refund may be delayed by 1–2 months.

FAQ

Do I have to use a Citizen Digital Certificate to file?

No. Besides the Citizen Digital Certificate, you can log into the e-filing system using your NHI card (register a password on the NHIA website first), the Mobile Citizen Digital Certificate (TW FidO app), or mobile-phone authentication. Mobile-phone authentication is the simplest — you just need a mobile number registered in your own name, your NHI card number, and your ID number.

What's the income threshold below which I don't have to pay tax?

Based on the 2025 thresholds, a single office worker earning under NT$446,000 a year (NT$97,000 exemption + NT$131,000 standard deduction + NT$218,000 special deduction for salaries) basically owes no tax. But even if you don't owe tax, if your employer withheld income tax during the year, file anyway to claim the refund.

Will I be fined if I forget to file?

Under Article 110 of the Income Tax Act, an individual who has tax payable but fails to file faces a fine of up to 3× the under-reported tax, on top of paying the back tax. If you filed but under-reported, the fine is up to 2×. But if you voluntarily file and pay the make-up before any complaint or audit, Article 48-1 of the Tax Collection Act lets you avoid the penalty — you only owe interest. Late tax payment carries a 1% surcharge for every 3 days overdue, and the bureau will pursue forced collection after 30 days. ⚠️ Note: The "10% late-filing fee / 20% non-filing fee" cited in many popular articles applies to corporate income tax, not to individual income tax.

What's the most cost-effective way for couples to file?

Couples have three calculation options: combined taxation of all income, separate taxation of salary income, or separate taxation of all income types. As a rule of thumb, when there's a big salary gap between the two of you, separate taxation usually wins. The e-filing software auto-runs all three and you just pick the lowest result.

Do I have to report platform creator income (YouTube, podcasts, sponsored content)?

Yes. The MOF formally includes streamer and platform-creator income in the individual income tax for 2026. The guidance period runs until June 30, 2026 — during this window, voluntary make-up filings carry no penalty and no interest. If you earned YouTube, Twitch, Instagram, or TikTok ad revenue, sponsored content fees, or paid-subscription income in 2025, make sure to file during the guidance period.

Filing isn't scary — going in unprepared is. With a few weeks left before May, get your documents in order and your deductions tallied, and you can wrap the return in 20 minutes. For full filing-process details, see the 2026 Taiwan Income Tax Complete Guide; once your refund lands, the 2026 Tax Refund Money Management Guide breaks down the smartest ways to allocate it.

item.title: Your After-Work Side Hustle: Essential Free Online Tools for Freelancing
item.description: A practical guide to free online tools for freelancers and side hustlers — covering image optimization, document management, financial tracking, and time management to boost productivity at zero cost.
item.content:encoded:
Starting a new side income stream after get off work sounds tempting, but it often comes with new challenges. In addition to completing cases within a limited time, they also have to face various work processes - client communication, document management, financial calculations, file processing - each of which requires corresponding tools. And for those who are starting down the slash path, the subscription fees for tools are the first hidden expense.

I have encountered many pitfalls in the past few years when I have been taking on cases. At first, I foolishly paid for several software subscriptions, but later I discovered that many free online tools can solve most problems. Today I will share the free tools that have made my case-taking life much easier, and how to use them to reduce costs and improve efficiency.

Image batch processing: a daily savior for designers and community editors

If your side business involves visual content—whether it’s case design, community management, or handicraft seller—image processing should be a weekly routine. I often encounter this scenario: the customer requires 20 product images to be compressed and sent to him in a package, or materials of different proportions need to be converted into specific sizes and uploaded to various platforms.

In the past, I would use Photoshop one by one, which was time-consuming and labor-intensive. Later, I discovered that some free tools can batch compress, convert formats, and resize, which directly saves a lot of time. The "Picture Tool" on this site can process multiple photos at once, supports conversion between JPG, PNG, and WebP formats, and the quality will not be reduced too much after compression. I usually run through the pictures before sending them to clients or uploading them to the community.

The benefit of this tool is not only to save time, but also to help you improve your professionalism invisibly - customers receive the most optimized materials and the loading speed is fast, which invisibly improves the quality of your service.

Exchange rate conversion for freelancers: essential homework when taking on overseas cases

After working on the side for a while, you may start taking cases from overseas clients. I felt very excited at first, but then came a practical problem: How to convert the quotation into the local currency? The exchange rate changes every day, and you may lose a lot if you make a mistake.

item.title: Japan Solo Travel Guide: Essential Preparation and Practical Tools for Your Trip
item.description: A comprehensive guide to planning your Japan trip: from flight booking and currency exchange to itinerary planning and on-the-go tips including exchange rates, AI travel planning, and unit conversion.
item.content:encoded:
Traveling to Japan has become an annual itinerary for many Taiwanese people. Although traveling freely is comfortable, it also requires some preparation in advance so that you won’t be in a hurry when you arrive at the place. I have been to Japan no less than ten times. From the initial confusion to now being able to arrange things properly, I have accumulated a lot of practical experience. Today I’m going to share everything from pre-trip preparations, currency exchange strategies, itinerary planning, to how to deal with various small challenges you will encounter during the trip.

Preparation before traveling: Compare air tickets and accommodation together to find the most cost-effective combination

The first step is to book air tickets and accommodation, but don’t look at them separately, because sometimes the more expensive air tickets and cheaper accommodation can save the total cost.

When comparing air tickets, I usually check them on Skyscanner, Google Flights and the airline’s official website at the same time, because sometimes it’s cheaper to buy directly from the airline (especially when it comes to promotions from airlines like Cathay Pacific and JAL). It’s important to avoid peak times – times like Japan’s cherry blossom season (late March to mid-April) and Golden Week (late April to early May) can see flight prices double. If schedule flexibility allows, flights may be 30% to 50% cheaper by traveling a month in advance or pushing it back to the off-season.

In terms of accommodation, business hotels in Tokyo (such as Toyoko Inn and Daiwa Roynet) cost about NT$3,000 to NT$5,000 per night. The rooms are small but clean and convenient. Airbnb can be more cost-effective in Kyoto and Osaka, especially if you’re traveling with a group of people. But be aware that the cleaning fee of Airbnb in Japan is sometimes higher than the room price. Read the ratings and reviews before placing an order.

Currency exchange strategy: When is the most cost-effective time to exchange for Japanese yen?

This is where many people get into trouble. The cost of currency exchange may be higher than you think, and you may accidentally spend hundreds of Taiwan dollars more.

My strategy is: bring about half in cash and rely on credit cards and IC cards for the rest. Many places in Japan already accept credit cards, but there are still some small shops that only accept cash. IC cards (Suica or Pasmo) are very easy to use in Tokyo and Kansai. They can be used for taking rides or shopping at convenience stores without having to take out your wallet every time.

Bank exchange rates in Taiwan are usually better than those at the airport, so exchange most of your cash at the bank before departure. If you need Japanese yen temporarily when you arrive in Japan, you can withdraw money using an international Visa card at 7-Eleven ATM. The exchange rate is usually good (because the bank will use the business exchange rate of the day), and the handling fee is about 100 to 150 yuan.

Before departure, I will use the "Exchange Rate Conversion" tool on this site to check the latest Japanese yen exchange rate, so that I can estimate how much Japanese yen the Taiwan dollar in hand can be exchanged for. When checking out at a drug store, you can quickly estimate how much NT dollars you will actually have to pay - you don’t have to hold your computer for a long time.

Trip planning: Day arrangements and AI tools save you time

The itinerary planning for independent travel in Japan is a test of strategy. The geographical location, transportation time, and opening hours of attractions must all be considered. If you don't arrange it well, you may waste a lot of time moving around.

My experience is that if it’s 3 days, it’s recommended to stay in Tokyo only and don’t take the Shinkansen to Kansai; if it’s 5 days, you can add 3 days in Tokyo and 2 days in Kyoto or Osaka; if it’s 7 days, 3 days in Tokyo plus 2 days in Kyoto and 2 days in Osaka is the standard itinerary; for more than 10 days, you can add Hokkaido or the central region. Set aside at least a full day in each city so it doesn't turn into a marathon of sightseeing.

Planning your own itinerary is actually quite time-consuming, especially checking the location, transportation and business hours of each attraction. This site has a TripCraft AI travel planning tool that can automatically generate recommended itineraries based on your number of days, interests and budget, including attractions, restaurants and transportation routes. The time saved can be used to research must-eats or shopping lists.

Countdown and days calculation before departure

It sounds very basic, but many people don’t understand “how many days are left” and “how many annual leave days will be used up during the trip” before departure. If you leave on April 10th and come back on April 17th, how many days off do you need to take? Have you ever had consecutive days off during this period and can you take one less day off? If the calculation is wrong, it may be confused with the number of days of leave requested by the company.

The "Date Calculator" on this site can accurately calculate the number of travel days and working days. "Countdown Timer" allows you to set a countdown to the departure day - to remind yourself that it's time to pack your luggage, exchange currency, and confirm your hotel. I usually set a countdown immediately after booking my flight to make the anticipation of departure tangible.

Practical tips on the road: Temperature and unit conversion in one second

When arriving in Japan, there are some differences in life that require quick adaptation. The most common one is temperature judgment.

The first time I went to Tokyo, I saw the weather forecast said 5°C and I had no idea what to wear. I later learned that 5°C is about the temperature required to wear a thick sweater and a coat. At 10°C, a light jacket is enough, at 20°C, long sleeves are enough. But if you’re going to Hokkaido, where minus 10°C is the norm in winter, you’ll need a down jacket and a windproof jacket.

The "Unit Conversion" tool on this site supports common conversions such as temperature, weight, distance, etc. Especially when the suitcase is overweight, you need to quickly know how many kilograms equal how many pounds. It is fastest to directly use tools to convert.

I’d also like to share a little dressing tip: Japan’s indoor heating is very strong, so it’s best to adopt the “onion style” in winter—you can take off your coat when you enter a department store or restaurant, and put it on again when you come out. Much more practical than wearing a super thick piece of clothing.

After returning from travel: Don’t delay in organizing photos

During a week in Japan, you might accumulate 500 to 1,000 photos on your camera and phone. If you don't sort it out while your memory is clear after you come back, you will put it off until you don't want to touch it again.

The first step in photo organization is filtering and compression. If you just want to share on social media or create a travel photo album, compressing the photos can significantly reduce the file size while retaining sufficient quality. The "Picture Tool" on this site can compress photos or convert formats in batches (such as converting HEIC taken on iPhone to JPG). It is not a problem to process dozens of photos at a time. Backing up to the cloud or an external hard drive is much faster and saves more space.

My habit is to sort it out on the first weekend back, select the best photos, compress them and upload them to the photo album, and back up the rest of the original photos to an external hard drive. It’s true that the longer you put it off, the less you want to do it.

FAQ

**Q: Is it safe to go to Japan during typhoon season (September to October)? **

A: Typhoons are difficult to predict, but Japan has done a good job in disaster prevention. If the itinerary encounters a typhoon warning, some attractions and transportation will be temporarily adjusted. It is recommended to buy travel inconvenience insurance. Flight cancellation or attraction closure can at least reduce financial losses. Also pay close attention to the weather forecast beforehand.

**Q: How to calculate consumption tax and tax refund? **

A: Japan’s consumption tax is 10% (8% on food). The threshold for tax refund is 5,000 yen (price before tax included) spent in a single store in a single day, and it is easier to get a refund in department stores and large drugstores. Just show your passport when checking out and tell the clerk that you want a tax refund. There are two ways to get a tax refund: deduct the tax directly, or include the tax at checkout and apply for it at the airport before departure.

**Q: Should I buy Suica or Pasmo? **

A: Suica is used in Tokyo and Icoca is used in Kansai. The functions are almost the same. These IC cards can be used for rides, convenience stores and vending machines. If you only go to one city, just buy an IC card for that city. Currently, there are limited channels for purchasing physical cards. It is recommended to confirm whether the digital version of iPhone/Apple Watch is available before departure.

**Q: Is there a big difference in budget if I go alone with friends? **

A: The advantage of going alone is that the itinerary is flexible, but the disadvantage is that the average cost of accommodation is high. My experience is that the cost of going alone will be 20-30% more than if it is shared equally between two people. The main difference lies in the accommodation. But if three or more people share Airbnb, the cost will become very cost-effective. In terms of food, one can easily walk into a small restaurant with only a few seats. Sometimes that is the most authentic food.

Traveling independently in Japan is not as complicated as you think. The key is to do your homework beforehand. From air tickets, accommodation, currency exchange, itinerary planning, to various calculations and conversions during the trip, make good use of online tools to automate these chores, so that you can focus on what is really important - enjoying the journey, taking good photos, and tasting delicious food. I hope this sharing is helpful to you. See you on your next trip to Japan!

item.title: How to Write a Resume That Gets Noticed: A Complete Guide for Job Seekers
item.description: Submitted 30 resumes with no response? The problem might not be your skills. This guide covers structure, quantifying achievements, ATS optimization, formatting, and cover letters to help you stand out.
item.content:encoded:
Submitted 30 resumes, but received very few responses? Have you ever thought that the problem may not be your ability, but how to write your resume?

According to some HR reports, they spend an average of 6 seconds scanning a resume. This means that you have to catch their attention instantly to have a chance to advance to the interview stage. But what kind of resume can be seen? This article shares the pitfalls I have experienced and the techniques I have learned from the perspective of job seekers.

Basic structure of resume: not more is better, but clearer is better

Let me start with a misunderstanding: a resume is not a complete record of your life. Many people will write down every job and project since college, and the result is that their resume becomes a 3-4 page long essay. What is the effect of this? HR will skip faster.

A good resume should contain these parts:

Personal information: Name, contact number, Email, LinkedIn or personal website. This is the only way HR will contact you, so make sure this information is correct. I've heard of people filling in their phone numbers incorrectly and missing out on great opportunities.

Work experience: Arrange in reverse chronological order, with the most recent job first. Just write 3-5 key points for each job, no more. This is the core of the entire resume. I will explain how to write it in detail later.

Education: List highest education and related degrees. If you have been working for more than 5 years, the educational field can be simplified and there is no need to list high school.

Skills: List job-related skills, such as Excel, Adobe Suite, specific software, or language proficiency. Don't fill in function words like "interpersonal communication" and change it to specific tools and techniques.

Self-introduction or career summary: Optional, but if written well, can be the face of the entire resume.

The structure is like this, the focus is simple and clear. A good resume should be one page, at most one and a half pages. Don’t expect HR to read your life story carefully.

Quantitative results: "Improving performance" is not as good as "increasing 30% within half a year"

This is the most common mistake. When many people write resumes, they will use descriptions like this: "Responsible for marketing and promotion, with remarkable results", "Improved Facebook fan interaction", "Improved customer service process". It all sounds good, but the problem is: without specific numbers, there is no convincing.

When HR scans resumes, their eyes will automatically track the numbers. Because numbers are the most objective evidence. Try changing it to this:

"Through A/B testing and remarketing activities, the website conversion rate increased from 2.1% to 2.8% within half a year, adding 150,000 yuan in revenue to the company." "Implementing Instagram post strategy adjustments, the fan interaction rate increased by 45% within 3 months, and a single post reached a maximum of 8,000 people." "Optimized customer service SOP, shortening the average response time from 4 hours to 2.5 hours, and improving customer satisfaction to 4.6/5."

See the difference? Numbers make everything concrete and convincing. How to quantify the results? Ask yourself: How much revenue did this project increase or how much cost did it save? How many participants or data were touched? By what percentage did time efficiency improve? Not every result can be quantified, but 80% is fine. Taking the time to organize this data will greatly improve the competitiveness of your resume.

Via ATS system: Keywords are more important than literary talent

In 2026, most medium and large companies (especially technology, finance, and foreign companies) use ATS (Applicant Tracking System) to automatically screen resumes. Before HR can actually see your resume, you must first pass the ATS level. The working logic of ATS is to search for keywords in job descriptions. Only resumes that hit the keywords will be displayed to HR.

Practical practice: Before applying for a job vacancy, paste the job description in Word and circle 5-10 keywords (skills, tools, professional titles, industry words), and then check whether these words appear naturally in your resume. For example, if the job vacancy says "Familiar with GA4, SQL, A/B testing", it is not enough to use "website analysis" in your resume. You must clearly write the original words of "GA4", "SQL" and "A/B testing".

⚠️ Don’t stuff keywords at the end of the page or hide them in white fonts (modern ATS will detect cheating), and don’t stuff irrelevant keywords - if you really get into the interview, HR will break the news as soon as you ask.

Differences in resume emphasis for different positions

Marketing, administration, business, design - different positions, HR looks at resumes from different angles.

Marketing Position: HR will look at your campaign effectiveness, data analysis capabilities, and creative achievements. If you have done social marketing, you should list the fan growth rate and interaction rate; if you have done content marketing, you should explain the frequency of posting and traffic growth. Data is king.

Administrative Positions: Being organized, careful, and able to execute are key. Explain how you optimize processes, reduce error rates, and improve department collaboration. HR will look at your project management skills and cross-department communication record.

Business Position: Performance speaks for itself. List your sales, customer acquisition numbers, and customer retention rates. If there are large customers, you can list the customer size and cooperation period. Also mention your negotiating skills - how did you win this client?

Design Position: Portfolio is more important than words. But your resume still needs to explain what design tools you have used, what types of projects you have participated in (graphic design, UI/UX, visual marketing, etc.), and the commercial value brought by the design results. For example: "Redesign the product interface and reduce the churn rate of new users from 35% to 22%."

General principle: Emphasize the most important indicators for this position.

Avoid common landmines: add points to your resume, not take away points

Once you have written good content, don’t let it get ruined by these small details.

Long text, too much nonsense: "During this position, I proactively learned and applied various marketing tools, and worked with the team to achieve the company's marketing goals." This sentence can be changed to: "Using Google Analytics and HubSpot, in conjunction with SEO strategies, increased website traffic by 65%." Cut off the empty words such as "active" and "cooperate together" and go straight to the point.

Confusing typesetting, different font sizes: Use a consistent font (Arial or Microsoft Black), a consistent size (text 11-12pt), and a unified format. Don’t use 7 colors, 3 fonts – it just looks unprofessional.

Titles are vague or oversimplified: Don’t write “employee” or “staff.” Write "Marketing Planning", "Community Manager" and "Business Development Specialist". Job titles help HR quickly identify your role.

Never Update: Review your resume at least every six months. Make sure your latest work experience is at the top, and expired skills can be removed. An outdated resume will make HR doubt whether you are seriously looking for a job.

How to write an autobiography: Don’t start with “My name is XXX”

An autobiography is often the weakest link in a resume. Many people wrote: "My name is Wang Xiaoming. I am 28 years old and was born in Taipei. I am a diligent, serious and responsible person. I have loved marketing since I was a child..." This is a running account, not an autobiography. HR already knows your name and what you have done from your resume. What he wants to see is: Why you?

The golden formula of an autobiography: First, give a brief background (1 sentence): "I am a marketing planner with 5 years of marketing experience." Second, explain the career transition or core driving force (2-3 sentences): "After the first campaign in my previous company successfully increased sales by 300,000, I found that I am particularly passionate about data-driven marketing." Third, demonstrate core capabilities (2-3 sentences): "I am good at using GA to analyze user behavior and plan A/B Test and quickly adjust strategies based on data. In the past year, the number of followers of the social channel I am responsible for has increased by 120%." Fourth, explain why you want to join this company (1-2 sentences). Such an autobiography should be no longer than 150 words but clearly articulate your value proposition.

If you are not good at organizing text, you can try TWTools' [Resume Generator] (/resume/), which has an AI autobiography generation function - enter a few key information, and the tool will help you create a first draft, and then adjust it according to your own style. Of course, AI retouching is also supported to change blunt descriptions into more powerful expressions. 3 templates, 8 colors, one-click export to PDF after completion, neat and beautiful layout.

FAQ

Q: Should I write down all my work experience?

A: No need. If you have worked for more than 10 years, you only need to write down your work for the last 10 years. Earlier work can be omitted unless particularly relevant. Brevity is better than completeness.

Q: What format should I use to submit my resume?

A: Unless specifically requested by the company, please submit in PDF format. The layout of the PDF will not change depending on the computer environment of the other party, ensuring that the layout you put so much effort into is seen correctly. However, please note that when the ATS system parses the PDF, it may misread the contents of tables and columns, so the layout is mainly single-column text to avoid complex tables.

Q: Is it necessary to write an autobiography?

A: If the company does not specifically require an autobiography, the self-introduction block on the resume will suffice. But if there is an autobiography field, remember to take the time to write with quality. This is an opportunity to show your personal style.

There is no magic in writing a resume. The most effective way is simple: Speak out your results in numbers, use ATS keywords, format them clearly, create a page, and then adjust the focus according to the position before submitting. Your next job is out there, just show HR that you're worthy of an interview within 6 seconds.
