item.title: 6 Free AI Tools Every Office Worker Needs in 2026: Cut Overtime in Half
item.description: Can GPT-5.3, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Perplexity, Canva Magic Studio, Notta, and Gemini in Sheets really save time for office workers? We tested 6 free AI tools across common 2026 work scenarios.
item.content:encoded:
Is getting off work delayed again and again every day? 2026’s AI tools may be able to help

Taiwanese office workers work an average of 4.5 hours of overtime per week. Many people blame the heavy workload, but in fact a lot of time is eaten up by "repetitive work": writing emails, organizing information, making meeting minutes, searching for information... These tasks are not technically difficult, but they are very time-consuming.

2024-2026 is the turning point for generative AI from "toy" to "daily tool". The capabilities of the free version have caught up with the paid version 1-2 years ago; market differentiation also allows each tool to find its own sweet scene. This article actually tests the latest versions of 6 free AI tools in 2026 to see what tasks they can really help you save time and what pitfalls you should pay attention to.

1. ChatGPT free version (GPT-5.3): daily copywriting and first draft of emails

Purpose: writing emails, starting a case, drafting proposal copy, sorting out key points, and brief translation

OpenAI will upgrade the main model of the free version to GPT-5.3 in 2026. Free accounts can send up to 10 messages every 5 hours, and will automatically drop to the mini version after exceeding the limit. It is more than enough for daily needs such as "writing a business email" and "organizing the key points of the meeting into 5 points".

  • Example 1: Business email - 25 minutes to decide the wording → AI produces a first draft + you change 3 sentences = about 5 minutes
  • Example 2: Outline of the project - I want to list 5 angles in 45 minutes → Talk to AI and come up with 3 directions in 10 minutes + you choose one and then refine it
  • ** Pitfalls **: GPT-5.3 will still "make up stories confidently", and specific data (financial reports, news dates, names of people) must be verified by yourself. The free version cannot use Deep Research, Voice Mode advanced features and GPT-5.5 Thinking.

2. Claude Sonnet 4.6 Free Edition: Long Article Writing and Detailed Thinking

Purpose: long article editing, technical document reading, complex logical reasoning, Chinese writing with nuances

Anthropic's Claude is particularly delicate in Chinese writing, and Sonnet 4.6 is the strongest mid-range model in 2026. The free version has about 30 messages per day (there will be a queue during peak hours). Projects and Extended Thinking cannot be used, but it can handle most copywriting needs.

  • Example 1: Proofreading long articles - 5,000 words proposal, check sentence by sentence yourself 1.5 hours → Claude finds logical insecurities and redundant words + you only look at the marked points = 25 minutes
  • Example 2: Excel formula disassembly——I couldn’t understand the IFERROR + INDEX + MATCH nest written by my colleague, Claude disassembled it piece by piece + gave an alternative version with better readability
  • ** Pitfalls **: The free version has a context limit for a single conversation, and large files (> 100 pages of PDF) are processed into slices. Opening too many paging at the same time will hit the rate limit.

⚠️ Common Privacy Warning: Conversations between ChatGPT and the free version of Claude** will be used for model training** (can be turned off in settings). Don’t throw your customer list, employee salaries, and contract terms into the free version; if the company has an enterprise version authorization, use the enterprise version.

3. Perplexity free version: real-time news and industry information quick check

Purpose: Check the latest industry trends, competitor actions, market data, and standard citation sources

Perplexity is positioned as an "AI search engine". It connects to news RSS and the latest web pages, and can find market information for the second quarter of 2026 faster than information other than ChatGPT's "knowledge deadline". Especially useful for marketing, business, and analysts.

  • Example: "New tax regulations for individual sellers on Taiwan's e-commerce platforms in 2026" → A summary + 6 source links will appear in seconds; it will take you 5 pages to go through Google.
  • 2026 Free Edition Limitations: Unlimited basic searches, but Pro searches (in-depth research mode) are limited to 5 times per day and 3 file uploads per day. For severe research needs, it is recommended to upgrade to Pro ($20 USD/month).
  • Pitfall: Occasionally the dates of similar news are confused, be sure to check each reference link. There will still be errors in the recognition of proper nouns (especially Chinese names of people and places).

4. Canva Magic Studio: Quickly generate presentations, posters, and community diagrams

Purpose: Quickly make presentations, promotional posters, social copywriting and graphics, and brand material extensions

2024-2026 Canva integrates all AI functions into Magic Studio - including Magic Design (generate a complete briefing from one sentence), Magic Switch (convert the briefing into PDF/video/social graph), Magic Write (copywriting), Magic Eraser (eliminate memorization), etc. Free accounts can use most functions, but there is a monthly generation limit.

  • Example: 90 minutes to manually create a 12-page presentation (template selection, color change, image search, layout) → Magic Design generation + you fine-tune = 25 minutes
  • Pitfalls: The free version has limited library and color matching options. Clicking on some "Pro Elements" buttons will jump to the paid page. If it is for important clients or for external release, it is recommended to use Photoshop / Affinity to fine-tune the draft produced by Magic Studio.

5. Gemini in Google Sheets / Excel Copilot: formulas, pivot analysis, data organization

Purpose: Write VLOOKUP / INDEX-MATCH, find data logic, generate pivot analysis, and structure complex data

Google will fully open Gemini to free Gmail accounts in 2024 Q4. Gemini in Sheets can use natural language to describe requirements, and AI can automatically write formulas or suggest pivot analysis. Microsoft launched Copilot in Excel at the same time (the personal version requires a Microsoft 365 subscription to use, and the free version has more restrictions).

  • Example 1: "Classify these 2,000 customer data by region and calculate the revenue of each region" - 2 hours manually → AI formula writing + you check = 15 minutes
  • Example 2: "Find the products whose sales increased this month compared with the previous month" - AI directly generates conditional format + sorting formula
  • ** Pitfalls **: Sometimes the logic of AI-generated formulas is not rigorous enough, and complex multi-table associations still need to be checked by yourself; if sensitive data (employee salaries, customer information) are processed with a free Google account, privacy risks must be assessed.

6. Notta Chinese verbatim: meeting minutes save half the time

Purpose: Meeting recording → Chinese verbatim → AI summary and action items

⚠️ Important correction: Otter.ai, which was often recommended in the past, does not support Chinese - it can recognize "English with a Chinese accent", but the Chinese voice will be directly garbled. The correct choice for Taiwanese users is:

  • Notta (Chinese verbatim manuscript with high accuracy and maintained by Taiwanese team)
  • Whisper (OpenAI open source) + self-built (free but technical background required)
  • Tinrec, Miaoting Recording, iFlytek (local tools with the best Chinese experience)
  • Google Meet built-in verbatim script (supports Chinese starting from 2024, available with free Workspace account)

Implementation process (taking Notta as an example):

  • Example: Manually record a 1-hour meeting + 3 hours to complete the verbatim transcript afterwards → Notta automatic conversion + AI summary = 12 minutes
  • Pitfalls: The Chinese verbatim manuscript will still have errors in identifying proper nouns (company name, person name, product name), so you need to go through it quickly and proofread it; before recording the meeting, please inform the participants and ask for their consent, which complies with the personal information law.

How to make good use of AI without falling into pitfalls?

  • Always go over it: AI is a first draft assistant, not a final draft. All emails, plans, and materials should be checked by yourself.
  • Data must be verified: AI will make up stories and figures. Any specific content involving customers, financial reports, and regulations must be confirmed by yourself.
  • Privacy and Confidentiality: Don’t throw company secrets, employee privacy, and customer information into free AI tools. For sensitive content, please use the enterprise version (turn off training), local LLM, or de-identify it in advance.
  • Pick the right scenario: AI is most useful in "first draft generation", "information query" and "data sorting"; it is least useful in jobs that "require original ideas", "require in-depth knowledge of the industry" and "require building relationships".
  • You don’t need to learn all the tools at once: Start with the tasks you repeat the most every week, pick a corresponding tool and use it for 1-2 weeks, and then evaluate whether to continue using it.

2026 Workflow Combination Recommendations

Your role Main tool set
Business / Consulting Perplexity (rapid industry intelligence) + ChatGPT (email draft) + Notta (customer meeting recording)
Marketing Canva Magic Studio (visual) + Claude (long article) + Gemini in Sheets (data)
Engineering Claude (write code, debug) + ChatGPT (short query) + Perplexity (technical news)
HR / Administration ChatGPT (letters, forms) + Notta (interview verbatim) + Canva (internal training materials)
Entrepreneurship/Personal Career Use them all, but only use the free version for each one + only upgrade for severe needs to pay for one

7-day getting started plan for using AI tools for the first time

If you haven’t started using AI yet, jumping directly into watching video tutorials can easily lead to information overload. It is recommended to follow this order:

  • Day 1-2: Register for a free ChatGPT account and try "Help me translate this English email into Chinese" and "Write these 5 key points into a 200-word meeting summary" and other small tasks with specific input
  • Day 3-4: Try Perplexity, ask about "recent regulatory changes" and "new trends in a certain competitive product" in your work field, and observe whether the source of the citation is reliable.
  • Day 5-6: Pick a meeting recording (obtain the consent of the participants), use Notta to run the verbatim transcript + AI summary, and compare it with your manual recording
  • Day 7: Review this week's "What tasks did AI really save me time on?", continue to use those one or two, and leave the others for later.

⚠️The key to this project is not to "learn all the functions", but to find 1-2 usages that really suit your workflow**. The reason why most people fail to use AI is not because the tools are not good, but because they want to learn too much at once.

5 common cases of AI pitfalls (to avoid repeating the same mistakes)

  1. Throw the customer list directly into ChatGPT for sorting: The free version will be used for training, which is equivalent to leaking customer information. Modification: First use Excel to replace the customer name with Company A and Company B, and then replace it with the real name after AI processing.
  2. Directly copy market reports written by AI: AI will hallucinate (fabricate) market data and citation sources, and company decisions may be misjudged based on this. Revised method: After AI publishes the first draft, verify the source item by item, and put a question mark on any numbers that cannot be found.
  3. AI summary sent directly to supervisor after meeting: AI will miss key nuances (sarcasm, reserved remarks, unstated promises). Modification: Treat the AI ​​abstract as a "fill-in-the-blank draft" and go through it yourself to fill in the current atmosphere and implicit resolutions of the meeting.
  4. AI translation is sent directly to customers: Chinese-English translation often suffers from "over-literal translation" and "misuse of culturally sensitive words". Modified method: Give contextual hints to the target readers (United States/Japan/Europe). After reading, ask colleagues who can speak the language to take a look.
  5. Code written by AI is directly pasted into production: AI often uses outdated APIs, forgets error handling, and references non-existent packages. Modified method: Run locally + write unit test + Git diff to view line by line.

AI tools are not here to replace you, but to liberate you from "mechanical work" and give you time to think about more important things. Starting next week, pick a tool to handle the tasks you repeat most every week and see how much time you save after a month.

item.title: 2026 Tax Filing: Education, Tuition, and Tutoring Deductions Plus New Brackets to Save NT$20,000
item.description: 2026 tax filing has major changes: exemption raised to NT$97K, long-term care to NT$180K, preschool deduction NT$150K/$225K. This guide covers all education-related deductions plus dual-income household scenarios.
item.content:encoded:
In May tax season, you may have left education deductions on the table

Plenty of office workers spend tens of thousands of NT dollars a year on their kids' education (tuition, tutoring, talent classes, and more), but they don't know how much of it qualifies as a deduction at tax time. Some deductions the government never proactively flags — you only cut your tax bill if you claim them yourself. The 2026 filing season (reporting tax year 2025 income) introduces several new rules, so if you have children's education expenses, read this carefully.

2026 filing basics — start here

Tax season runs May 1 to May 31, 2026. Major changes this year (reporting tax year 2025 income):

Item Tax Year 2024 (2025 filing) Tax Year 2025 (2026 filing) Change
General personal exemption NT$92,000 NT$97,000 +NT$5,000
Personal exemption (age 70+) NT$138,000 NT$145,500 +NT$7,500
Standard deduction (single) NT$124,000 NT$131,000 +NT$7,000
Standard deduction (married joint) NT$248,000 NT$262,000 +NT$14,000
Special deduction for salaries NT$218,000 NT$227,000 +NT$9,000
Special deduction for long-term care NT$120,000 NT$180,000 +NT$60,000 (50% jump)
Preschool (1st child) NT$150,000 NT$150,000 Unchanged
Preschool (2nd child and beyond) NT$225,000 NT$225,000 Unchanged
Basic living allowance (per person) NT$202,000 NT$213,000 +NT$11,000

Two items that matter most to middle-class families: the long-term care special deduction jumps from NT$120,000 to NT$180,000 (saves NT$7,200 for someone earning over NT$80,000 monthly in the 12% bracket), and the basic living allowance hits NT$213,000 — which shifts the "minimum standard of living" threshold.

2026 individual income tax brackets and rates

Net Comprehensive Income Tax Rate
NT$0 – 590,000 5%
NT$590,000 – 1,330,000 12%
NT$1,330,000 – 2,660,000 20%
NT$2,660,000 – 4,980,000 30%
Over NT$4,980,000 40%

Knowing your bracket lets you calculate how much each extra NT$10,000 of deductions saves. For example, in the 12% bracket every NT$10,000 of deductions saves NT$1,200; in the 20% bracket, NT$2,000.

Education-related deductions

1. Special deduction for children's tuition (most common)

If you support a child enrolled at a junior college or above recognized in Taiwan, you can deduct NT$25,000 of tuition per child per year (tuition must have been paid within the tax year or paid in installments).

  • Eligibility: Children enrolled at MOE-recognized junior colleges and above (universities, technical colleges, 4-year technical institutes), domestic or overseas.
  • Amount: Cap of NT$25,000 per child per year.
  • Multiple children: Three kids in college → deduct NT$25,000 each, NT$75,000 total.
  • Not eligible: Open University, Open Junior College, the first 3 years of 5-year junior colleges (years 1–3), language schools.
  • Common gaps: Dorm fees and book fees typically aren't deductible — only "tuition + miscellaneous fees." Check whether your payment receipt reads "tuition" or "accommodation."

2. Special Preschool Deduction (substantially raised in 2026)

The tax year 2025 rules raised the deduction significantly and removed the wealth-exclusion clause (previously, taxpayers in the 20% bracket and above couldn't use it; now all brackets qualify):

  • 1st child: NT$150,000 per year (raised from NT$120,000).
  • 2nd child and beyond: NT$225,000 per year (unchanged at NT$225,000).
  • Eligibility: Children under age 6 (raised from under age 5).
  • Applies to: Children enrolled in licensed kindergartens, daycare centers, or registered nanny care.

⚠️ Common confusion: Many old articles cite "NT$12,000 + children under age 5" — that's the 2024 rules and no longer applies to 2026 filing. If you see a guide quoting NT$12,000 for 2026, skip it.

3. Children's education expenses (private junior high and below)

Tuition for private junior high school or private senior high school (vocational schools excluded) gets you a small additional deduction when claiming the child as a dependent. The mechanism isn't a "direct deduction" — instead, you flag it when listing dependents and the tax authority calculates the savings.

  • No deduction for public schools: Government-subsidized public middle and high schools don't get an extra deduction.
  • Civil servants' education subsidy for children: If you're a civil servant, this amount is subsidized directly by the government, so you don't claim it again at tax time.

4. Tutoring and talent classes? Usually no — but there are exceptions

General tutoring schools and music, art, or sports talent classes typically can't be deducted on the individual income tax return. Two exceptions:

  • Long-term care "home-care course fees": If you take a government-approved care-training course (the long-term care special deduction rises to NT$180,000 in 2026), the fee qualifies.
  • Lifelong learning courses (subsidized in some regions): A few counties offer "active senior learning" or "senior continuing education" subsidies, but those are direct subsidies, not tax deductions.

Worked examples for dual-income families (2026 rules)

Example A: Dual-income, Spouse A supports two parents, Spouse B supports 2 children

Spouse A (NT$60,000 monthly, NT$720,000 annual):

  • General personal exemption: NT$97,000 (self)
  • Supporting father: NT$97,000
  • Supporting 80-year-old mother: NT$145,500
  • Standard deduction (couple): NT$262,000 (shared by both spouses)
  • Special salary deduction: NT$227,000

Spouse B (NT$50,000 monthly, NT$600,000 annual):

  • General personal exemption: NT$97,000
  • Supporting Child A (college student): NT$97,000 + tuition NT$25,000
  • Supporting Child B (age 4): NT$97,000 + Preschool Deduction NT$150,000 (1st child)
  • Special salary deduction: NT$227,000

Total household deductions: 9.7×4 + 14.55 + 26.2 + 22.7×2 + 2.5 + 15 = NT$1,484,500

Total household annual income NT$1,320,000 − total deductions NT$1,484,500 = negative, no tax owed (basic living allowance NT$213,000 × 4 = NT$852,000 is already covered).

Example B: Single-income family, 2 children at different education levels

Primary earner (NT$80,000 monthly, NT$960,000 annual):

  • General personal exemption: NT$97,000 (self)
  • Supporting spouse: NT$97,000
  • Supporting Child A (college student): NT$97,000 + tuition NT$25,000
  • Supporting Child B (age 5): NT$97,000 + Preschool Deduction NT$150,000 (1st child)
  • Standard deduction (couple): NT$262,000
  • Special salary deduction: NT$227,000

Total deductions: 9.7×4 + 26.2 + 22.7 + 2.5 + 15 = NT$1,052,000

Net taxable amount: 96 − 105.2 = −NT$92,000 (tax owed: 0).

Adding the NT$180,000 long-term care special deduction (if the spouse is caring for an elder) drops the tax base even further — the new NT$180,000 long-term care provision really pays off here.

How much tax can you actually save in a year?

Suppose you earn NT$60,000 a month (NT$720,000 a year), supporting 1 college student and 1 toddler (age 5). Without claiming these deductions, you'd land in the 12% bracket:

Deduction Amount Tax Saved at 12%
Child's tuition NT$25,000 NT$3,000
Preschool (1st child) NT$150,000 NT$18,000
Long-term care special deduction (spouse caring for elder) NT$180,000 NT$21,600
Total annual savings NT$355,000 NT$42,600

For a family earning NT$60,000 a month, claiming the right education and long-term care deductions saves over NT$40,000 a year — roughly an extra month of disposable income.

How to make sure you don't miss these deductions

1. Prepare complete proof of payment

  • University: Tuition invoice, payment receipt (attach to the tax return when submitted for audit).
  • Kindergarten / nanny: Monthly payment receipts or annual invoices (keep originals or copies through the May filing).
  • Long-term care course: Course receipt + the host organization's registration certificate.

2. Check the right boxes when filing online

In the MOF's e-filing system, go to "Basic Information" → "Dependents" and verify each child's fields:

  • Check "tuition" + amount (university).
  • Check "preschool" + amount (under age 6).
  • Check "long-term care" (if there's someone needing care).

3. Pick one of the multi-factor authentication methods

The 2026 e-filing system has 6 login methods: mobile-phone authentication / NHI card + registration password / Citizen Digital Certificate / Mobile Citizen Digital Certificate / household registration number + lookup code / Financial Certificate. Mobile-phone authentication is the easiest — login in about 1 minute.

4. Visit the tax office in person

If you're uneasy about the online system, bring all your receipts and ID to the local tax office and file at the counter. Staff will help you check whether you've missed any deductions.

5. Watch the timing

Some deductions require the expense to be "paid within the tax year" — for example, tuition must be paid between January and December 2025 to qualify for the May 2026 filing. Prepaid or deferred fees may fall in different tax years.

FAQ

Q1: How does the "NT$225,000 from the 2nd child onward" preschool deduction work? A: Every 2nd, 3rd, and subsequent child (under age 6) in the family deducts NT$225,000. 1st child NT$150,000 + 2nd child NT$225,000 + 3rd child NT$225,000 = NT$600,000. Families with 3 young children see major tax savings.

Q2: My child is a college freshman who enrolled in September 2025. Can the tuition be deducted in the May 2026 filing? A: Yes. Tuition paid in the second half of 2025 falls under "tax year 2025" and gets claimed in the May 2026 filing. But the next-semester tuition you'll pay in February 2026 belongs to "tax year 2026" and can only be deducted in the May 2027 filing.

Q3: How do I sequence deductions for maximum savings? A: Pick standard or itemized — you can't use both. For most families, the standard deduction (NT$262,000 for a couple) is the easier path, unless your large medical bills, donations, and home mortgage interest exceed NT$262,000. Special deductions (education, preschool, long-term care) stack on top of either standard or itemized.

Q4: Single and childless — what should I watch for in 2026 filing? A: ① The standard deduction rises to NT$131,000, ② the special salary deduction rises to NT$227,000, ③ the basic living allowance is NT$213,000 — the combined tax-exempt threshold goes up by about NT$23,000. Workers earning under NT$40,000 a month basically owe no tax.

Filing in May isn't just an "obligation" — it's an annual chance to cut your tax bill legally. Families with kids in school plus elderly relatives who need care should especially comb through every available deduction. Before the May 31 deadline, gather every supporting document so nothing slips through.

2026 will be the year when subscription inflation explodes. Netflix will increase the standard plan from NT$330 to NT$380 in November 2024. The annual fee of Microsoft 365 Personal Edition will increase from NT$2,190 to NT$3,090 (a 41% increase). YouTube Premium, Spotify, and Apple Music will also increase their prices one after another. For office workers in Taiwan, "The service I ordered has increased again" has become news that they hear almost every quarter.

Surveys show that the average Taiwanese office worker pays 6-8 subscriptions a month, which often adds up to more than NT$2,000. However, more than 30% of the subscriptions are actually unused. These "sleep subscriptions" unknowingly become your fixed monthly expenses, which may cost you an extra NT$10,000-20,000 in a year. The most annoying thing is that the money is scattered among various credit card accounts and telecommunications bills, making it difficult to see the total amount at a glance.

2026 Subscription Inflationary Environment: The Numbers You Need to Know

Before you start sorting out your subscriptions, first take a look at the official monthly fees for Taiwan’s mainstream subscription services in 2026. This comparison table will be the basis for your next decision.

Services Individual Plan Family/Couple Plan Student Plan Remarks
Netflix Basic/Standard/Premium 290 / 380 / 460 (Multiple devices included) — 2024-11 Price increase
Spotify Premium 168 Couple 228 / Family 298 88 Family maximum 6 people, address verification required
Apple Music 165 Family 265 90 Family up to 6 people
YouTube Premium(Android/Web) 199 Home 399 119 iOS increased to 260 due to commission
Disney+ Monthly 285 / Year 2,790 Premium Monthly 335 / Year 3,280 — Premium support 4K + HDR + 4 devices
Microsoft 365 Personal/Family 3,090/year 4,190/year (6 people) — 2024-11 Big jump with Copilot
iCloud+ 50 GB / 200 GB / 2 TB 30 / 90 / 300 (home sharing included) — Family sharing available from 200 GB

⚠️ Note: iOS in-app purchases will be subject to 30% Apple tax, so subscribing to YouTube Premium from iPhone will cost NT$ 60 more than from computer or Android. It is recommended that all subscriptions that support multiple platforms be ordered from a computer or Android, and then used to log in with an iPhone.

Step 1: Take a complete inventory of your subscriptions

Open your credit card and cell phone bills and find any recurring charges. The most easily missed thing is "telecom bill collection" - Chunghwa Telecom, Taiwan Telecom, and Far EasTone will include Netflix and Disney+ in their monthly bills, and users often forget to include them.

Organize the list according to the following categories:

  • Streaming Entertainment: Netflix, Disney+, Apple TV+, Hami Video, myVideo
  • Music: Spotify, Apple Music, KKBOX, YouTube Music
  • Cloud Storage: iCloud+, Google One, OneDrive, Dropbox
  • Productivity Tools: Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Notion Plus, Adobe Creative Cloud
  • AI Tools: ChatGPT Plus, Claude Pro, Perplexity Pro, Gemini Advanced
  • Sports and Fitness: Gym monthly membership, yoga app (Down Dog, Nike Training Club Pro), sports watch subscription
  • VPN / Security: NordVPN, ExpressVPN, anti-virus software
  • Others: Switch Online, PS Plus, e-books (Kindle Unlimited, Hami Bookstore), online courses

Many people will be surprised to find that "I actually have 12 subscriptions" - 5 of them may not remember buying them at all, or they forgot to cancel after subscribing for a certain event.

Step 2: Evaluate the "actual usage" of each subscription

Ask yourself four questions for every subscription:

  1. How many times have you opened it in the past 30 days? (not "how many times do you want to use it", but how many times have you actually opened it)
  2. If canceled, will it really affect daily life?
  3. Are there any cheaper alternatives (free version, family plan, annual subscription discount)?
  4. Can you share it with family/friends to reduce costs?

Here are a few real cases in 2026:

  • NETFLIX STANDARD PLAN NT$ 380: Worth it if you watch it ≥ 3 times a week; if you don’t watch it 5 times a month, you can switch to YouTube free content or merge it into a family account (only if you have the same address)
  • Microsoft 365 personal NT$ 3,090/year: If you only use Word + Excel, the free Google Docs/Sheets are enough; if the whole family needs Office + 1 TB cloud, change to the home version NT$ 4,190/year. Shared by 6 people, the per capita NT$ 698/year is far more cost-effective than the personal version
  • Apple Music personal NT$ 165: Family plan can be changed to NT$ 265 / 6 people = NT$ 44 per person, much lower than the personal version
  • YouTube Premium individual NT$ 199: Those who watch ads heavily + listen to videos in the background (no ads) + YouTube Music all-in-one is worth it. Light users can also block ads with Brave browser + Adblock (but mobile devices are limited)

Step 3: Execute the "Subscription Cooling-off Period"

If a subscription has not been used for more than 30 days, just cancel it and try it. Most services will retain your account and settings for 90-180 days. If you want to resubscribe in the future, you only need to click twice, but this 30-day "vacuum period" will let you see whether you really need it.

Implementation steps:

  1. Mark the next deduction date for each subscription on your mobile calendar
  2. Remind yourself 3 days before the deduction date to check whether you have actually used it this month.
  3. Cancel unused items instead of "trying for another month" (self-deception will extend to the third or fourth month)
  4. Look back 30 days after canceling and ask yourself, "Did I miss it?" If not, then cancel permanently.

Step 4: Divide the family plan between people - the real amount of money saved

Some subscriptions support family plans, but require same address verification (Spotify will start checking in 2023, Netflix will follow up in 2024). If you share it with family members or people living with you (roommates, partners), the actual monthly fee per person can be reduced to 1/3 to 1/6 of the original price:

Services Personal version Family plan 6 people/4 people sharing equally Savings per person per month
Spotify 168 298 50 (6 people) 118
Apple Music 165 265 44 (6 people) 121
YouTube Premium(Android) 199 399 67(6 people) 132
Microsoft 365 3,090/year 4,190/year 698/year (6 people) 199/month
iCloud+ 200 GB 90 90 22.5 (4 people) 67.5

⚠️ The family plan is not just about "finding friends" - the service provider will use the IP address, geographical location, and Wi-Fi name to determine whether you live together. Netflix has begun charging "additional account fees" (additional account NT$ 100/month) to cross-address users. The safest family plan participants are family members or roommates who actually live with them.

Step 5: Regular review (once every quarter)

Don’t think that “check it once and you’re done.” Three months later, you may have subscribed to a new service (seeing a limited-time offer), or you may have forgotten that a certain annual subscription is about to expire. It is recommended to set aside 15 minutes every quarter (3 months):

  • Reopen credit card bill + telecom bill
  • Compare the list to see if there are any "unrecorded deductions"
  • Annual subscription that is about to expire - decide whether to renew, set a reminder 3 days before expiration
  • Check out which services will increase in price in 2026, and evaluate whether it’s time to downgrade or cancel your subscription

Example: Xiao Li 2026 sorting and subscribing before and after comparison

Monthly expenses before consolidation:

  • Netflix Standard 380 + Spotify Personal 168 + iCloud+ 200 GB 90 + Microsoft 365 Personal 258 (3,090÷12) + YouTube Premium Personal 199 + Notion Plus About 320 (USD $10 × 32) + Online Courses 500 + Gym 1,500 = Monthly Fee NT$ 3,415

After review:

  • Netflix changed to share an account with my sister (same address) → split half of 190
  • Spotify changes to the family plan for 6 people (the whole family listens) → 50
  • iCloud+ changed to Family Sharing 200 GB → 22.5
  • Microsoft 365 home version 4,190/year ÷ 6 people ÷ 12 months → 58
  • YouTube Premium to Family Plan Android → 67
  • Notion Plus Cancel (free version is enough for personal use) → 0
  • Online courses do not require annual subscription, but can be purchased individually as needed → average 150
  • Switch gym to YouTube Fitness + Monthly Voucher → 500
  • Monthly fee is NT$1,037, monthly saving is NT$2,378, annual saving is NT$28,536

The key is not to cut off all subscriptions, but to make every money correspond to real use value. For Xiao Li, the extra NT$ 28,536 each year can be converted into an emergency reserve fund, an annual travel fund, or start a regular fixed investment of 0050.

Subscribe to long-term strategies in the age of inflation

2024-2026 subscription inflation tells us: “Affordable now” does not equal “affordable next year”. Each service may increase its price by 10-40% in any given November without warning. Long-term coping strategies:

  1. Single service monthly fee upper limit: Set personal standards (for example, "a single subscription shall not exceed 0.5% of monthly salary"). Exceeding the upper limit triggers review
  2. Thoughts on Subscription Annuity: Calculate the monthly fee × 12 as the annual fee. Seeing "Spotify 2,016 yuan a year" will be more realistic than "168 yuan a month"
  3. Awareness of Substitutes: If Spotify increases, try KKBOX and Apple Music; if Netflix increases, try Disney+; no subscription is "irreplaceable"
  4. Family plan priority: all services that can be divided into people are in the family plan, and only services without individual options are left in the individual plan

Unsubscription tutorial for mainstream subscription services

The real reason why many people don’t unsubscribe is that “they can’t find the cancel button”—the service provider will deliberately hide the process deeper. The following is a summary of the cancellation paths for mainstream subscriptions in 2026:

Services Cancel path Notes
Netflix Account → Account Settings → Cancel membership Cancellation can still be used until the end of the current period
Spotify Account → Subscription plan → Cancel Premium Return to the free version and still log in to listen
YouTube Premium YouTube Settings → Purchases & Memberships → Manage iOS Uninstalled from App Store instead of YouTube App
Apple Music / iCloud+ Settings → Apple ID → Subscriptions → Cancel Subscription All Apple subscriptions are here
Microsoft 365 account.microsoft.com → Services & Subscriptions → Manage Turn off "Auto-Renew" first
Disney+ Account → Subscription plan → Cancel subscription Telecom collection must be canceled from the telecom provider page
Telecom collection (China / Taiwan / Far EasTone) Management of various telecom mobile phone numbers → Value-added services → Cancellation Cancellation from the original platform may be invalid

⚠️ Telecom Collection Trap: Many people fail to cancel from the Netflix App because the subscription is tied to the Chunghwa Telecom bill - you must return to the Chunghwa Telecom website to cancel it. Confirmation method: Check which company paid last month's bill.

Added "48-hour cool-down list" before subscribing

Many subscriptions are added impulsively (seeing limited time offers, recommendations from friends, or a certain need). It is recommended to create a "48-hour cool-down list":

  1. When you see a service you want to subscribe to, write it down first. Don’t subscribe immediately
  2. Reassess after 48 hours:
    • How many times have I thought about it in the past 48 hours?
    • Are there any existing subscriptions that already meet the same needs?
    • Is the monthly fee × 12 annual fee worth it?
    • Do I estimate it will last 3 months or 12 months?
  3. Still want to subscribe → subscribe; didn’t expect it → don’t subscribe

This 48-hour delay can block 60-70% of impulse subscriptions.

Get started: Open your credit card statement, spend 15 minutes listing all your subscriptions, and ask yourself, "Am I really using this?" The money you save in a year can be enough to buy a new phone, save for a travel fund, or get an annual health checkup.

item.title: 2026 Taiwan Labor Reforms: Minimum Wage NT$29,500, Daily Parental Leave, NT$100K Maternity Subsidy, Hourly Family Care Leave
item.description: Starting January 1, 2026, multiple Taiwan labor benefits take effect: minimum wage raised to NT$29,500/month (NT$196/hour), parental leave can be applied per day, NT$100K maternity subsidy per birth, and family care leave is now hourly. This guide covers the legal basis, eligibility, and how to apply.
item.content:encoded:
Starting from January 1, 2026, Taiwan's new labor system will have four major changes: an increase in the minimum wage, detachable days off for child care, a maternity subsidy totaling NT$100,000 per child, and family care leave switched to "hourly" leave. Each item directly affects office workers' salary, family planning and leave flexibility. This article compiles the legal basis, scope of application, application notice period, twin overweight guarantee and other practical details of the four new systems, so that you not only know "there is", but also "how to use".

1. A quick overview of the new labor system in 2026

New project Main changes Implementation date Source of law
Minimum wage increase Monthly salary 28,590 → 29,500 yuan; hourly wage 190 → 196 yuan 2026-01-01 "Minimum Wage Law"
Child care stay is removable and can be applied for on a single day before each child turns 3 years old, with a maximum of 30 days per child 2026-01-01 Article 16 of the "Gender Equality Work Act"
Maternity subsidy 100,000 per child Original social insurance maternity benefit + government supplementary difference = 100,000 2026-01-01 Post-birth Key points of labor maternity subsidy
Application for changing the hours of family care leave 7 days a year = 56 hours, application for split hours 2026-01-01 Article 20 of the "Gender Equality Work Act"

The minimum wage has been raised for ten consecutive years, parental leave is allowed in "days" for the first time, maternity benefits starting at NT$100,000, and family care leave that can be split into "hours" - these four together are the most comprehensive wave of labor law reforms since 2024. Let’s break it down item by item below.

2. The minimum wage is raised to 29,500 yuan (hourly wage 196 yuan)

Adjust content

  • Monthly minimum wage: 28,590 → 29,500 yuan (up 910 yuan, 3.18% increase)
  • Hourly minimum wage: 190 → 196 yuan (up 6 yuan, 3.16% increase)
  • Estimated number of beneficiaries: approximately 2 million workers
  • Announcement Date: 2025-09-04 (Resolution of the Minimum Wage Review Committee of the Ministry of Labor)
  • Implementation date: 2026-01-01 from New Year's Day

This is the second adjustment to the Minimum Wage Law since it was enacted, and it is also the tenth consecutive year that the basic wage has been raised**.

It’s related to your salary

  • Monthly salary earners: The original monthly salary is less than 29,500 yuan. The employer must make up the amount to 29,500 yuan starting from 2026-01-01. Otherwise, it violates Article 79 of the Minimum Wage Law and may be fined up to 1 million yuan.
  • Hourly wage earners: If the original hourly wage is less than 196 yuan (some service industries, work-study students), employers must also make up the amount.
  • Not only the "lower class" will benefit: the Labor Insurance Salary Grading Table and Labor Retirement Contribution Wages linked to the minimum wage will also automatically increase. The monthly labor and health insurance premiums may slightly increase by NT$10-30, but the employer's labor pension contributions will also increase (the annual cumulative difference is about NT$1,000-2,000).

3. The “day” application for childcare stay can be removed (Amendment to Article 16 of the Gender Equality Work Act)

Differences between past and present

  • Old system (before 2025): Childcare leave without pay requires at least 1 month, and the whole month is calculated
  • New system (starting from 2026-01-01): Before each child reaches the age of 3, he or she can apply for a child care stay in day units, a single period shall not exceed 30 days, and the overall period can still be combined to a maximum of 2 years

How to separate the parents for a total of 60 days

Each parent can apply for a maximum of 30 days in "day" units (converted to a total maximum of 60 days for both parents). For example:

  • Mom asked in installments 5+10+15 = 30 days ✅
  • Dad, please give me another 20 days of relay ✅ (total 50 days)
  • There are still 10 days left to use flexibly

You can still receive the 80% salary subsidy after demolishing the sky.

Starting from 2026-01-01, childcare stay allowance and salary subsidy will be paid on a proportional basis, and the original rule of "less than 1 month will be counted as 1 month" will be cancelled. It means: If you ask for 5 days, you will get 5 days of 80% salary allowance, it will not be underestimated.

Application notice period (graded according to duration)

Number of days to apply Number of days to notify the employer in advance
30+ days 10 days ago
Less than 30 days 5 days ago
Emergencies (child is sick, nanny asks for leave, school is suspended) 1 day ago

Who can apply?

All workers with children under 3 years old are eligible. There are no restrictions on full-time workers, contract workers, or part-time workers. The employer may not refuse (Article 21 Gender Equality at Work Act).

4. The total maternity subsidy is 100,000 yuan per child (new system in 2026)

Subsidy structure: original benefit + government to make up the difference

The "Expanded Maternity Subsidy Program" will be implemented from 2026-01-01, adopting a dual-track approach of "original insurance benefits + government to make up the difference":

Social insurance maternity benefit + government top-up subsidy = NT$100,000 total per birth

For example, if the original labor insurance maternity benefit is NT$66,000, the government makes up the NT$34,000 difference, bringing the total to NT$100,000.

Covered groups (not limited to labor insurance)

Status Original insurance benefit Total after top-up
Labor insurance insured person About NT$66,000, depending on insured salary NT$100,000
National Pension, including homemakers and freelancers About NT$37,000 NT$100,000
Farmer insurance About NT$45,000 NT$100,000
Civil servant/public employee insurance Based on applicable rules NT$100,000
Women with no social insurance coverage 0 NT$100,000

Extra support for twins and higher-order multiples

The amount increases by the number of babies:

  • Twins: NT$200,000 total
  • Triplets: NT$300,000 total
  • Quadruplets: NT$400,000 total, and so on

Application process: automatically combined, no separate form required

People do not need to submit a separate top-up subsidy form. The Bureau of Labor Insurance and other social insurance agencies will automatically combine the calculation and pay it in one lump sum.

Payment timing

  • National Pension / women without insurance coverage: paid on 2026-05-07
  • Labor insurance / farmer insurance: paid on 2026-05-08

Can be combined with local government birth allowances

The central government's NT$100,000 subsidy is independent from city and county birth allowances. If you meet the local household registration requirements, you can receive both. For example, Taipei City adds NT$40,000 per birth and Hsinchu City adds NT$15,000. With local top-ups, some families may receive more than NT$150,000 in total.

5. Family care leave can now be taken by the hour (Gender Equality in Employment Act, Article 20 amendment)

Flexibility from days to hours

  • Old system: family care leave was taken by the day, up to 7 days per year
  • New system, from 2026-01-01: it is still 7 days per year, but can be split into 56 hours (7 x 8 = 56), and employers may not refuse it

Example: if you take a child to the doctor from 9 a.m. to noon, you can request 3 hours of family care leave. Under the old system, you might have needed to take half a day or a full day, using more leave than necessary.

It is unpaid leave, but employers may not deduct attendance bonuses

Family care leave is unpaid leave, so employers are not required to pay wages for those hours. However, under Article 21 of the Gender Equality in Employment Act:

  • It may not be treated as absence
  • It may not affect attendance bonuses, performance reviews, or other benefits
  • Violations may result in fines from NT$20,000 to NT$300,000

Applicable situations: sudden family care needs

  • A family member needs medical care or hospitalization
  • A young child needs vaccination
  • A school closure creates temporary care needs
  • Emergency room visits or accompanying a family member for an examination
  • Covered family members include parents, spouse, children, grandchildren, siblings, and spouse's parents

6. FAQ

Q1: What if my company has not updated its minimum wage, daily parental leave, or hourly family care leave policies? The company is legally required to update its HR policies. You can first remind HR and show the Ministry of Labor announcement. If nothing changes within one month, contact the 1955 labor hotline or your local labor affairs bureau. Workers do not carry the burden of proving every violation; the labor bureau can initiate an inspection.

Q2: Can daily parental leave be taken one day at a time? Yes. For example, a mother can take 5 days starting on May 1, return to work for a week, and then take another 3 days. This is legal. Employers may coordinate staffing within a reasonable scope, but they may not reject the request outright.

Q3: Can I receive the NT$100,000 maternity subsidy if I do not have labor insurance? Yes. The new system covers women without any social insurance coverage, with the government making up the full NT$100,000. Homemakers, students, and freelancers who give birth or deliver prematurely on or after 2026-01-01 are included.

Q4: Are the NT$200,000 for twins or NT$300,000 for triplets paid in installments? No. The payment is made in one lump sum to the designated account, calculated by the number of babies. A family with triplets receives NT$300,000 at once.

Q5: What is the difference between family care leave and personal leave? Family care leave is unpaid but cannot be used to deduct attendance bonuses. Personal leave is also unpaid and may affect attendance or performance reviews. Family care leave is limited to sudden family care needs, while personal leave has no specific reason requirement. Use family care leave first, then personal leave if you exceed 7 days or 56 hours.

Conclusion

Taiwan's 2026 labor reforms combine responses to low birth rates, worker rights, and family-friendly employment. The minimum wage of NT$29,500 per month and NT$196 per hour protects baseline income. Daily parental leave plus the 80% wage subsidy prevents parents from being forced to take a full month off for a short care need. The NT$100,000 maternity subsidy, combined with local government allowances, reduces the early financial pressure of childbirth. Hourly family care leave prevents workers from losing half a day or a full day of attendance for a short family care need.

One practical step to take today: open your company's HR system or ask HR whether the leave rules have been updated for the 2026 system. If they have not, the employer is legally required to adjust them. Rights are not something to wait for passively; they need to be checked and claimed.

Further reading: 2026 Annual Leave Guide, How to Calculate Labor Day Overtime Pay, and Parental Leave Day Calculator.

item.title: Save Money on a NT$35K Salary: 2026 Practical Guide for Young Workers in Taiwan
item.description: Rising prices, stagnant salary — can you still save on a NT$35K monthly income? This 2026 practical guide breaks down rent, food, transit (TPASS pass), and high-yield digital accounts (Richart 3.5%, NEXT Bank 2%) so you can save NT$8,000–12,000 monthly.
item.content:encoded:
Prices are rising and wages haven’t changed much. Can you still save money with a monthly salary of 35,000? Many people think it is “impossible”, but many young colleagues around me are using a few simple strategies to steadily save NT$8,000–12,000 per month in 2026. This article breaks down the four major expenditures of rent, meals, transportation, and savings, and gives you the latest median rent in 2026, TPASS 1,200 monthly pass, and Richart’s 3.5% high interest rate living and other practical figures.

1. It doesn’t matter if the salary is not much, the key is to spend it wisely

The annual CPI growth rate in Taiwan in 2026 is about 1.6%, and the price increase is moderate compared to the previous two years. However, office workers with a monthly salary of 30,000 to 40,000 yuan still need to be careful about every dollar they spend. Let me break down the monthly salary of 35,000 for you:

Expenditure items General scope Money-saving version Monthly savings amount
Rent (double north independent suite) 15,000-20,000 6,000-10,000 (shared apartment) 5,000-10,000
Meal expenses 8,000-10,000 4,000-6,000 (self-cooked for 3-4 days) 3,000-5,000
Transportation 2,500-4,000 (gas + parking) 1,200 (TPASS monthly pass) 1,500-2,500
Newsletter + Subscription 1,500-2,500 800-1,200 500-1,000
Miscellaneous + Entertainment 4,000-6,000 2,500-3,500 1,500-2,500
Monthly savings 0-2,000 8,000-12,000 —

The key is that the "saving money version" is not about asceticism - it is about choosing the right plan for each expenditure, and then automatically transferring the money saved, so that you can spend the remaining money however you like without overspending. Let me break it down for you item by item below.

Real case: Miss A’s monthly salary NT$35,000 expense list

Miss A, 27 years old, shares a 3-bedroom apartment in Zhonghe, New Taipei (NT$8,000, including management fees, water and electricity), self-catering for 3 days + eating out for 4 days (meals NT$5,500), TPASS NT$1,200 monthly pass (NT$1,200), mobile phone + two subscriptions (NT$1,000), miscellaneous entertainment approx. NT$3,000, actual monthly savings: 35,000 − 8,000 − 5,500 − 1,200 − 1,000 − 3,000 = NT$16,300. Among them, NT$10,000 is automatically transferred to Richart to get 3.5%, NT$5,000 is fixed at 0050, and the remaining NT$1,300 is reserved for flexibility. The accumulated principal and interest of deposits in one year is about NT$130,000-140,000. After 5 years, with the compound interest of ETF, the assets can be accumulated to nearly NT$800,000.

2. Rent: 2026 Shared apartment vs. living in a home

Rent is the largest expense, and a little savings will be worth the savings on other items. The latest market trends in 2026:

  • Shared apartment in Shuangbei: 6,000–10,000 yuan (the last MRT sections such as West District, Xinzhuang, Shulin, and Yonghe are cheaper, while those in East District, Xinyi, and Banqiao business districts are on the higher side)
  • Independent Suite: 15,000–25,000 yuan (the elevator building includes management fees, and the rent per square meter in the essence of New Taipei District will exceed 1,000 yuan starting from 2025)
  • Monthly allowance for living at home: 3,000–5,000 yuan (the most economical, but it depends on the family situation)

Save money by renting a shared apartment, but you should pay attention to 3 things

  1. Second Landlord Risk: Confirm the identity of the landlord before signing the contract and ask to see the property tax bill or proof of property ownership.
  2. Lease Contract Legality: Only when it is legally registered as "residential use" can you claim the rent deduction
  3. The deposit must not exceed 2 months: According to the "Regulations on the Development and Management of the Rental Housing Market", it is illegal to overcharge

Don’t forget to claim your rent deduction

Starting from 2026, the rent deduction amount will be increased to Special deduction amount of 180,000 yuan/year (effective retroactively from 2014). The monthly rent is NT$8,000 × 12 = 96,000, and the 5% tax rate applies to annual income below NT$500,000, which can save about NT$4,800 in tax refund. For details, see Complete Guide to 2026 Tax Filing.

3. Meal expenses: The real difference between self-cooking and eating out

Eating out for lunch + dinner every day costs NT$300, which is just over NT$9,000 a month. If you cook 3-4 days a week, buying food and gas costs about NT$3,000-4,000 a month, and you can save NT$4,000-5,000 by this alone**.

Actual measurement of self-cooking cost in 2026 (one month)

  • Vegetables (bought at traditional markets): 800–1,200 yuan (20% to 30% cheaper than supermarkets)
  • Meat/eggs (2kg chicken breast + 30 eggs per week): NT$1,200–1,500
  • Seasonings/Rice and noodles: 500–700 yuan
  • Water, electricity and gas bonus (multi-purpose for self-cooking): 300–500 yuan
  • Total: 2,800–3,900 yuan/month (26-30 meals in total for lunch and dinner)

How to save money on eating out

For those who cannot cook every day, you can use the "lunch box strategy": choose a buffet for 90-110 yuan for lunch, and simply cook dinner at home, which costs about 200 yuan a day on average and 6,000 yuan a month.

Beverage fees are often underestimated

A cup of hand shake costs 50-70 yuan, and drinking 3 cups a week is 800-900 yuan a month. Switch to bringing your own coffee or tea bags and save more than 10,000 yuan a year.

4. Transportation: TPASS 1,200 monthly pass vs motorcycle

Many people think that "TPASS is only 1,200, is there any trap?" - No, this is a policy of central + local subsidies in 2023, stable operation from 2024, and TPASS 2.0 frequent guest discount will be launched on 2026-01-14.

Monthly ticket prices in each district

  • Beibei Jitao: 1,200 yuan (MRT + bus + Taiwan Railway section + some passenger transportation + YouBike free for the first 30 minutes)
  • Central (Zhongzhang Tou Miao): 699 or 999 yuan
  • South (Nangaoping): 999 yuan
  • Single County and City Plan: NT$399 in Tainan/Kaohsiung/Pingtung and other cities

TPASS 2.0 Frequent Customer Feedback (2026 onwards)

After registering the e-ticket to the Frequent Frequent Customer Discount Reward Area of the Highway Bureau, you can enjoy rewards for riding ≥ 11 times per month, and the reward ratio is graded according to the number of times. It's like the ticket price has dropped again.

Locomotive vs monthly ticket calculation

Project Locomotive TPASS monthly pass
Gas money 1,200-1,800 0
Parking fee 600-1,500 0
Insurance / License Tax / Maintenance Amortization 500-800 0
Monthly Pass 0 1,200
Total 2,300-4,100 1,200

As long as the daily commuting distance is less than 20 kilometers and within a metropolitan area, TPASS beats motorcycles. The remaining distance/occasionally going out of town can be connected by YouBike + passenger transportation.

5. Savings and investment: high-interest deposits + ETF regular quota

The money saved is dealt with in two parts: Establish an emergency reserve first → then make regular fixed investment.

Emergency reserve fund: 3-6 months of living expenses, save at high interest rates

Digital Account High Interest Savings Interest Rate in 2026 (Q2 Announcement):

Bank New Account Interest Rate Limit Old Account / Notes
Taishin Richart 3.5% Within 300,000 (2026/03/02-07/01) Old household within 300,000 1.8%
Future Bank (NEXT) 2% Within 200,000 + 1.5% for excess over 50,000 Regardless of new or old accounts
Yongfeng DAWHO 1.5% Within 300,000 To 2026/06/30
Federal New New Bank Up to 15% Lower limit limit New account limit

Strategy: First save 3 months of living expenses (approximately NT$100,000-150,000) and put it in Richart or NEXT Bank to earn interest, and then consider other uses if there is more.

Regular Fixed Amount ETFs: The Long-Term Power of Compound Interest

Buy 0050 (Yanta Taiwan 50) or high dividend ETF (0056/00919) for a fixed monthly amount of NT$3,000–5,000. 0050’s annual interest-bearing return in the past five years is approximately 10.88%, which is far better than survival. 5,000 per month for 10 years (estimated at 8% compound interest) can accumulate to NT$920,000.

Autopay: The iron rule of saving first and spending later

Open the bank app, set up Salary Account → Savings Account for automatic transfer, and transfer NT$8,000–10,000 directly to Richart or NEXT the next day after payday. If you don't see the money, you won't spend it. This is more than 3 times more successful than "saving according to how much is left" at the end of the month.

6. FAQ

**Q1: ​​I am 30 years old and still earning a monthly salary of 35,000. Should I change my job? ** Saving money and changing jobs go hand in hand, not choosing one over the other. A monthly salary of 35,000 means that the market can still grow. You can also: ① Use the strategies in this article to save 10,000 per month to build a financial buffer. ② Learn new skills or take certifications to gradually increase your salary. The more buffer you have, the more likely you are to challenge for a higher-paying position when changing jobs.

**Q2: Can you really save so much by sharing a house? Will roommates be troublesome? ** You can save 5,000–10,000 by sharing a flat, but the running-in costs need to be taken into consideration. It is recommended to look for 2-3 room types, where tenants can work/rest independently (to prevent roommates from being unemployed at home), share utility bills/consumption of public supplies in writing, and make a clear agreement before moving in.

**Q3: Will the high interest rate remain so high? ** Won't. Richart 3.5% is a limited-time project from 2026-03-02 to 2026-07-01; most banks' high-interest deposits are "short-term projects" and may drop to 1.5-2% later. You need to monitor bank announcements regularly, or simply evaluate your account every 6 months.

**Q4: 0050 has risen a lot, is it too late to enter the market now? ** The core of regular quotas is to spread time risks. "Highest point vs. lowest point" has limited impact on long-term investors. The constituent stocks of 0050 are among the top 50 in Taiwan stock market in terms of market capitalization. They are growing in tandem with Taiwan's economy and will not lose out to the market in a 5-10 year cycle. The key is not "when to enter the market" but "continue to enter the market".

**Q5: 0050 vs 0056 vs 00919, which one should I choose? ** 0050 is a "market capitalization" type that pursues capital gains, with an annual interest rate of about 10.88% in the past five years and a yield rate of 1.39-2%; 0056 and 00919 are "high dividend" dividend distribution strategies, with a yield rate of 5-7% but weak capital gains. At the stage of accumulating principal for young people, it is recommended to mainly use 0050, with 1-2% of 0056/00919 to support life. Gradually switch to higher dividends as you approach retirement.

**Q6: Can credit cards be used? Will it be maxed out accidentally? ** The credit card itself is not guilty. The problem lies in "swiping without reconciliation." Suggestions: ① Only apply for 1-2 cards with practical rewards (life bill card + overseas card) ② Reconcile the bill when it comes, and add reasons for all unexpected expenses ③ Set automatic full payment to avoid recurring interest (annual interest rate 7-15%) ④ Dynamically track the proportion of monthly credit card expenditures in salary, and be alert if it exceeds 30%.

7. 2026 Budget Review in an Inflationary Environment

In the past few years, you have been able to slowly save money by saving money and not investing, but the environment you will face in 2026 is different - you must actively reallocate your budget in line with inflation figures.

2026 Inflation Numbers: Mild But Sustained

Data from the General Accounting Office: Inflation rate was 1.75% in February 2026 and slowed to 1.2% in March. Although it is not like the peak of breaking 3% in 2022-2023, it still continues to eat up purchasing power. For an office worker with a monthly salary of 35,000, inflation alone will reduce your real purchasing power by about NT$5,000-8,000 per year, so "flat = regression".

The relative position of minimum salary vs monthly salary of 35K in 2026

Starting from January 2026, the minimum salary will be adjusted to monthly salary NT$29,500 / hourly wage NT$196. A monthly salary of 35,000 is about 18% higher than the minimum wage and falls into the "slightly higher than the bottom" range. If your salary has not increased in 5 years, the real purchasing power will actually be lower than the 35K in 2020. This is not alarmist, it is purely numerical fact.

Comparison of three major budget allocation rules (actual calculation for monthly salary 35K)

Rules Savings Life Others Applicable objects
333 Principle NT$11,667 NT$11,667 (living) NT$11,667 (emergency fund) Newbie who just started to learn to save money
631 Principle NT$10,500 NT$21,000 (living) NT$3,500 (insurance) Shuangbei ethnic group with high rent/commute burden
4321 Principle NT$7,000 NT$10,500 (living) NT$14,000 (investment) + NT$3,500 (insurance) Advanced financial managers who already have emergency funds

Charlie recommends the version with a monthly salary of 35K:

  • Savings + Investments: NT$10,000-12,000 (high interest deposits + ETF regular quota)
  • Living necessities (rent/meals/transportation): NT$18,000-20,000
  • Personal enjoyment + learning: NT$3,000-5,000
  • Insurance + Emergency Preparedness: NT$2,000-3,000

The key is "Automatic transfer and diversion" - let the system transfer the savings part first on the payday, and the rest is for living expenses. Save first and then spend is the thinking of the rich. Spending first and then saving only leaves you with debt.

"Minimum Implementation List" to Fight Inflation: Prioritize these 3 things

  1. Open source NT$1,000-3,000 per month: Take on 1-2 light side jobs (design, copywriting, administrative helper), the increase is much greater than the inflation of 1-2% (extended reading: [Side Job Recommendation Tools and Tax Guide] (/blog/en/freelance-side-hustle-tools/))
  2. Change to buy interest-bearing ETF: 0050 annualized interest rate 10.88% > inflation 1.2%, let the assets outperform prices on their own
  3. Avoid "fake discounts": The "promotional prices" of mass merchandisers/online shopping often have built-in price increases. The actual unit price can only be seen by comparing the historical ratio.

Inflation is not the end of the world, but leaving it alone will slowly erode your efforts today. Take 5 minutes tonight to make a list of your subscriptions and evaluate whether you can cut off one or two — This is the fastest concrete action to show "I have combated inflation."

in conclusion

If you want to save money with a monthly salary of 35,000, it’s not about doing hard work, it’s about choosing the right plan + automation**. You can save 5,000-10,000 by renting in a shared house or living at home, you can save 2,000-3,000 by using TPASS instead of motorcycle, you can save 4,000-5,000 by cooking for 3-4 days, and you can automatically transfer your salary to Richart and get 3.5% - the difference is NT$8,000-12,000 per month.

The money saved is processed with 3-6 months emergency reserve (high-interest living savings) + monthly fixed quota of 3,000-5,000 ETFs. After 10 years, the compound interest alone will accumulate to nearly one million. Money will not grow on its own, but it will earn interest on its own. First thing to do today: open your bank app and set up automatic transfers, things will be different starting next month. With 5 minutes of decision-making cost per month, options open up for the next ten years.
