The overall winning rate for any prize is about 10.5%, which is slightly higher than Lotto.

Lottery drawing time

Monday to Saturday in the evening 20:30 (Note: There is no lottery draw on Sundays, originally many people mistakenly thought that it was held every day).

Matching and receiving prizes: Determination process of amount levels

The process of claiming the prize after winning varies depending on the single bet amount and the total amount of the entire lottery ticket. The following table summarizes the latest regulations for 2026:

Single bet amount Total amount of the entire lottery ticket Prize collection channels Taxation
5,000 yuan (inclusive) and below 200,000 yuan (inclusive) and below Any lottery shop and lottery betting station No income tax withheld
Above 5,001 yuan Below 200,000 yuan (inclusive) All business units of China Trust, lottery betting stations Full deduction of 20% income tax + 4/1000 stamp duty
Any amount 200,001 to 5 million yuan China Trust’s designated business unit Same as above
Any amount Above 5 million yuan Telephone appointment required China Trust Customer Service Same as above

⚠️ IMPORTANT UPDATE:

  • In the past, online articles often wrote "2,000 yuan threshold", this is the old system. The current regulation in 2026 is that the withholding limit is RMB 5,000 for a single payment**.
  • The period for claiming the prize is 3 months from the draw date (the earlier article wrote "60 days" incorrectly).
  • The prize redemption institution is not the Bank of Taiwan, but China Trust and Commercial Bank. It can also be redeemed at Penghu First Credit Union and Kinmen Credit Union, making it convenient for people on outlying islands.

Prize matching method

There are three fastest ways:

  1. Taiwan Lottery Official App Scan the lottery barcode and automatically match the prizes
  2. This website Taiwan lottery lottery query tool, check the latest lottery numbers of all lottery types on one page
  3. Go to any lottery store and ask the store machine to scan

When matching the prize, please make sure that the lottery ticket is intact and has not been torn or altered, otherwise it may affect the redemption of the prize.

A complete comparison of the winning probabilities of the three major lottery tickets + the psychology of gambler’s fallacy

Before buying lottery tickets, understanding the winning chances and bonus structures of the three major lottery types can help you choose the right gameplay that suits you. The following is a comparison of three mainstream lotteries in 2026:

Lottery type Chance of winning the jackpot Jackpot amount Overall winning rate Frequency of draws
Power Color About 1/22.09 million Cumulative system (history highest about 3.2 billion) About 11.78% Monday, Thursday
Grand Lotto Approximately 1/13.98 million (0.0000072%) Accumulation system (history high 937 million, 2009) Approximately 6.68% Tuesday, Friday
Jincai 539 About 1/8.01 million Fixed 8 million About 11.10% Every day

Although Powerball has the lowest chance of winning the jackpot (one in 22.09 million), it has the highest "overall winning rate" (approximately 11.78%, with an average of 1 winning bet for every 8.5 bets), so the expected value of small prizes is the best. Jincai 539 has no accumulation mechanism - even if you win continuously, the jackpot is still 8 million, which is suitable for players who "want to have something to look forward to every day".

Three common lottery psychology traps:

  1. Gambler's Fallacy: It is wrong to believe that "if 7 has not been opened recently, it will definitely be opened next period". Each lottery drawing is an independent event, and the results of previous periods will not affect the odds of this period.
  2. Sunk Cost: "I have bought 100 issues without winning, and I should win if I buy 10 more." This idea will make you lose more and more. The more you invest ≠ the closer you are to winning.
  3. Availability Heuristic: The media only reports on the "Lottery Lottery Shop" + the grand prize winner, making people overestimate the probability of winning. The odds of a jackpot of 1/22.09 million are 22 times lower than the odds of being struck by lightning (1/1 million), but you won’t see the “22.08 million people who didn’t win” in the news.

Rational advice: Treat lottery tickets as entertainment expenses, not as investments. Set a lottery budget every month (it is recommended that it does not exceed 10% of entertainment expenses). If you win, you will be happy and if you don’t win, you will donate it to charity (about 28% of the government surplus goes back to the social welfare fund).

Why do lottery ticket sales increase during inflation?

Observing that during the inflation period from 2022 to 2024, Taiwan Lottery sales** will increase by 8-15% annually** - this is related to the behavioral economics phenomenon of "declining relative purchasing power → psychologically more willing to gamble on a turnaround opportunity". Taiwan Lottery’s sales exceeding NT$150 billion in 2024, a record high, is concrete evidence of this trend. But lotteries are not an anti-inflation tool and the long-term expected value is still negative. To truly combat inflation, it is more practical to return to asset allocation (ETF regular quota/high-interest living savings).

FAQ: Lottery Frequently Asked Questions

Q1: Does the lottery shop really "give out big prizes"? Which one is easier to win?

Winning the lottery is a purely random event and has no causal relationship with the location of the lottery ticket bank or the past record of winning big prizes. The media often reports that a certain lottery shop offers "new jackpots" simply because the store has a large sales volume and naturally has a higher chance of winning the jackpot. Don’t go long distances to a lottery shop just to “get the big prize”, as this will only increase your time cost.

Q2: Which one is more cost-effective among Weilicai, Big Lotto and Jincai 539?

Purely from the expected value point of view, the long-term return rate of each bet of 50 yuan for each of the three is less than 50 yuan (the difference is the government’s public welfare surplus distribution). But if we consider "entertainment vs. possibility of winning":

  • If you want to chase the big prize and accept the extremely low probability: choose Power Color
  • If you want to have a medium chance and guarantee a bonus of more than one million: choose Big Lotto
  • If you want to have something to look forward to every day and enjoy small amounts of entertainment: choose Jincai 539

Q3: Do I have to claim it in person after winning? Can I ask a family member to pick it up on my behalf?

Single bets of less than 5,000 yuan can be collected by others with lottery tickets, no identity verification is required. Single bet exceeds 5,000 yuan Since it involves withholding income tax, the winner needs to handle it in person with his or her ID card; if entrusting someone else, the ID cards and power of attorney of both parties are required. **Major awards (above one million) are strongly recommended to be handled in person to avoid entrustment disputes.

Q4: Do I need to declare income tax again after withholding 20%?

Charitable lottery winnings are subject to separate taxation and do not need to be incorporated into the comprehensive income tax return after 20% withholding. In other words, tax is paid once it is withheld. However, it is recommended to keep the withholding voucher for inspection.

Q5: Can lottery tickets be reissued if they are lost or damaged?

Cannot be reissued. Lottery tickets are bearer securities, and losing them is equivalent to giving up the right to win. It is recommended to sign the back of the lottery ticket immediately after winning the prize and keep it in a safe place.

Conclusion: rational consumption, healthy entertainment

Before buying a lottery ticket, please remember three things:

  1. Act within your ability: Set a monthly lottery budget limit that does not exceed the proportion of entertainment expenses
  2. Understand the odds: The Powerball jackpot is 1/22.09 million, which is 22 times lower than the chance of being struck by lightning (about 1/1 million)
  3. Surplus for charity: Even if you don’t win, part of the amount will go back to social welfare and be regarded as a small amount to participate in charity.

item.title: Typhoon Days Off in Taiwan: 2026 Updated Suspension Standards & Worker Rights
item.description: When a typhoon hits Taiwan, everyone wants to know "Will work and school be cancelled tomorrow?" This guide covers the legal basis, wind and rainfall standards, decision timing per municipality, and practical implications for wages, makeup classes, and service industry workers, including 2026 updates to Keelung standards.
item.content:encoded:
Whenever a typhoon strikes, the question most people ask is "Will classes be suspended tomorrow?" Taiwan will encounter more than one class suspension almost every year during the typhoon season. However, from decision-making timing, wind and rain compliance standards to salary processing, many details are actually unclear to most people. This article starts from the source of the law and clarifies all the practical rights and interests you need to know at once.

Picture: The city scene when a typhoon hits (picture placeholder, to be added)

Legal basis: "Measures for suspending work and class work due to natural disasters"

Taiwan's typhoon holiday is not something that can be issued with just one sentence of administrative order, but has a clear legal source. The core basis is the "Regulations on Suspension of Work and Class Work in Natural Disasters" formulated by the Office of Personnel and Administration of the Executive Yuan in 1996 and subsequently revised many times. This method standardizes:

  • Which natural disasters will trigger the suspension of classes (typhoons, heavy rains, earthquakes, floods, etc.)
  • The authority and responsibility for the suspension of classes (central vs. local)
  • Objective standards for wind and rain compliance
  • Announcement timing and media communication method
  • Labor attendance and payroll processing principles

In other words, when you see county and city governments announcing the suspension of classes, there is a whole set of regulations and processes in operation, not the personal preference of the chief executive. Only by understanding this mechanism can you control your rights and interests during typhoons.

Who decides? Decision-making rights and responsibilities are clarified at once

Many people think that the suspension of classes is a unified announcement from the central government, but it is not. Decision-making power lies in the hands of local chiefs:

  • Agencies and schools within municipal districts: shall be announced by the mayor
  • Institutions and schools within the jurisdiction of **county (city): decided by the county (city) mayor
  • Governments at all levels can also authorize decisions to lower-level heads based on topography, landforms, and historical experience in disaster prevention (for example, mountainous towns and villages can make independent announcements)

This is why there is a phenomenon of "neighboring counties and cities let one side go and the other side not" - because the decision-making power is decentralized, and each county and city government makes independent judgments by referring to the meteorological data, geographical characteristics, and past disasters in its own jurisdiction. It rains equally in Taipei City and New Taipei City, but different decisions may be made due to different mountain areas, topography, and watersheds.

Objective standards for achieving wind and rain standards

Although the final decision rests with the director, the "Operation Measures" stipulates objective weather conditions standards as a basis for judgment:

Wind power standard

According to the typhoon warning forecast of the Central Meteorological Administration, areas where the typhoon wind radius may pass through within 4 hours, the forecast is:

  • Average winds reaching level 7 or above (more than 50.4 kilometers per hour), or
  • Gusts can reach level 10 or above (above 89.4 kilometers per hour)

If any of the conditions is met, suspension of classes and classes can be considered.

Rainfall standard

For a heavy rain scenario, when the cumulative rainfall forecast for the next 24 hours reaches the following thresholds and has caused a disaster or is at risk of causing a disaster:

  • Flat ground: 350 mm
  • Mountain areas: 200 mm

⚠️ New system in 2026: Keelung City announced that starting from 2026, it will be adjusted to 200 mm regardless of mountainous areas and flat land. The reason is that the terrain of Keelung is mainly hilly, and the original standard of 350 mm for flat land no longer meets actual disaster prevention needs. It has not yet been announced whether other counties and cities will follow suit.

Wind strength comparison (Beaufort wind scale)

Wind level Wind speed range (km/h) Description Standard effect
Level 7 50.4–61.5 Strong winds make it impossible The average wind reaches the lower limit
Level 8 61.6–74.1 Strong wind breaks branches —
Level 9 74.2–88.5 Strong wind damages light house —
Level 10 88.6–103.8 Strong wind uproots trees Gust reaches the lower limit
Level 11 103.9–120.0 Storm brings heavy damage —
Level 12 120.1+ Hurricane is extremely destructive —

When you hear the weather anchor say "gusts above level 10," it means that the weather conditions are close to the threshold for suspending work and classes.

Timing of decision: When will it be announced?

County and city governments usually announce decisions at the following timings based on typhoon trends:

  • The afternoon to evening of the previous day (17:00–22:00): Most counties and cities will announce the typhoon that is determined to be affected the next day during this time. This is the prime time period that office workers are most concerned about
  • Early morning (05:00–06:00): If the typhoon track changes rapidly or the wind and rain suddenly intensify at night, an emergency announcement may be made before going out
  • Morning of the day (before 10:00): For typhoons that are progressive or will arrive in the afternoon, classes and classes may be suspended starting from afternoon after work or class.

The most reliable way to inquire is to directly check the official page of the "Natural Disaster Suspension of Work and Class Situation Inquiry" of the General Office of Personnel and Administration, or use this site's "Typhoon Suspension of Work and Class Inquiry Tool" to integrate the real-time status of 22 counties and cities, saving you the trouble of searching for announcements from each county and city government one by one.

Picture: TWTools typhoon class suspension query tool (actual screenshots to be added)

Legal significance: Is the typhoon fake a "fake"? How is the salary calculated?

The answer to this question will surprise many people: Typhoon leave is not "fake" legally. Its official name is "Public Institutions Suspension of Office or Work Due to Natural Disasters". According to the "Key Points of Labor Attendance Management and Wage Payment in Institutions Affected by Natural Disasters" (issued by the Ministry of Labor):

Workers’ absence from work → Not counted as absenteeism or personal leave

If work is suspended during a typhoon, employers shall not treat workers' absence as absenteeism, nor may they force workers to use personal leave, sick leave, or special leave as deductions. However, the following rules govern whether wages are paid:

Situation Labor Rights Employer Obligations
The government announced that work is suspended and workers fail to show up It does not count as absenteeism Wages must not be paid to** (it is "not attributable to both parties"), but they are encouraged to be paid
The government announced that work is suspended and workers voluntarily attend work Work is paid Wages should be increased (not less than 1 times the original salary), commonly known as "double pay"
The government has not announced a work suspension, and workers are unable to attend work due to wind and rain They must ask for leave in advance Employers may deduct wages based on personal leave/special leave
Injury or financial loss during work The case will be deemed as an occupational accident The employer shall be liable for occupational accident compensation

⚠️ The key point is "Whether wages must be paid" does not mean "must not be paid" - Many people mistakenly believe that no wages will be paid during typhoon leave. In fact, most companies will choose to pay wages to maintain employee relations. This is the "flexibility" provided by the law to employers rather than mandatory wage deduction regulations. If your company does not pay you, you can negotiate; if you are on duty, be sure to confirm whether your salary has been doubled.

Practical rights during typhoon holiday

The way different identities are handled on the day of typhoon holiday varies greatly. The following table summarizes common scenarios:

Identity Status on the day of typhoon holiday Precautions
Office workers (laborers) Failure to show up is not considered absenteeism; voluntary attendance is double pay Confirm the employer's salary policy; keep attendance records
Students If there are no classes on the day of suspension, the school usually arranges make-up classes** Make-up classes may be held on Saturdays or during winter and summer vacations
Civil Servants It is regarded as a day off during working days and the salary will be paid —
Service industry (such as convenience stores, restaurants) A high proportion of people who still need to be present due to the nature of the business Employers should increase wages; if there is no increase, you can appeal to the Labor Bureau
Dispatch workers The Labor Standards Act applies to the same as regular workers Dispatch companies are not allowed to unilaterally deduct wages
Timekeepers Same as workers, failure to attend the original scheduled shift will not be counted as absenteeism Wages are calculated based on the original scheduled shift
Self-employed workers (delivery, SOHO) No employer relationship, no double salary applicable Make your own judgment on whether to attend work; Typhoon insurance recommends renewal

FAQ: Frequently Asked Questions about Typhoon Holidays

Q1: When will the government announce the suspension of classes and classes? Which one is right, TV ticker or official website?

Please refer to the official inquiry page of the Personnel and Administration Office. Information from TV stations or news websites is sometimes delayed or mistakenly posted, and when it comes to disputes, announcements on the official website are the main ones.

Q2: What should I do if I go to work on the day of the typhoon holiday and my boss says "no subsidy was announced"?

According to the "Key Points on Wage Payment", those who voluntarily work during the typhoon holiday must receive an additional salary (at least 1 time). If the employer fails to pay, the employer can appeal to the local labor bureau/labour bureau. It is recommended to keep attendance records, time clock information, and conversation records with supervisors as evidence.

Q3: How will the school make up for the typhoon holiday?

The policies of each school are different. Most elementary schools to high schools will arrange make-up classes on all day classes on Saturdays or compressed winter and summer vacations. Colleges and universities mostly handle the situation in a flexible manner, leaving it to each department to decide whether to make up classes.

Q4: What does it mean when you see "Stop going to work, stop attending classes" on the query page of the General Office of Personnel and Administration?

"Stop going to work" is targeted at workplaces of government agencies and companies; "Stop going to school" is targeted at schools at all levels. Usually syncs, but there are occasional exceptions. For example, under certain circumstances, it may be announced that "schools will be stopped but work will not be stopped." This is often the case when there is wind and rain in the afternoon. The purpose is to allow parents time to pick up their children early.

Q5: Are injuries caused in car accidents due to collapsed road trees and flooding caused by typhoons considered occupational disasters?

If a worker is assigned by the employer to go out for work or for company business needs (such as delivery, field work), and an accident occurs on the way, he or she may claim that it is a commuting accident or an occupational accident, and the employer shall bear the liability for occupational accident compensation. It is recommended to keep the report record and medical receipts after the accident, and notify the company's occupational accident handling window.

Conclusion: Standard actions during typhoon days

Before a typhoon approaches, it is recommended to prepare in the following order:

  1. Track the weather: Pay attention to the path forecast of the Central Meteorological Administration 2-3 days before the typhoon makes landfall.
  2. Whether the service is expected to be suspended: Determine the probability of wind and rain reaching the standard based on the passing time of the storm radius
  3. Announcement period monitoring: After 17:00 in the evening of the previous day, intensively check the page of the General Administration of Personnel or the tools of this website
  4. Confirm employer policy: whether there will be additional wages for voluntary attendance and how to deal with inability to attend work
  5. Reserve time: Make the decision to go out after the suspension of classes and classes for the day is announced, and reduce unnecessary outings during typhoons.

With the legal source and rights under control, Typhoon Tian no longer passively waits for news, but responds preparedly. Check the typhoon tool on this site to get the latest announcements from 22 counties and cities in Taiwan →
